papers.title: The use of cold-stored platelets to provide hemostasis in dogs with thrombocytopenia.
papers.authors: Monaco SA, Haines JM, Guess SC, Fiedler SM, Wardrop KJ
papers.abstract: Platelet transfusion can be lifesaving in dogs with severe thrombocytopenia and hemorrhage, but platelet products are limited by short shelf life and contamination risk. Cold-stored platelets (CSP) may provide a practical alternative, but in vivo hemostatic efficacy in dogs is unknown. Evaluate the clinical hemostatic efficacy and safety of CSP transfusions in thrombocytopenic dogs. Twenty-four thrombocytopenic dogs from a veterinary teaching hospital population that received CSP transfusions between March 2022 and October 2024. Retrospective cohort study. Medical records of dogs receiving platelet concentrate stored at 4 °C for up to 21 days were reviewed. Hemorrhage severity was assessed using a modified Daily Canine Bleeding Assessment Tool (DOGiBAT) score before transfusion and at 1 and 4 h post-transfusion. Primary outcomes included change in bleeding score, clinical response, transfusion reactions, and survival to discharge. Twenty-four dogs received 27 CSP transfusions. Mean pre-transfusion platelet count was 23 × 103/μL (range, 2-107 × 103/μL) and mean post-transfusion count was 28 × 103/μL (range, 2-100 × 103/μL; P = .84). Mean DOGiBAT score decreased from 3.15 ± 2.4 at baseline to 2.21 ± 2.1 at 4 (mean change, -0.94; P = .002). Clinical improvement occurred in 19 of 27 transfusions (70%). No transfusion reactions were documented. Nineteen of 24 dogs (79%) survived to discharge. Cold-stored platelets were well-tolerated and associated with decreased bleeding severity in thrombocytopenic dogs, supporting CSP as a practical platelet transfusion option for clinical hemostatic support.

papers.title: Case series: Superficial lipomatous hamartoma in dogs and cats is a previously unreported NLCS-like dermal lesion.
papers.authors: Kästner L, Marchewski J, Henrich M
papers.abstract: In humans nevus lipomatosus cutaneous superficialis (NLCS) is a rare, benign dermal hamartoma characterized by aggregates of adipose tissue within the dermis without any connection to the subcutaneous tissue. Although NLCS is a well-recognized entity, it is considered a rare lesion with limited reports in the human literature. To date, no comparable cases have been reported in dogs and cats. Over the course of one and a half years, six cases (five in dogs, one in a cat), resembling NLCS-like lesions, were examined. In this report, we compare these cases to the human condition regarding macroscopic features, histopathology, sex, and age of the affected patients. In all cases, the dermal lesions were composed of aggregates of well-differentiated adipocytes within the dermis. Given the morphological similarity to the lesion in humans, the term "nevus lipomatosus superficialis-like lesion" might be appropriate. However, given the controversial use of the term 'nevus' in veterinary medicine and a potential for confusion with pigmented lesion, we propose the term "superficial lipomatous hamartoma" for this entity.

papers.title: Case Report: Allogeneic adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells for severe chronic kidney disease in a dog.
papers.authors: Yu Y, Lv X, Zhou X, Ma Y, Li H, Wang W, Song Y
papers.abstract: This case report explored the clinical improvement and short-term tolerability of allogeneic adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (AD-MSCs) in the treatment of severe chronic kidney disease (CKD) in dogs. A 9-year-old female Pomeranian was diagnosed with chronic kidney disease (CKD) caused by acute kidney injury and, after conventional treatment failed, received intravenous infusion of AD-MSCs from healthy donor dogs. The AD-MSCs were aseptically collected, isolated, cultured, characterized, and subjected to microbiological safety testing, and were then administered intravenously at a dose of 3 × 10 6 cells/kg every 2 weeks for a total of four infusions, with dexamethasone premedication to reduce the risk of adverse reactions. Following AD-MSC administration and continued conventional care, reductions in serum creatinine and phosphorus and a downward trend in blood urea nitrogen were observed, along with improvements in body weight, body condition score, appetite, and mental status; no adverse events were observed. The results of this case suggest the feasibility and short-term tolerability of allogeneic AD-MSCs for severe CKD in dogs and provide a reference for clinical research on cell-based therapy for canine CKD.

papers.title: Case Report: Concurrent ventricular septal defect, pulmonic stenosis, and intrapulmonary arteriovenous anastomoses in a Korean raccoon dog ( Nyctereutes procyonoides koreensis ).
papers.authors: Kim S, Kim M, Han JI, Lee K, Yoon H
papers.abstract: A 3-month-old intact male Korean raccoon dog ( Nyctereutes procyonoides koreensis ) was rescued and admitted to the Jeonbuk Wildlife Rescue Center with lethargy, dehydration, and dermatologic lesions consistent with Sarcoptes scabiei infestation. Physical examination detected a grade IV/VI systolic murmur, and thoracic radiography revealed generalized cardiomegaly. Transthoracic echocardiography identified a perimembranous ventricular septal defect (VSD) with left-to-right shunting. Although no distinct structural abnormalities of the pulmonic valve were observed, increased pulmonic flow velocity (3.87 m/s), mild pulmonic regurgitation (1.68 m/s), and post-stenotic dilation of the main pulmonary artery supported a diagnosis of pulmonic stenosis (PS). Agitated saline contrast echocardiography demonstrated intrapulmonary arteriovenous anastomoses (IPAVAs), with microbubbles appearing in the left heart after the fourth cardiac cycle; this shunting decreased following oxygen supplementation. Five weeks later, thoracic radiography demonstrated a reduction in cardiac silhouette size, although cardiomegaly persisted. Echocardiography demonstrated progression of the VSD to bidirectional shunting. Systolic doming of the pulmonic valve, together with increased pulmonic flow velocity (4.39 m/s) and pulmonic regurgitation velocity (2.07 m/s), indicated worsening PS. Repeat agitated saline contrast echocardiography revealed microbubbles in the left heart within four cardiac cycles and in the abdominal aorta, indicating a right-to-left shunt component consistent with bidirectional shunting. These findings were attenuated after oxygen supplementation. The Korean raccoon dog subsequently died during anesthetic induction for further diagnostic imaging. Postmortem examination confirmed a perimembranous VSD and type A valvular PS characterized by fused commissures, with concurrent right ventricular hypertrophy, dilation, and interventricular septal thickening. To our knowledge, this case report is the first to describe the concurrence of VSD, PS, and IPAVAs in a Korean raccoon dog. It suggests that progressive PS may contribute to reversal of shunting across a VSD.

papers.title: Serological response to field rabies vaccination in owned dogs in the immune belt of Peninsular Malaysia.
papers.authors: Noorazmi MSN, Ahmad Yunus AF, Che Rose FZ, Ballakrishnan N, Mohd Ziadi MZ, Ismail MAR, Razali MA, Rajeendran A, Abd Aziz MR, Wan Omar Bakri WN, Zainun Z, Merawin LT, Mohd Saeid FH
papers.abstract: Rabies vaccination is conducted along the northern border of Peninsular Malaysia, but paired field serological data are limited. We analysed routine programme data from 154 owned dogs sampled immediately before vaccination and 30-83 days later (median, 43 days). Rabies virus-neutralising antibody levels were measured using the fluorescent antibody virus neutralisation test. Paired levels in IU/mL were compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, and benchmark proportions were compared using the exact McNemar test. The proportion with levels ≥ 0.5 IU/mL increased from 72.7% (112/154; 95% confidence interval [CI], 65.2-79.1%) to 98.1% (151/154; 95% CI, 94.4-99.3%; p < 0.001). Three dogs remained below the benchmark. Median levels increased from 1.98 IU/mL (interquartile range [IQR], 0.38-5.92) to 13.5 IU/mL (IQR, 4.5-13.5); the median paired increase was 5.45 IU/mL (bootstrap 95% CI, 3.31-7.25; p < 0.001). Levels increased in 128 dogs, were unchanged in 19 and decreased in seven. Eighty follow-up values equalled the dataset maximum of 13.5 IU/mL, suggesting possible upper-end censoring. Vaccination history identified 99 previously vaccinated dogs and seven recorded as receiving their first vaccination, limiting comparison of these groups. Nearly all dogs retained at follow-up met the serological benchmark. Convenience sampling, incomplete follow-up and uncertain measurement limits restrict inference to this cohort and preclude estimates of population immunity or clinical effectiveness.

papers.title: Attitudes and practices of veterinarians regarding feline pain management in Western vs Eastern Europe.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Bukhari SSUH, Marangoni S, Almendros A, Luna SPL, Steagall PV
papers.abstract: This study aimed to report and compare attitudes and practices of veterinarians regarding feline pain management in Eastern and Western Europe. A questionnaire was developed and divided into demographic data, drug availability/administration, and pain management practices. The questionnaire went through content and face validity and was translated into several languages. An internet-based survey was created, and responses were collected using a convenience sampling method. Data were analyzed using multiple correspondence analysis. In total, 833 participants from Europe were included. Most respondents indicated good knowledge of acute pain assessment and recognition (n = 478, 57.4%). The Feline Grimace Scale was the most commonly used instrument to assess acute pain (n = 346, 41.5%). Chronic pain scoring instruments were not used by 48.5% (n = 404) of participants. Meloxicam and robenacoxib were the most used non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for chronic pain management. Limited knowledge of pain assessment, non-use of NSAIDs in cats undergoing surgery, and postoperative use of opioids were more closely associated with Eastern than Western Europe. Reported good knowledge of pain management, pre- and intraoperative use of NSAIDs, use of pain scales and preoperative opioids, having a specialty diploma, and working in a cat-friendly practice were associated with Western Europe compared with Eastern Europe. Important regional differences were found regarding feline pain management across Europe. Continuing education, wider implementation of validated pain assessment tools, and improved access to analgesics may help reduce regional disparities and improve feline welfare.

papers.title: Feline stress through owners' eyes: comparing perceptions in veterinary clinics with and without designated cat-only areas or hours.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Baltz A
papers.abstract: ObjectivesThis study compared veterinary clinics with and without designated cat-only areas or hours across four domains: feline stress during visits, handling and restraint techniques, owner education on preventive care and common diseases, and overall client satisfaction.MethodsA cross-sectional questionnaire study was conducted across eight clinics in Greater Lisbon, Portugal (between November 2015 and January 2016). In total, 204 cat owners completed a 37-question survey evaluating clinic experience, feline stress, owner education and service quality. Respondents were divided based on whether their clinic offered feline-segregated areas or hours (n = 96) or not (n = 108). Data were analysed using χ 2 and Mann-Whitney U-tests ( P  <0.05), with effect sizes calculated via Cramér's V and rank-biserial correlation.ResultsOwners at non-segregated clinics reported greater difficulty removing cats from carriers ( P  = 0.034) and administering home medication ( P  = 0.040). Their cats were more frequently scruffed (18.4% vs 7.4%) or sedated (10.3% vs 2.5%; P  = 0.046; Cramér's V = 0.24), with the presence of other species increasing perceived stress ( P  = 0.004; r  = 0.21). Non-segregated clinic owners also received significantly less information regarding feline leukaemia virus (42.6% vs 17.7% uninformed; P  <0.001), feline immunodeficiency virus (40.7% vs 15.6%; P  <0.001), flea prevention (27.8% vs 7.3%; P  <0.001) and deworming (21.3% vs 5.2%; P  = 0.001). Satisfaction with staff and veterinarians was higher in the segregated group ( P  = 0.001 for both).Conclusions and relevanceClinics utilising designated cat-only spaces or hours demonstrated superior outcomes across all evaluated domains. These findings provide quantitative support for cat-friendly principles, suggesting that investing in species segregation, staff training and client education yields tangible improvements in animal welfare, client relationships and veterinary practice quality.

papers.title: Advances in detection canine science at Auburn University.
papers.authors: Chester E, Lazarowski L, Wang X, Bartol FF, Johnson CM

papers.title: Sugammadex at 2 mg/kg provides rapid and sustained reversal of moderate rocuronium-induced neuromuscular blockade in isoflurane-anesthetized dogs.
papers.authors: Chang RN, Wang HC, Chang CC, Chen IY
papers.abstract: To investigate the efficacy of 2 mg/kg sugammadex in reversing moderate rocuronium-induced neuromuscular blockade (NMB) in dogs, focusing on recovery time and recurarization. In this prospective, nonrandomized, unblinded experimental study, 12 healthy adult mixed-breed dogs were evaluated before elective surgery and assigned to a control group (spontaneous recovery; n = 6) or a reversal group (2 mg/kg sugammadex; n = 6). Anesthesia was induced with propofol and maintained with isoflurane without premedication. Neuromuscular function was monitored using train-of-four (TOF) acceleromyography. Moderate NMB was defined as TOF count 1 to 3, and complete NMB recovery was defined as a normalized TOF ratio (TOFR; measured TOFR/baseline TOFR) ≥ 0.9. Rocuronium (0.6 mg/kg IV) was administered, followed in the reversal group by sugammadex (2 mg/kg IV) at first-twitch (T1) reappearance. Dogs in the reversal group were monitored for 60 minutes after complete NMB recovery. Recovery time was defined as T1 reappearance to normalized TOFR ≥ 0.9; recurarization was defined as a subsequent decrease in normalized TOFR to < 0.9 after complete NMB recovery. Recovery time was significantly shorter in the reversal group (median [range], 1.3 [0.8 to 3.0] minutes) than in the control group (18.6 [12.3 to 35.5] minutes). No recurarization was observed. Sugammadex at 2 mg/kg provided rapid reversal of moderate rocuronium-induced NMB in isoflurane-anesthetized dogs. No recurarization was observed during the 60-minute monitoring period after complete NMB recovery. Sugammadex at 2 mg/kg may be considered for reversal of moderate rocuronium-induced NMB at T1 reappearance in dogs. However, objective neuromuscular monitoring remains essential to guide reversal decisions and confirm neuromuscular recovery.

papers.title: Acute postoperative hypophosphatemia is a potential sequela following hepatectomy in dogs.
papers.authors: Bryant RE, Skinner OT, Barchilon M
papers.abstract: To describe posthepatectomy hypophosphatemia in dogs and evaluate whether the extent of hepatectomy was associated with postoperative hypophosphatemia. This was a retrospective, observational study of dogs that underwent hepatectomy from January 1, 2019, through December 15, 2025, with serum phosphorus concentrations recorded preoperatively and within 72 hours postoperatively. Dogs with comorbidities or complications expected to influence serum phosphorus were excluded. Data included extent of hepatectomy (division/subdivisional) and change in serum phosphorus concentration (ΔP). Phosphorus and the proportions of dogs with recorded hypophosphatemia were compared between dogs undergoing division hepatectomy and subdivisional hepatectomy using the Mann-Whitney test and Fisher's exact test, respectively. 42 dogs were included (19 subdivisional, 23 division hepatectomy). Median ΔP was -0.8 mg/dL (range, -3.8 to 3.4). ΔP was greater in dogs with division hepatectomy (-0.9 mg/dL; range, -3.8 to 3.4) than subdivisional hepatectomy (-0.5 mg/dL; range, -1.7 to 1.2). Seven of 42 dogs (16.7%) developed postoperative hypophosphatemia at a median of 20 hours (range, 16 to 43); all dogs had undergone division hepatectomy (7 of 23 [30.4%]). Three dogs were treated with IV potassium phosphate. No dogs (0 of 19 [0%]) with subdivisional hepatectomy had recorded hypophosphatemia. Hypophosphatemia can arise in dogs after liver resection, primarily following division hepatectomy or greater. There was an overall decrease in phosphorus for both divisional and subdivisional hepatectomy groups. Routine assessment of phosphorus following hepatectomy may be considered to minimize the risk of consequential hypophosphatemia.

papers.title: Intra-articular 2.5% polyacrylamide hydrogel provides sustained clinical improvement over 1 year in canine elbow osteoarthritis.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
papers.authors: Corral JA, Levine D, Barnhard JA, Tringali AA, Green MM, Brunke MW
papers.abstract: To evaluate the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of IA 2.5% injectable polyacrylamide hydrogel (iPAAG) in dogs with elbow osteoarthritis (OA). We hypothesized that treatment would improve pain and function, with minimal adverse events. This prospective single-site clinical study enrolled client-owned dogs from October 2023 to October 2024. Dogs with elbow OA confirmed by CT received unilateral or bilateral IA injections with 1 mL of 2.5% iPAAG. Assessments were conducted on day 0 (baseline) and at 2 weeks, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, and 12 months after injection using the Canine Brief Pain Inventory (CBPI) Pain Severity Score, CBPI Pain Interference Score, modified Glasgow Composite Pain Scale, Numerical Rating Score, elbow goniometry, thoracic limb girth, and joint effusion. Complete blood count and serum biochemistry were performed at baseline and 3 months after injection. 18 dogs were treated; 16 completed the study. There were significant improvements in all measures between baseline and 3 to 12 months. The CBPI Pain Severity Score, CBPI Pain Interference Score, modified Glasgow Composite Pain Scale, Numerical Rating Score, elbow flexion, elbow extension, thoracic limb girth, and joint effusion had an overall effect size of 0.44, 0.53, 0.69, 0.63, 0.31, 0.64, 0.53, and 0.64, respectively. There were minimal, self-limiting adverse events and no clinically significant changes in blood work. 2.5% iPAAG appears to be well tolerated, safe, and effective for the IA treatment of canine elbow OA. Study limitations included a small sample size and lack of control group. These findings support 2.5% iPAAG as a targeted therapy for canine elbow OA. Further research is warranted to evaluate histological effects.

papers.title: Case Report: Long term multimodality treatment of canine hepatocellular carcinoma with serial monitoring of serum alpha-fetoprotein.
papers.authors: Dan TJ, Yang CH, Kim YJ, Kang MH, Kang MA, Lee KS, Park HM
papers.abstract: A 13-year-old spayed female Shih Tzu presented with a several-month history of progressively increasing liver enzyme activities concurrent with managed hyperadrenocorticism. Diagnostic imaging revealed a solitary hepatic mass originating from the caudate process of the caudate lobe adhering to the caudal vena cava. Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) was confirmed via histopathological examination of an ultrasound-guided tru-cut biopsy, accompanied by a markedly elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) concentration. Molecular targeted therapy with olaparib was initiated since complete surgical resection was unachievable due to tumor adherence to the caudal vena cava and conventional chemotherapy has limited efficacy for canine HCC, based on genomic profiling. Following objective tumor progression and worsening mass effect after 2 months, cytoreductive surgery was performed. Postoperatively, olaparib and canine interleukin-15 (cIL-15) immunotherapy were instituted to control potential micrometastases. The patient achieved clinical and radiographic stability for a 10-month follow-up period, accompanied by a significant drop in serum AFP levels. However, following the discontinuation of cIL-15 and subsequent reduction of olaparib dosage because of suspected adverse effects, serum AFP levels rebounded progressively, and tumor recurrence was confirmed via ultrasonography. The patient died 20 months after the initial detection of the mass. This case describes the clinical course of canine HCC managed with a multimodal therapeutic approach and highlights the potential utility of serum AFP as an adjunctive biomarker for disease monitoring.

papers.title: Epidemiology of voluntarily reported dog and cat bite incidents in a large-scale, multi-site veterinary network in the UK and Ireland.
papers.authors: Malkani R, Singleton D, Martin D, Vinke M, Playforth L, Collis M, Oxley JA
papers.abstract: Dog and cat bites are an occupational risk within veterinary practise. Despite this, there is minimal research exploring the occurrence and details surrounding such incidents. The aim of this study was to use a large veterinary group's existing incident and near miss reporting system in the UK to explore the incidence of dog and cat bite reporting and surrounding details of such incidents. Dog and cat bite incidents were identified from January 2024 to October 2025 covering all clinics in the UK and Ireland (>1,000). A total of 2,327 dog (1,239; 53.24%) and cat (1,088; 46.76%) bites were reported. The most common anatomical bite location was reported to be the hands and fingers for both dog (63.0%) and cat (80.6%) bites. The majority of bites for cats (77.96%) and dogs (80.60%) occurred between 9 a.m. and 6 p.m. Location of in-clinic bites differed between staff, with the veterinarians most commonly bitten in the consult room and non-veterinarians most often bitten in the preparation area. Regarding perceived behaviour, the term 'aggression' was most frequently used in reports. In conclusion, this report highlights the common occurrence of dog and cat bite related injuries, providing insights into surrounding factors. Factors need to be considered to reduce bites such as low stress handling, environment adaption and encouraging advancement of knowledge of animal behaviour. More needs to be done to help the reporting of incidents, incorporate human behaviour change approach and education to prevent bite incidents.

papers.title: Manganese dioxide nanozyme alleviates PEDV GIIc-associated growth retardation in neonatal piglets by improving antioxidant status, intestinal morphology, and manganese homeostasis.
papers.authors: Wang J, Lai X, Hu M, Liang S, Wu T, Fan X, Luo Y, He J, Che L, Chen D, Wu A
papers.abstract: Porcine epidemic diarrhea virus (PEDV) infection threatens swine production, and growth retardation in neonatal piglets born to infected sows requires practical intervention. This study evaluated the effects of oral manganese dioxide (MnO 2 ) nanozyme supplementation on growth and physiological indices in these piglets. In this study, 16 litters from PEDV GIIc-infected sows were assigned to four treatment groups according to body condition and PEDV RT-qPCR Ct value, with four litters from uninfected sows used as the negative control (NC). From 3 d of age to 21 d of age, piglets from PEDV-infected sows received oral MnO 2 nanozyme at different concentrations every other day. Compared with NC group, PEDV-positive control (PC) group had lower average daily gain and jejunal villus height ( P < 0.05), decreased serum CAT activity and serum GSH concentration, reduced jejunal GSH concentration, altered manganese transporter expression in the duodenum, and increased hepatic manganese accumulation. In piglets, oral MnO 2 nanozyme restored average daily gain to normal levels, improved jejunal villus height, and maintained GSH concentrations in serum, jejunum, and liver at levels not different from NC. MnO 2 nanozyme administration also increased duodenal DMT1 expression, decreased hepatic expression of transporters such as ZIP8, tended to increase duodenal manganese content, reduced hepatic manganese-transporter expression relative to the PC group, and alleviated hepatic manganese accumulation. In rectal fecal samples from piglets, MnO 2 nanozyme increased the relative abundance of beneficial bacterial genera, including Prevotella and Bifidobacterium . Oral MnO 2 nanozyme supplementation was associated with alleviation of PEDV GIIc-associated growth retardation and changes in intestinal morphology, antioxidant status, and manganese-related indices. The 5 mg/L group showed a favorable growth response at the lowest tested concentration. Baseline body-weight differences should be considered when interpreting these findings, and further controlled studies are needed to establish the underlying mechanisms and optimal administration regimen.

papers.title: Assessment of radiographic healing after tibial plateau leveling osteotomy in young and older dogs using the modified RUST scoring system.
papers.authors: Anderson BL, Frederick SW, Popovitch C
papers.abstract: To compare radiographic osteotomy healing scores after tibial plateau leveling osteotomy (TPLO) in young (2-5 years) and old (8-12 years) dogs using the modified Radiographic Union Score for Tibial fractures (mRUST) system, and to evaluate agreement between large language model-assisted interpretation (LLM), surgeon, and surgical resident scoring. Client-owned, 20-40 kg dogs treated with unilateral TPLO at ages 2-5 or 8-12 years between 2023 and 2025 were retrospectively identified. Dogs with endocrinopathy or atypical TPLO or recovery were excluded. Dogs were assigned to Group 1 (2-5 years) or Group 2 (8-12 years). 8-week postoperative radiographs were scored independently by an LLM, a surgeon, and a surgical resident using the 4-point mRUST system. Scores were compared between age groups using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test, and interrater agreement was assessed using an intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Group 1 had 49 dogs; Group 2 had 51 dogs. Group 1 had a mean (SD) age of 3.82 (1.11) years, while Group 2 had a mean (SD) age of 9.24 (0.99) years. mRUST scores did not differ between age groups across LLM ( p  = 0.352), surgeon ( p  = 0.908), or resident assessments ( p  = 0.588). LLM, surgeon, and resident scores had only fair agreement (ICC = 0.4504, p  < 0.001). Chronological age was not associated with mRUST score following TPLO at the 8-week postoperative evaluation. The mRUST system demonstrated moderate agreement between human observers. LLM scoring showed promise; further refinement is needed for clinical application.

papers.title: Outcomes and prognostic factors in dogs with subcutaneous and intramuscular hemangiosarcoma treated with hypofractionated radiation therapy and chemotherapy.
papers.authors: Rebelo AP, Furtado A, Sellon R, Roberts GD, Fidel J
papers.abstract: Subcutaneous (SC) and intramuscular (IM) hemangiosarcoma (HSA) in dogs are aggressive malignancies with high rates of recurrence and metastasis. Surgery is the primary treatment, but incomplete excision is common, and the role of radiation therapy (RT) remains unclear. This single-institution retrospective study evaluated outcomes and toxicities in dogs with SC and IM HSA treated with hypofractionated RT using either 24 Gy in three 8-Gy fractions (days 0, 7, and 21) or 30 Gy in five 6-Gy fractions every other day, with or without surgery and chemotherapy. Fifty-three dogs were included: 27/53 (51%) SC HSA and 26/53 (49%) IM HSA; 35/53 (66%) had macroscopic disease at RT. Overall, 47/53 (89%) received chemotherapy, of which 42/47 (89%) received doxorubicin; 35/42 (83%) received it concurrently with the first RT fraction. Among 30 evaluable dogs, the RT objective response rate (ORR) was 93% (37% complete, 56% partial). Local progression or recurrence (LPR) occurred in 11/36 (30%) dogs after a median of 128 days, predominantly with macroscopic disease (10/11). Median time to progression (TTP) was not reached (95% CI, 621 days-not reached). In an exploratory multivariable Cox analysis, metastasis was associated with increased hazard of LPR (HR, 14.95; 95% CI, 2.84-78.72; p  = 0.0014), whereas surgery was associated with a lower hazard, but not significantly (HR, 0.15; 95% CI, 0.018-1.24; p  = 0.079). Overall median survival time (MST) was 306 days (95% CI, 284-875). On univariable analysis, anemia, absence of surgery, macroscopic disease at RT, metastasis, and tumor size at diagnosis >6 cm were associated with shorter survival. Dogs undergoing surgery prior to RT had longer survival (MST, 2059 vs. 287 days; p = 0.007). In multivariable analysis, anemia remained independently associated with increased hazard of death (HR, 3.20; 95% CI, 1.38-7.45; p  = 0.0069), whereas metastasis, surgery, and tumor size were not independently associated with survival. Chemotherapy was not associated with survival. Radiation-associated adverse events were generally mild. Hypofractionated RT, as part of multimodal treatment in most dogs, was associated with a high ORR and may provide durable local control in dogs with non-visceral HSA.

papers.title: Combined cold atmospheric plasma and photobiomodulation is associated with improved early macroscopic and ultrasonographic wound-healing parameters after unilateral mastectomy in female dogs: an exploratory randomized intra-individual controlled clinical study.
papers.authors: da Silva GRV, de Oliveira Filho MS, de França Silvestre SF, Carneiro GA, de Lucena RBM, Costa CMR, Facundo PLD, Silva FLC, de Paula Antunes JMA, de Castro Demoner L, de Paula VV, Carvalho AT, Barboza CAG, Júnior CA, de Oliveira MF, de Almeida Amorim MM, de Moura CEB
papers.abstract: Postmastectomy complications remain relevant in veterinary surgery. Although cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) and photobiomodulation (PBM) may improve tissue repair, evidence on their combined use is limited. This exploratory pilot study evaluated CAP-PBM therapy in nine female dogs undergoing unilateral mastectomy. A prospective, randomized, blinded, intra-individual controlled clinical study was conducted in nine female dogs with mammary neoplasia undergoing clinically indicated unilateral mastectomy. In each dog, one half of the surgical wound was randomly assigned to receive sequential CAP and PBM therapy, while the contralateral half remained untreated and served as an intra-individual control. Evaluations were performed on postoperative days 3, 7, and 14 (D3, D7, and D14) using macroscopic scoring systems, ultrasonography, and infrared thermography; histomorphometric analysis was performed only on D7. Treated regions showed significantly lower Modified Hollander Scar Scale (p < 0.001) and Modified Draize Scoring System (p = 0.001) scores. Ultrasonographic assessment demonstrated lower semiquantitative scores (p = 0.029) and reduced subcutaneous thickness (p = 0.034), especially during the early postoperative period. Thermographic findings did not differ significantly between groups. Histological analysis revealed numerically greater re-epithelialization in treated areas, although without statistical significance (p > 0.05). In this exploratory pilot study, combined CAP + PBM therapy was associated with improved early macroscopic and ultrasonographic healing parameters after mastectomy in female dogs. These preliminary findings support further investigation of CAP + PBM as a promising non-invasive adjuvant strategy for postoperative wound management, pending confirmation in larger, adequately powered randomized studies.

papers.title: Histomorphometric characterization of cardiac nodes in cattle, ponies, and cats.
papers.authors: Gómez-Torres F, Ballesteros-Acuña L, Ruíz-Saurí A
papers.abstract: The sinoatrial node (SAN) and atrioventricular node (AVN) are essential components of the cardiac conduction system and play a critical role in initiating and propagating the electrical impulse. To characterise these cardiac nodes across different species, we examined the hearts of ten cattle, ten cats, and five male ponies without evidence of cardiac disease using conventional histological and immunohistochemical techniques. Morphometric parameters of the nodes and their constituent cells were quantified at different magnifications. The SAN displayed an oval morphology in all species. Its diameter was 888.58 ± 6.36 μm in cats, 2143.17 ± 199.13 μm in ponies, and 2033.28 ± 939.44 μm in cattle. Mean nodal density was significantly higher in ponies than in cattle (p = 0.011). Pacemaker (P) cells of the AVN were significantly larger in ungulate species than in cats (p < 0.001). Heart bone (os cordis) was identified in all ten cattle hearts and in one cat heart, showing typical features of compact bone and bone marrow. Cartilaginous metaplasia was observed in all pony hearts and in 60% of cat hearts and was associated with reduced AVN size and cellularity in cats. These findings highlight important interspecies differences and contribute to the understanding of conduction system pathology in veterinary cardiology. The structural changes in the cardiac nodes in these species warrant more in-depth functional research, given the lack of functional cardiac assessment and the small sample size.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Experimental Evaluation of the Immunogenicity of Feline Erythrocyte Antigen 6 (FEA 6) in Transfusion-Naive FEA 6-Negative Cats.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Bangash MY, Blais MC
papers.abstract: ObjectivesFeline Erythrocyte Antigen 6 (FEA 6) is a newly identified red blood cell (RBC) antigen in cats discovered following an unintentional sensitization event, suggesting it can be immunogenic. Its ability to consistently induce alloimmunization remains unknown. This prospective study evaluated FEA 6 immunogenicity in transfusion-naive, FEA 6-negative cats by assessing anti-FEA 6 alloantibody production and plasma levels. A secondary objective was to bank polyclonal anti-FEA 6 antibodies.MethodsFifty-three cats underwent AB and extensive blood typing for FEAs 1-6, naturally occurring alloantibody (NOAb) screening, and compatibility testing to select donor-recipient pairs. FEA 6 prevalence was assessed in 82 type A cats. Two transfusion-naive, FEA 6-negative cats received FEA 6-positive, otherwise compatible RBC transfusions and were monitored for anti-FEA 6 alloantibody production by gel column agglutination. Repeat transfusions were performed if alloantibodies became undetectable. Agreement between recipient-derived and reference anti-FEA 6 alloantibodies was evaluated in 51 type A cats using kappa statistics.ResultsFEA 6 prevalence among type A cats was 75.6% (62/82); NOAb were detected in 10.3% of screened type A cats, but none were directed against FEA 6. Both recipients developed anti-FEA 6 alloantibodies. Recipient 1 responded after two sensitizations, whereas recipient 2 responded after a single transfusion. Both reached peak titers of 1:8, with alloantibodies detectable through days 372 and 200, respectively. Recipient-derived anti-FEA 6 alloantibodies showed substantial agreement with the reference anti-FEA 6 antibody (κ = 0.64-0.78, P < .001) and almost perfect agreement with each other (κ = 0.87, P < .001).Conclusions and relevanceTransfusion of FEA 6-positive RBCs induced anti-FEA 6 alloantibodies in all transfusion-naive, FEA 6-negative recipients, supporting FEA 6 immunogenicity and its likely contribution to unexplained post-transfusion alloantibodies in cats. The resulting polyclonal antibodies may support FEA 6 typing and transfusion research, although more durable reagents remain needed.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Mineral Analysis of Feline Treats: Unrecognized Sources of Phosphorus and Calcium in the Management of Chronic Kidney Disease.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Harris AN, Harris T, Vaden S
papers.abstract: Dietary phosphorus restriction is a cornerstone of chronic kidney disease (CKD) management in cats. While therapeutic renal diets are formulated to limit phosphorus intake, treats also contribute to total dietary phosphorus and calcium intake. The objective of this study was to quantify the phosphorus and calcium content of some feline purée-style treats and evaluate their potential contribution to dietary mineral intake in cats with CKD. A convenience sample comprising four flavors of commercially available Inaba Churu purée treats and three flavors of Weurva low-phosphorus purée treats were analyzed. Phosphorus and calcium concentrations were quantified using inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry and reported descriptively as milligrams per sachet and milligrams per 100 kcal. Phosphorus content varied widely across products, ranging from 9 to 36 mg per sachet (64-600mg/100kcal). The evaluated Churu treats contained higher phosphorus concentrations (29-36 mg/ sachet) than the evaluated Weruva low-phosphorus formulations (9-10 mg/sachet). Calcium concentrations ranged from 0.14 to 4.06 mg per sachet (2.3-67.7 mg/100 kcal), with corresponding calcium-to-phosphorus (Ca:P) ratios ranging from 0.004 to 0.119. Phosphorus and calcium content, including Ca:P ratios, varied substantially among the products evaluated. These differences should be considered as part of the overall dietary management of cats with CKD, particularly when treats are administered routinely.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Assessment of an educational social media campaign on improving feline osteoarthritis pain awareness and knowledge among cat owners.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Wong WS, Alcântara H, Bukhari SSUH, Murrell J, Steagall P
papers.abstract: Objectives - Feline osteoarthritis (OA) is highly prevalent but often underdiagnosed, largely owing to owners' difficulty recognising subtle clinical signs. This study evaluated the effects of an evidence-based, peer-reviewed educational social media campaign on cat owners' knowledge and awareness of feline OA.Methods - A prospective, interventional study was conducted with a convenience sample of adult, non-veterinary cat owners recruited via social media. Participants completed a validated online survey assessing knowledge and attitudes about feline OA before and after viewing an evidence based social media campaign (i.e., the intervention) covering 4 domains (introduction, clinical signs, diagnosis, management). Paired non parametric tests compared pre- and post-intervention total knowledge scores, individual knowledge items and Likert scale attitude items.Results - A total of 53 participants completed both surveys. Mean total knowledge scores increased from 19.9 ± 3.1 to 23.6 ± 2.8 (p < 0.001). Correct identification of OA as non-curable increased from 49.1% to 83% (p < 0.001), and the misconception that OA only affects senior cats decreased from 13.2% to 0% (p = 0.02). Recognition of key risk factors improved: neutering after 6 months of age (9.4% to 60.4%, p < 0.001) and outdoor access (28.3% to 73.6%, p < 0.001). Recognition of scratching posts as an option for environment changes increased from 24.5% to 60.3% (p <0.001). The owners' confidence in their ability to contribute to diagnosis increased (Hodges-Lehmann shift +0.99, p = 0.04), knowledge of environmental modifications increased (+1.49, p <0.001), and stress about lifelong management decreased (-0.99, p = 0.01). Most participants (≥91%) found the intervention materials enjoyable and useful; 96% would share the content with others.Conclusion and relevance - An evidence-based educational social media campaign significantly improved cat owners' awareness and knowledge regarding feline OA, suggesting a scalable platform to complement traditional veterinarian-client communication.

papers.title: Efficacy and Safety of Allogeneic Mesenchymal Stromal Cells Versus Lokivetmab in Mild-To-Moderate Canine Atopic Dermatitis: A Single-Blind Randomised Study.
papers.authors: Pasikowska M, Ciszewska-Ceran J, Cekiera A, Gocek E, Grzesiak J, Reniewicz P, Popiel J, Szczepanik M, Wilkołek P
papers.abstract: Canine atopic dermatitis (cAD) is a chronic allergic inflammatory skin disease that requires multimodal management. Allogeneic mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) have emerged as a potential therapeutic option. To evaluate the efficacy and safety of an investigational allogeneic adipose-derived MSC product (PK/CM-1) in dogs with cAD. Dogs with mild-to-moderate cAD were enrolled in a single-blind, randomised study and allocated in a 2:1 ratio either to an experimental group (receiving a single intravenous dose of PK/CM-1) or a control group (receiving three monthly subcutaneous doses of lokivetmab). Clinical outcomes were assessed using the Canine Atopic Dermatitis Extent and Severity Index, 4th iteration (CADESI-04) and pruritus Visual Analog Scale (PVAS) scores on Day (D)28 (primary end-point) and D7, D56 and D84. Safety assessments included haematological and biochemical analyses on D84, along with monitoring for adverse events. Thirty-two dogs were included. By D28, both CADESI-04 and PVAS scores had significantly decreased from baseline in both groups. No significant differences between groups were observed on D28 (p = 0.696 and p = 0.088, respectively). Clinical improvement was sustained up to D84. In the experimental group, CADESI-04 and PVAS scores were lower on D84 than on D28 (p = 0.0074 and p = 0.0015, respectively). Two adverse events (one severe and one mild) occurred during PK/CM-1 administration. No clinically significant haematological or biochemical abnormalities were observed. PK/CM-1 demonstrated comparable efficacy and safety to those of lokivetmab over a 3 month period. Careful monitoring is recommended during intravenous administration of PK/CM-1.

papers.title: Target-controlled infusion of propofol induces rapid hypertriglyceridemia in healthy cats.
papers.authors: Arboit F, Mangini LT, Gasparotto JC, Griebeler LB, Oliveira JO, Vieira LS, Ohashi GS, Cadiñanos VDS, Paraguassú AO, Oberbeck EV, de Souza LB, Freitas GC, Floriano BP, Soares AV
papers.abstract: To evaluate serum triglyceride concentrations during target-controlled infusion (TCI) of propofol in healthy cats undergoing elective orchiectomy and to investigate the relationship between cumulative propofol dose and triglyceride concentrations. 8 healthy male cats were anesthetized using propofol administered via a TCI system targeting a plasma concentration of 7 µg/mL for 45 minutes. Blood samples were collected at baseline, after premedication, immediately after induction, and at 20 and 40 minutes of infusion for determination of serum triglyceride concentrations. Serum triglycerides increased significantly following propofol administration, with elevations detectable immediately after induction. Median concentrations were 41 mg/dL (range, 31 to 75) at baseline, 32 mg/dL (range, 20 to 99) after premedication, 128 mg/dL (range, 72 to 215) immediately after induction, 132 mg/dL (range, 106 to 227) at 20 minutes of infusion, and 143 mg/dL (range, 57 to 230) at 40 minutes of infusion. During anesthesia, 75% of the animals exceeded the reference interval for triglycerides. No significant correlation was observed between propofol cumulative doses and triglyceride concentrations. Target-controlled propofol infusion is associated with a rapid increase in serum triglyceride concentrations in cats even during short anesthetic procedures. Given the use of prolonged propofol infusions in veterinary anesthesia, these findings highlight the importance of considering potential changes in serum triglyceride concentrations, particularly in patients with underlying lipid or metabolic dysfunction.

papers.title: Stability and dermatological safety assessment of Cryptocarya alba (Peumo) and Laureliopsis philippiana (Tepa) essential oil-carrying dry shampoo formulations for dermal use in dogs.
papers.authors: Varas M, Jacobs M, Rojas N, Ramos P, Bruna F, Valenzuela-Barra G, Correa O, Díaz-Parra A, Ahumada M, Maturana G, Martínez I, Abusleme F, Rivera B, Bargsted MO, Siel D, Bravo J
papers.abstract: Antibiotic resistance is a major concern in human and veterinary medicine, supporting the development of alternative topical products for companion animals. This study aimed to develop and evaluate essential oil (EO)-based dry shampoo formulations incorporating EOs from Cryptocarya alba and Laureliopsis philippiana as potential veterinary dermocosmetic platforms for canine skin care and complementary management of superficial pyoderma. Starch-based dry shampoo prototypes containing C. alba or L. philippiana EOs were developed using corn starch, tapioca starch, or their mixtures. Magnesium stearate (MgS) was evaluated as a functional excipient, and two mixing protocols were compared. Optimized formulations were subjected to physicochemical characterization, thermal, mechanical, and 9-month stability assessments, and in vitro antibacterial testing against Staphylococcus pseudintermedius . Preclinical dermal safety was evaluated in BALB/c mice through macroscopic irritation scoring, body weight monitoring, and histological analysis. Subsequently, an exploratory, randomized, controlled, blinded, four-arm parallel-group study was conducted in 32 client-owned dogs with superficial pyoderma allocated to receive SLP, SCA, vehicle shampoo, or a chlorhexidine-based reference treatment for 21 days. MgS improved formulation homogeneity, fluidity, and reduced agglomeration, while the selected mixing protocol enhanced overall powder performance. The optimized formulations showed preliminary physical stability, although progressive changes in texture, fluidity, agglomeration tendency, and aroma were observed during storage. In vitro antibacterial activity was assay-dependent: no measurable inhibition zones were observed by agar diffusion, whereas serial dilution and viable-count assays showed concentration-dependent reductions in bacterial recovery, including effects associated with the vehicle formulation. No macroscopic or histological signs of dermal irritation were observed in mice. In dogs, the formulations were well tolerated under the evaluated conditions. Microbiological outcomes differed numerically among groups but not significantly; among the EO-containing formulations, SCA showed the most favorable exploratory profile, including culture negativity in 3/8 dogs and the highest proportion of dogs reaching a non-significant bacterial burden. These findings support the feasibility of incorporating C. alba and L. philippiana EOs into starch-based dry shampoo prototypes and provide preliminary evidence of physical stability and dermal tolerability. However, the assay-dependent antibacterial response, alkaline formulation pH, limited batch replication, and exploratory clinical design preclude conclusions regarding clinical efficacy. Further studies should include formulation optimization, quantitative chemical stability assessment, dermal permeation studies, and larger randomized controlled clinical trials.

papers.title: Perioperative analgesic effects of opiranserin in canine castration: a pilot study.
papers.authors: Lee S, Oh S, Lee I, Son WG
papers.abstract: Opiranserin, a non-opioid analgesic acting as a glycine transporter 2 inhibitor and 5-HT2A receptor antagonist, was evaluated for reducing intraoperative rescue analgesia and postoperative pain in dogs undergoing castration under isoflurane anesthesia. Eight healthy male Beagle dogs were randomized to receive a continuous rate infusion of opiranserin (5 mg·kg -1 ·h -1 for 1 h before induction, then 0.33 mg·kg -1 ·h -1 for 9 h; n = 4) or 0.9% saline ( n = 4). Anesthesia was induced with alfaxalone and maintained with isoflurane (1.5% end-tidal); all dogs received meloxicam and cefazolin preoperatively, without locoregional analgesia. Hemodynamic responses (ΔMAP, ΔHR) were recorded across 11 surgical events; rescue remifentanil was given when both increased ≥20% from baseline. Postoperative pain was scored with the Glasgow Composite Measure Pain Scale-Short Form (GCMPS-SF) from 30 min after extubation (T0) through T7, with rescue analgesia at scores ≥5. Primary outcomes were intraoperative rescue analgesia frequency and postoperative GCMPS-SF scores; secondary outcomes were intraoperative hemodynamic responses, postoperative rescue consumption, and adverse effects. Data were analyzed with Mann-Whitney U tests and linear mixed models with Bonferroni-adjusted comparisons. The opiranserin group required fewer intraoperative rescue interventions than the normal saline group (median 2 [2-2] vs. 6.5 [3-9]; p = 0.021). GCMPS-SF scores showed significant effects of group ( p = 0.030), time ( p = 0.047), and group × time interaction ( p = 0.034), with lower scores in the opiranserin group at T1 (adjusted p = 0.012) but not at other time points. Among secondary outcomes, significant overall effects of group were found for ΔMAP ( p = 0.011) and ΔHR ( p = 0.048), and of surgical event for both ( p < 0.001 and p = 0.008), with no group × event interaction; no individual event differed significantly after correction. Cumulative postoperative rescue analgesic consumption and the incidence of adverse effects did not differ between groups. These preliminary findings suggest that opiranserin may reduce intraoperative rescue analgesia requirements and attenuate postoperative pain in dogs, warranting confirmation in larger trials. The absence of significant adverse effects is reassuring but should be interpreted cautiously given the small sample size.

papers.title: Use of plasma chromogranin a epitopes vasostatin and catestatin as biomarkers for catecholamine-producing tumours in dogs.
papers.authors: Prabert J, Hanson J, Ishigaki K, Asano K, Höglund K, Stridsberg M, Höglund OV
papers.abstract: Differentiation of catecholamine-producing tumours from other adrenal tumours remains difficult. Chromogranin A (CgA) is a marker for catecholamine secretion in the body. An assay for quantification of the CgA epitopes vasostatin and catestatin has been validated for use in dogs but not yet evaluated in dogs with catecholamine-producing tumours. The aims were to evaluate the assays foranalysis of plasma concentrations of the CgA epitopes vasostatin and catestatin in dogs with adrenal tumours and to compare concentrations between catecholamine-producing tumours and adrenocortical tumours in dogs that were subjected to adrenalectomy. Twelve dogs with histopathologically confirmed catecholamine-secreting tumours (eleven pheochromocytomas (PCCs), one extra-adrenal sympathetic paraganglioma (PGL)) and twelve with adrenocortical tumours were included in the study. Plasma concentrations of the CgA epitopes vasostatin and catestatin were determined byradioimmunoassay (RIA), before adrenalectomy in 23 out of 24 dogs and after adrenalectomy in six of the dogs with catecholamine-secreting tumours (five PCC, one PGL). Tumour diagnosis was made by histopathology in all cases. Overall, median plasma concentration of the CgA epitopevasostatin in dogs with catecholamine-secreting tumours was 0.82 nmol/L (interquartile range (IQR) 0.52 to 1.60 nmol/L), which was significantly higher(Wilcoxon rank sum exact test, P= 0.0374) than the vasostatin concentration in adrenocortical tumours (median 0.50; IQR 0.34 to 0.59 nmol/L). A subsetof dogs (5/12) with catecholamine-secreting tumours had elevated plasma vasostatin concentrations preoperatively. After successful surgery, thepreoperatively elevated plasma vasostatin concentrations decreased numerically, however without reaching statistical significance. Catestatin concentrationdid not differ between tumour types. Elevated plasma concentration of the CgA epitope vasostatin showed potential as a biomarker for asubset of catecholamine-secreting tumours.

papers.title: Target-controlled infusion of propofol induces rapid hypertriglyceridemia in healthy cats.
papers.authors: Arboit F, Mangini LT, Gasparotto JC, Griebeler LB, Oliveira JO, Vieira LS, Ohashi GS, Cadiñanos VDS, Paraguassú AO, Oberbeck EV, de Souza LB, Freitas GC, Floriano BP, Soares AV

papers.title: Spontaneous tumors in dogs and cats in Algeria: a dual-source descriptive study of practitioner-reported patterns and histopathology-submitted cases.
papers.authors: Bouchoukh AS, Boukhechem S, Bougherara H, Chaabi AZ
papers.abstract: Algeria has no documented national companion-animal cancer registry, and limited information is available on tumors encountered in veterinary practice or reaching histopathological confirmation. This dual-source descriptive study combined two independently analyzed components: a histopathology-based descriptive case series of diagnostic tumor submissions from dogs and cats, and a cross-sectional questionnaire survey of veterinarians practicing in Algeria. The first component characterized tumors reaching histopathological confirmation, whereas the second examined practitioner-reported tumor patterns, perceived diagnostic-resource availability, and self-reported preparedness. The histopathology-based case series comprised 86 tumor submissions from 81 animals accrued between March 2022 and March 2025. Mammary tumors were the largest category (43/86; 50.0%), followed by cutaneous/subcutaneous tumors (20/86; 23.3%); 80 tumors (93.0%) were classified as malignant. Among 162 questionnaire responses collected between October 2024 and May 2025, 111 respondents selected "dogs and cats" as their main animal group. Mammary tumors were reported by 109 respondents (98.2%), cutaneous/subcutaneous tumors by 79 (71.2%), and canine transmissible venereal tumor (CTVT) by 54 (48.6%); multiple categories could be reported. The most frequent self-reported preparedness rating was "Moderately prepared" (52/111; 46.8%), while 99 of 110 respondents with valid data (90.0%) rated diagnostic resources as either "Insufficient" or "Not at all satisfactory." Mammary and cutaneous/subcutaneous tumors ranked first and second in both sources, whereas the rankings of the remaining categories differed. Because the sources represented different populations, analytical units, denominators, and diagnostic pathways, the comparison was restricted to an exploratory descriptive assessment and was not interpreted as evidence of differences in population-level tumor occurrence. This study provides an initial structured account of companion-animal tumor documentation in Algeria. The partial agreement between the two sources, together with unfavorable diagnostic-availability ratings, suggests potential gaps between clinical recognition, histopathological confirmation, and systematic recording. Standardized submission and coding procedures, improved specimen-transport and formal pathology-referral pathways, broader geographic participation, and progressive development of companion-animal cancer registration are needed to strengthen the national evidence base.

papers.title: Molecular evidence of Bartonella spp. in wild felids from Brazil.
papers.authors: Dias CM, Lee DAB, da Silva JVDSA, Nunes LB, May Júnior JA, Baggio-Souza V, Peters FB, Favarini MO, Albano APN, Segui SD, Terra SR, Tirelli FP, Cherem J, Morzele HB, Tortato MA, Lagos AR, Manzano FV, de Oliveira Tourinho TC, Machado RZ, Soares JF, André MR
papers.abstract: Among Felidae, domestic cats play a role as reservoirs for Bartonella henselae, Bartonella clarridgeiae, and Bartonella koehlerae. Despite the well-known relationship between Bartonella spp. and domestic cats, to date, there is still a paucity of reports on Bartonella spp. in wild felids. The aim of this study was to molecularly detect and characterize Bartonella spp. in blood and tissue samples from wild felids sampled in Brazil. Among 291 DNA samples (211 blood, 77 spleens and three livers), 3.09% (9/291) were positive in the Quantitative Real-Time PCR (qPCR) assay for Bartonella spp. based on the nuoG gene: 1/44 Leopardus pardalis, 3/61 Leopardus geoffroyi, 1/66 Panthera onca, 1/3 Herpailurus yagouaroundi, and 3/32 Leopardus wiedii. In the phylogenetic analyses, while the gltA sequence detected in L. wiedii grouped with Bartonella henselae, the gltA and ftsZ sequences detected in L. geoffroyi clustered within the same subclade as Bartonella sp. sequences previously identified in wild rodents and associated fleas. These findings reinforce that besides harboring Bartonella species associated with cats, wild felids also may act as accidental hosts for Bartonella species associated with wild small mammals, possibly as a consequence of predation.

papers.title: Doxorubicin-induced Cardiotoxicity in Dogs: A Narrative Review.
papers.authors: Sunpongsri S, Roos T, Gerhing R, Zandvliet M, Santarelli G
papers.abstract: Doxorubicin, an anthracycline widely used in both human and veterinary oncology, is highly effective against a variety of malignancies in dogs, including lymphomas, sarcomas and carcinomas. Despite its efficacy, doxorubicin exposure can be associated with cardiotoxicity, which may present acutely or chronically, potentially leading to severe cardiac arrhythmia and congestive heart failure. Mechanisms underlying cardiotoxicity are multifactorial, including oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, DNA damage via topoisomerase IIβ, inflammation and dysregulated cell death pathways such as apoptosis, pyroptosis and ferroptosis. In dogs, known risk factors include higher cumulative dose, breed predisposition to idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy, and higher body weight. Cardiac biomarkers, electrocardiography, echocardiography and other advanced imaging techniques have been employed to detect cardiac changes that can be seen also in the absence of clinical signs. However, current evidence is predominantly derived from experimental and retrospective research, highlighting the need for large prospective clinical studies to strengthen recommendations for monitoring and prevention. A deeper understanding of doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity in dogs is needed to identify factors influencing individual susceptibility, clarify the progression from subclinical damage to clinical cardiac dysfunction, and guide future research. Emerging approaches, including advanced echocardiography, microRNAs, proteomic biomarkers and pharmacokinetic modelling, may help improve early detection and guide more individualised dosing to minimise toxicity.

papers.title: A zingiberene-selenium nanoparticle formulation modulates oxidative, inflammatory, and osteogenic responses during femoral fracture healing in rats.
papers.authors: Albarakati AJA
papers.abstract: Bone fracture healing involves coordinated inflammatory, oxidative, and remodeling processes. This study evaluated free zingiberene and a zingiberene-selenium nanoparticle (zingiberene-SeNP) formulation in a rat femoral fracture model. Twenty-four adult male Wistar rats were assigned to intact control, fracture control, fracture plus zingiberene (10 mg/kg/day), or fracture plus zingiberene-SeNP formulation (0.5 mg/kg/day, expressed as total administered formulation mass) groups for 35 days. Outcomes included serum calcium, phosphate, magnesium, and alkaline phosphatase (ALP); malondialdehyde (MDA), nitric oxide (NO), reduced glutathione (GSH), superoxide dismutase (SOD), and catalase (CAT); C-reactive protein (CRP), cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2), prostaglandin E₂ (PGE₂), myeloperoxidase (MPO), tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β), and nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB); C-terminal telopeptide of type I collagen (CTX-I), calcitonin, osteocalcin, osteoprotegerin (OPG), and bone morphogenetic protein-1 (BMP-1), together with radiographic and hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) histology. Fracture disrupted mineral, oxidative, inflammatory, and bone-turnover profiles. Both treatments improved multiple biochemical and inflammatory indices versus fracture control. The zingiberene-SeNP formulation showed stronger effects than free zingiberene for selected endpoints, including MDA, GSH, ALP, PGE₂, TNF-α, IL-1β, NF-κB, CTX-I, calcitonin, osteocalcin, OPG, and BMP-1. Radiographic and histological findings were consistent with improved callus organization and bone maturation. Overall, both treatments favorably modulated fracture-repair responses, with greater effects of the nanoformulation for selected parameters.

papers.title: Cross-sectional analysis of 152 hyperthyroid cats presented for radioactive iodine therapy in South Korea.
papers.authors: Son D, Chae Y, Yun T, Kim H, Lim JC, Kang BT
papers.abstract: Feline hyperthyroidism is one of the most common endocrinopathies in cats; however, its epidemiological characteristics remain poorly understood in South Korea. Although radioactive iodine therapy (RAIT) is a definitive treatment, studies focusing specifically on cats with hyperthyroidism undergoing RAIT are limited. Medical records of 152 cats with hyperthyroidism presented for RAIT were retrospectively reviewed to describe their epidemiological and clinical features. The median age at diagnosis was 12 years, and 30.3% of the cats were diagnosed incidentally. RAIT was usually performed soon after diagnosis, with a median disease duration of 5 months; only 4.6% of cats had a disease duration >2 years. Unilateral thyroid disease was the predominant pattern (50.7%), and severe hyperthyroidism (total thyroxine ≥19.4 μg/dl) was observed in 10.5% of cats. Only 40.1% of cats underwent RAIT following the veterinarian's recommendation, whereas 59.9% of owners sought RAIT independently. Human-licensed or generic methimazole was used more frequently than veterinary-licensed methimazole (84.0 vs. 18.1%). Pruritus occurred more frequently with human-licensed or generic methimazole than with veterinary-licensed methimazole ( p = 0.047). All cats were housed indoors. The regional distribution of cases differed from the reported national distribution of owned cats ( p = 0.016). No cats originated from Jeju-do, which differed significantly from the mainland regions ( p = 0.0004). Longer disease duration was associated with more advanced disease, including higher thyroid hormone levels and scintigraphic activity, increased bilateral involvement, and a higher rate of refractory response to antithyroid drugs (all p ≤ 0.001). This is the first study to characterize cats with hyperthyroidism that were presented for RAIT in South Korea. Key findings included an owner-driven pattern of RAIT selection, early use of definitive therapy despite a relatively late diagnosis, predominant use of non-veterinary methimazole formulations, and a higher frequency of pruritus as an adverse effect. These findings contribute to the epidemiological understanding of feline hyperthyroidism and may inform clinical decision-making in South Korea.

papers.title: Evaluation of the clinical course of immune-mediated polyneuropathy in cats after treatment with human intravenous immunoglobulins.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Schmitz AK, Sablotni Aguilera AP, Buhmann G, van Renen J, Parzefall B, Matiasek K, Matiasek LA, Fischer A
papers.abstract: Immune-mediated polyneuropathy (IMPN) manifests with generalised lower motor neuron (LMN) weakness and a remittent or relapsing clinical course. Evidence-based treatment recommendations for severely or chronically affected cats are limited. The objective of this study was to evaluate the clinical course and outcome of cats with IMPN after treatment with human intravenous immunoglobulins (hIVIg). Medical records from two veterinary referral hospitals were reviewed (2018-2025) for cats with IMPN treated with hIVIg. Cats were treated with 1-2 g/kg hIVIg divided over 2-4 days (0.5 g/kg/day). Clinical information, diagnostic findings, treatment details, and short- and long-term follow-up were evaluated retrospectively. Follow-up information was obtained from medical records and owner communication. Minimum follow-up duration was 8 months (range 8-51; median 17). Clinical course (partial and complete recovery, relapses) was compared between cats with acute/recent onset (four cats) or chronic presentation (five cats). Of nine cats, eight exhibited clinical improvement after hIVIg administration, achieving ambulatory status (walking >5 steps) within a median of 4 days (range 2-8). One cat failed to respond to hIVIg but improved after subsequent prednisolone therapy. For the overall cohort, the median time to complete recovery was 20 days, while the median time to partial recovery was 14 days. Relapses occurred in four cats, but weakness was less severe, and all cats recovered again. The remaining five cats remained relapse-free. Human IVIg was well tolerated in this small cohort, and rapid clinical improvement was observed in most treated cats. These findings suggest that hIVIg may be considered as a treatment option in selected cats with IMPN, including those with acute and chronic presentations. Larger prospective studies, including comparison with no treatment or corticosteroids, are warranted to further assess its efficacy.

papers.title: Reply to letter regarding "ACVIM-endorsed statement: consensus statement and systematic review on guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of chronic inflammatory enteropathy in dogs".
papers.authors: Heilmann RM, Jergens AE, Kathrani A, Allenspach K, Schmitz SS, Priestnall SL, Dandrieux JRS, O'Connor AM

papers.title: Medetomidine-vatinoxan is associated with a higher proportion of hypotension than dexmedetomidine in anesthetized dogs: a retrospective, matched-cohort study.
papers.authors: Rouse S, Muñoz K, Lerche P, Ballash G, Midon M, Aarnes TK, Pereira CHR
papers.abstract: To compare clinical parameters and medical interventions during the first hour of inhalant anesthesia in dogs administered medetomidine-vatinoxan (Zenalpha [ZEN]) versus dexmedetomidine (DEX) as IM preanesthetic agents. Medical records were searched to identify dogs premedicated with ZEN between August 2022 and January 2025. Dogs administered DEX between July 2021 and May 2026 were then identified and matched with α2-adrenergic receptor agonist dose equivalence prioritized. Generalized estimating equation models were constructed to assess associations between variables of interest and premedication type, while accounting for repeated measurements within paired matched sets. The ZEN group included 24 dogs (ZEN dose median, 10 μg/kg; range, 5 to 26 μg/kg), whereas the DEX group included 48 dogs (DEX dose median, 5 μg/kg; range, 3 to 10 μg/kg), with no differences between groups. Compared with DEX, premedication with ZEN was associated with an 18 beats/min higher heart rate, whereas mean arterial pressure was 19 mm Hg lower. Dogs receiving ZEN had 9.3-fold greater odds of receiving an IV fluid bolus and 6.8-fold greater odds of vasopressor administration. No differences were detectable between groups in IV interventions administered for a light plane of anesthesia. Findings indicated ZEN was associated with intraoperative hypotension in dogs during the first hour of volatile anesthesia, despite significantly higher heart rates. This effect translated into a significantly greater need for hemodynamic intervention. The effects of ZEN on arterial blood pressure warrant careful hemodynamic monitoring and preparedness to provide blood pressure support in dogs undergoing inhalant anesthesia.

papers.title: Rabies surveillance in the United States during 2024.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
papers.authors: Keshavamurthy R, Boutelle C, Bonaparte S, Gigante CM, Condori RE, Earnest R, Kirby JD, Nelson KM, Orciari LA, Ross Y, Wallace RM
papers.abstract: Describe the epidemiologic landscape of rabies and rabies testing in the US during 2024. Animal rabies testing results from approximately 130 public health, agriculture, and academic laboratories are collected by the US National Rabies Surveillance System (NRSS) each month. Data reported in 2024 were analyzed to examine temporal and geographic trends in animal rabies cases by rabies virus variant (RVV). In 2024, 3,834 cases of animal rabies were reported to the NRSS (4.2% of 90,343 samples submitted), representing a 2.0% increase from 2023. Of positive samples, 331 (8.6%) were domestic animals, and 3,503 (91.4%) were wildlife. The most commonly found rabid domestic animal was cats (243 positive [1.3% positivity]), and the most commonly found wildlife were bats (1,376 positive [5.7% positivity]) followed by raccoons (1,080 [10.1% positivity]). Two nonenzootic RVVs gained entry into the US in 2024. Four people died from rabies, including 2 who experienced bat exposures that were left untreated and 1 person whose case involved international travel. The expansion of the historical range of enzootic RVVs can lead to substantial public health and animal health burden. Domestically acquired human rabies cases in 2024 underscore the need for continual public education on the risks of rabies exposures to ensure timely and effective administration of postexposure prophylaxis. The internationally acquired human rabies case demonstrates that the US remains vulnerable to human and animal rabies importations. The NRSS plays a crucial role in protecting public and animal health by monitoring rabies trends in the US.

papers.title: Large language models demonstrate variable diagnostic performance and a systematic risk of undertriage in surgical triage of feline metacarpal and metatarsal fractures.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
papers.authors: Okur S, Özkalipçi Ç, Baykal B, Kartal T, Şenocak MG, Bedir AG, Yanmaz LE
papers.abstract: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of multiple large language models (LLMs) against expert consensus in determining surgical intervention needs for feline metacarpal and metatarsal fractures. In this retrospective study (December 2023 to February 2025), 73 clinical cases of feline metacarpal and metatarsal fractures were evaluated. Two board-certified veterinary orthopedic surgeons established a reference standard for surgical versus conservative management. Five LLMs (ChatGPT, version 5.2 [OpenAI Inc]; Gemini, version 3 Pro [Alphabet Inc]; Grok, version 4.1 [SpaceXAI]; Qwen, version 3.5 [Alibaba Cloud]; and Claude Sonnet, version 4.5 [Anthropic PBC]; and Claude Sonnet, version 4.5 [Anthropic PBC]) assessed anonymized case summaries using a standardized zero-shot prompt. Model recommendations were compared with the reference standard to calculate accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and the Cohen κ. The reference standard classified 49 cases (67.1%) as surgical and 24 (32.9%) as conservative. ChatGPT achieved the highest performance (accuracy, 84.9%; sensitivity, 79.6%; specificity, 95.8%; κ = 0.69). Other models showed lower performance; Qwen and Claude Sonnet failed to identify any surgical cases (0% sensitivity). A systematic bias toward conservative management was observed across all models, causing high false-negative rates (undertriage). LLMs demonstrate highly variable diagnostic performance and a systematic risk of undertriage in feline fracture assessment. While top-performing models approach expert-level agreement, others fail in critical clinical scenarios. Independent LLM use for surgical decision-making in feline orthopedics is not recommended due to undertriage risks. These tools require strict clinician oversight for preliminary triage.

papers.title: Medetomidine-vatinoxan (Zenalpha) results in reduction of systolic function, blood pressure, and heart rate with prolongation of electrocardiographic intervals in healthy dogs.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
papers.authors: Forsyth KK, Hogan DF, Dos Santos LFN, Weng HY
papers.abstract: To determine the effects of medetomidine-vatinoxan (Zenalpha; MVZ) on echocardiographic parameters, blood pressure, and cardiac rhythm in healthy dogs. Healthy, client-owned dogs were eligible for enrollment in this prospective, pretest/posttest study. Exclusion criteria included preexisting cardiac disease or medications that could alter the measured study parameters. Echocardiography, blood pressure, and 1-hour Holter monitor were performed at baseline and after sedation with MVZ per the manufacturer's guidelines. Multiple echocardiographic parameters, blood pressure, and arrhythmic burden score were assessed with pairwise comparisons between baseline and sedation. 21 dogs were enrolled in the study. Compared to baseline, MVZ resulted in significant reduction in multiple echocardiography-derived systolic function parameters (including ejection fraction, fractional shortening, end-systolic volume index, stroke volume index, and fractional area change), blood pressure, and heart rate, along with prolongation in PR and absolute QT intervals; there were nonsignificant increases in corrected QT interval and arrhythmic burden scores. Thirteen of 21 dogs (62%) developed or had worsening of atrioventricular nodal conduction on Holter monitor, while 2 of 21 (9.5%) developed or had worsening atrial or ventricular ectopic activity. Of all measured echocardiographic systolic function parameters, 15 of 21 dogs (71.4%) had 2 or more parameters below reference range with MVZ sedation. Sedation with MVZ resulted in significant changes to multiple cardiovascular and hemodynamic parameters. The cardiovascular effects of MVZ should be considered prior to sedation in dogs with, or being screened for, cardiovascular disease.

papers.title: Abnormal modified Insall-Salvati index values are associated with increased odds of medial meniscal tears in dogs with cranial cruciate ligament tears.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
papers.authors: Zayas JP, Steurer JA, Dixon BC, Newman RJ
papers.abstract: To evaluate the association between patellar height, as measured by the modified Insall-Salvati (IS) index, and medial meniscal tear in dogs with cranial cruciate ligament tears (CCLTs). Medical records from dogs treated for CCLT were reviewed. Preoperative patellar height was measured on mediolateral radiographs with the use of the modified IS index. Craniomedial stifle mini-arthrotomy documented the presence or absence of medial meniscal tears. Statistical analysis, adjusted to control for confounding variables, assessed whether abnormal IS index values were associated with meniscal injury. The study included 229 stifles. Abnormal modified IS index values were found in 12.6% (29 of 229) of stifles, of which 44.8% (13 of 29) had a concurrent medial meniscal tear. Among the dogs with a normal modified IS index (87.4% [200 of 229]), only 24.5% (49 of 200) had a concurrent medial meniscal tear. Dogs with an abnormal IS index had 3 times the odds of a medial meniscal tear (95% CI, 1.2 to 7.3) compared to those with a normal index. There was no statistically significant difference in the distribution between complete and partial CCLT between the normal IS index and abnormal IS index groups. Abnormal patellar height, as measured by the modified IS index, is significantly associated with increased risk of secondary medial meniscal tear in dogs with CCLT. Preoperative measurement of the modified IS index may help identify dogs at increased risk for meniscal tearing, supporting surgical planning and client communication.

papers.title: Ultrasonographic evaluation of the canine gracilis, semimembranosus, and semitendinosus muscles.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
papers.authors: Huguet E, Repac J
papers.abstract: To describe a practical technique for ultrasonographic evaluation of the gracilis, semimembranosus, and semitendinosus muscles in dogs. 2 clinically healthy client-owned German Shepherd Dogs were used for this tutorial. Owner consent and approval from the University of Florida College of Veterinary Medicine IACUC were obtained prior to participation. Dogs were clipped, sedated, and placed into dorsal recumbency in a relaxed position with bilateral coxofemoral abduction. A stepwise ultrasonographic approach was demonstrated with a high-frequency linear transducer. The image was optimized by adjustment of depth, focal zone placement, gain, and time-gain compensation. Scanning was performed in both transverse and longitudinal planes to assess muscle origin, body, and insertion. Normal anatomic relationships of the gracilis, semimembranosus, and semitendinosus muscles were identified to facilitate consistent evaluation. Ultrasound allowed clear identification of the gracilis, semimembranosus, and semitendinosus muscles on the basis of location, shape, echogenicity, and fiber orientation. The gracilis was identified in a transverse plane as a superficial, flat adductor muscle, with the semimembranosus located deeper and the semitendinosus positioned more caudally with a rounded contour. Standardized scanning planes enabled consistent visualization of muscle architecture and tendon attachments. Ultrasonography is a valuable, accessible tool for evaluating the gracilis, semimembranosus, and semitendinosus muscles in dogs. Familiarity with normal anatomy and scanning techniques is essential for the diagnosis of conditions such as fibrotic myopathy, facilitating earlier intervention.

papers.title: An anatomic plate provides successful outcomes for stabilization of periprosthetic femoral fractures and greater trochanteric osteotomies in dogs undergoing total hip replacement.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
papers.authors: Lotsikas PJ, Fink OT, Murphy S, Lirtzman RA, Kim SE, Lu M, Rochat M
papers.abstract: To report the clinical and radiographic outcomes of a locking proximal femoral anatomic bone plate in the management of periprosthetic femoral fractures (PFFs) and greater trochanteric osteotomies (GTOs) in dogs undergoing total hip replacement (THR). Medical records from August 2023 to February 2026 were reviewed for dogs with THR that developed PFF or underwent planned GTO and were subsequently stabilized with a locking proximal femoral anatomic bone plate. Cases involving a second plate, preexisting surgical site infection, or THR implant removal at the time of surgery were excluded. Eleven dogs were included-8 with PFF and 3 with GTO. The median age of dogs that sustained a femoral fracture was 7.5 years (range, 2 to 12.5 years). Three fractures occurred intraoperatively, and 5 occurred < 30 days postoperatively. The median age of dogs that underwent GTO was 2 years (range, 1 to 9 years). Of the 3 cases, 1 was a revision of a previously failed pin and tension-band repair of a GTO, and the other 2 were the primary repairs of the GTO. Radiographic bone healing and full function were achieved in all PFF cases. Two cases of GTO completely healed, and 1 was a delayed union but stable at12 weeks; all achieved full or acceptable function. One major complication occurred in the PFF group and was successfully revised with a larger plate. A locking proximal femoral anatomic bone plate provided adequate fixation and successful outcomes in dogs with PFF or elective GTO in dogs undergoing total hip replacement.

papers.title: Is annual Dirofilaria immitis antigen testing at preventive renewal proportionate to the residual infection risk in documented-compliant dogs?
