papers.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
papers.authors: Horvath M
papers.abstract: Current American Heartworm Society guidelines characterize prescribing macrocyclic lactone preventives in the absence of antigen testing as "NOT RECOMMENDED," regardless of compliance history or geographic prevalence. Number Needed to Screen, an established human preventive medicine framework applied here as a novel veterinary screening tool, has not previously been used to evaluate this guideline. Using county-level Companion Animal Parasite Council prevalence data and the compliance-gap distribution as a proxy, we derive geographically stratified Number Needed to Screen estimates varying approximately 25-fold across US states. A risk-stratified approach calibrated to local prevalence and compliance history merits prospective evaluation.

papers.title: Use of phenylephrine-soaked gauze following staphylectomy does not reduce the need for reintubation or temporary tracheostomy in brachycephalic dogs.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
papers.authors: Strain W, Reed RA, Grimes JA
papers.abstract: To determine whether application of phenylephrine-soaked gauze (PG) against the soft palate following staphylectomy reduces the incidence of reintubation and temporary tracheostomy. Electronic medical records for dogs that underwent staphylectomy from January 2023 through December 2024 were reviewed. Data collected included signalment, stage of laryngeal collapse, whether PG was used or not, and incidence of reintubation and temporary tracheostomy. Normally distributed data were analyzed with a Student t test; nonnormally distributed data were analyzed with a Wilcoxon test. Categorical data were analyzed with a Fisher exact test. 96 dogs were included (PG group, n = 56; no PG [NPG] group, 43). Dogs in the NPG group were more likely to have stage I versus stage II laryngeal collapse compared to those in the PG group. No other variables differed between groups. In the PG group, 19.6% (11 of 56) underwent reintubation and 7.1% (4 of 56) underwent temporary tracheostomy. In the NPG group, 22.5% (9 of 43) underwent reintubation and 5.0% (2 of 43) underwent temporary tracheostomy. There was no difference in reintubation or temporary tracheostomy between PG and NPG. The use of PG placed against the soft palate did not reduce reintubation or temporary tracheostomy rates among brachycephalic dogs undergoing staphylectomy. Veterinarians performing staphylectomy for brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome should not expect PG to reduce reintubation and temporary tracheostomy rates among patients; other methods to reduce soft palate swelling after staphylectomy should be evaluated.

papers.title: Teleneurology video recordings and live streams provide reliable neuroanatomic lesion localization in dogs and cats.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
papers.authors: Shinn R, Connolly B, Parker R, Togawa G, Rossmeisl J
papers.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the reliability and accuracy of teleneurology consultation for neuroanatomical lesion localization in client-owned dogs and cats. This prospective cross-sectional study was conducted from June to July 2023. Fifty-five client-owned dogs and cats presenting to an academic teaching hospital neurology service were enrolled. Animals were pragmatically allocated into 2 groups to undergo neurologic examination performed by veterinary students; group 1 underwent neurologic examination via prerecorded video, and group 2 was live streamed. A separate, in-person neurologic examination by a blinded board-certified neurologist or neurology resident served as the baseline assessment. The Cohen κ statistic was used to assess agreement between the neuroanatomical localization for each group. In total, 30 animals were evaluated in group 1 and 25 animals in group 2. Both teleneurology modalities demonstrated strong agreement with the in-person neuroanatomic localization. For group 1, κ was 0.84 (95% CI, 0.69 to 0.98). For group 2 (live stream), κ was 0.85 (95% CI, 0.66 to 1.00). Discrepancies in neuroanatomic localization were observed in 4 cases (13%) from group 1 and 3 (12%) from group 2. Teleneurology consultation shows promise as a reliable method for neuroanatomical localization in small animals. The observed high agreement suggested the potential utility of teleneurology consultation for nonemergent consultations, recheck appointments, and surgical follow-ups, particularly when a thorough examination with a dedicated videographer is ensured. Further standardization of protocols could enhance its widespread application.

papers.title: Retrospective evaluation of canine parvovirus monoclonal antibody supports faster clinical recovery in shelter dogs with naturally occurring canine parvovirus.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
papers.authors: Welton M, Hadden H, Herron M, Winston JA
papers.abstract: To retrospectively evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of the canine parvovirus monoclonal antibody (CPMA) administered with standardized supportive care for naturally occurring canine parvovirus (CPV) in a shelter setting. Electronic medical records from CPV-positive dogs treated at Gigi's Parvovirus Treatment Center between June 2020 and May 2024 were reviewed. All dogs received a standardized standard-of-care (SOC) algorithm. Dogs treated prior to August 2023 received SOC alone (n = 49), while those admitted thereafter received CPMA (0.2 mL/kg, IV) plus SOC (63). Primary outcomes were hospitalization duration, mortality, and time to isolation release criteria (2 consecutive negative CPV ELISA tests [SNAP; Idexx Laboratories Inc]). Secondary outcomes included modified clinical severity scores, medication scores, and total cost of care. Dogs receiving CPMA with SOC had significantly shorter hospitalization (median, 2 vs 4 days) and reached isolation release criteria sooner (median, 5 vs 6.5 days) compared with SOC alone. Mortality did not differ significantly (17% vs 22%). Maximum medication scores and overall cost of care were not statistically different, although CPMA-treated dogs showed a real-world median cost reduction of $978.50. One CPMA-treated dog experienced an anaphylactic reaction and recovered with supportive care. CPMA administration in combination with SOC accelerated clinical recovery and time to release from isolation compared with SOC alone. CPMA appears clinically effective and safe for naturally occurring CPV infections in a shelter environment. By reducing isolation time, CPMA may improve welfare, reduce behavioral risk associated with prolonged isolation and medical trauma, and support earlier adoption.

papers.title: A single-layer, full-thickness, simple continuous suture pattern is safe for hysterotomy closure in dogs undergoing cesarean section.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
papers.authors: Goldblatt BH, Burns JG, Marvel SJ
papers.abstract: To evaluate short-term complications for single-layer, full-thickness, simple continuous appositional closure (AC) of the uterus in dogs undergoing cesarean section (CS). Additional objectives included comparing the complication rates with dogs that underwent an inverting closure (IC) and reporting the litter size in dogs with subsequent pregnancies. A medical record review for dogs undergoing CS between May 2014 and February 2025 was performed at Colorado State University. Data retrieved included signalment, reason for CS, uterine closure pattern, anesthesia and surgery time, litter size, complications, and subsequent CSs. The study population included 77 dogs that underwent 89 CSs (70 AC, 19 IC). Postoperative complications were noted in 6 of 89 cases (6.7%). Closure pattern was not found to be a risk factor for development of postoperative complications. No dogs required intervention related to hysterotomy closure, and all dogs survived the 14-day follow-up period. One dog developed paralysis following epidural use at the time of CS. Twenty-four dogs had subsequent pregnancies: 19 of 24 (79.2%) after AC and 5 of 24 (20.8%) after IC. Full-thickness AC was not a significant risk factor for short-term postoperative complications. Both single- and double-layer, full-thickness hysterotomy closures were compatible with subsequent successful whelping and CSs. Single-layer, full-thickness, simple continuous appositional and double-layer full-thickness closures are safe for hysterotomy closure.

papers.title: Automated acute pain assessment in brachycephalic cats with ocular pain using the Feline Grimace Scale.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
papers.authors: Steagall PV, Li J, Marangoni S, Bukhari SSUH
papers.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility and limitations of an AI-powered Feline Grimace Scale (FGS) pipeline for acute pain assessment in brachycephalic cats with ocular pain. A total of 200 facial images of brachycephalic cats with ocular pain were used for model training and evaluation. A landmark localization model was used to predict facial landmarks. Pain prediction was performed with regression models from a machine-learning library (XGBoost; XGBoost Developers); 5 independent submodels were trained, each corresponding to 1 of the 5 FGS action units-ear position, orbital tightening, muzzle tension, whiskers change, and head position. Three configurations were applied to input variables: without muzzle tension and whiskers change, without whiskers change and head position, and all geometric descriptors retained. The landmark localization performance was assessed via normalized root mean square error (NRMSE), whereas pain prediction was assessed via mean absolute error, Pearson correlation, and R2 values. Facial landmark detection showed reduced accuracy in brachycephalic cats (NRMSE, 19.96%) compared with previous reports in predominantly mesocephalic cats (NRMSE, 16.76%). Pain prediction models demonstrated poor generalizability, showing the best results for without muzzle tension and whiskers change (mean absolute error, 0.168; R2, 0.115; Pearson correlation, 0.374). Automated landmark detection and pain prediction using an AI-powered FGS pipeline is possible in brachycephalic cats. However, cautious interpretation is needed due to limited annotated data, which precludes robust predictive performance estimates. Conformation-specific datasets are required before this AI-powered FGS pipeline can be used for pain assessment in brachycephalic cats.

papers.title: Development of a predictive model for estimation of postoperative risk following brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome surgery.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
papers.authors: Ruzics EA, Reynolds PS, Morse Z, Shipman J, Ham KM
papers.abstract: To identify risk factors for postoperative death and complications in dogs undergoing brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome (BOAS) surgery and utilize this information to develop a predictive model for risk estimation. Records of dogs undergoing BOAS surgery at a veterinary teaching hospital between 2012 and 2023 were reviewed. Predictor variables were categorized into domains, including signalment, history, clinical signs, underlying pathology, acuity status, and surgeries performed. Outcomes were categorized as death, major complications, or minor complications. The association between outcomes and predictors was modeled by logistic regression. Results were reported as ORs and regression coefficients with 95% CIs. A predictive model was created to estimate risk of mortality and complications following BOAS surgery. 297 cases were included. Twelve dogs (4%) died prior to discharge. Major complications (airway interventions and pneumonia) were reported for 29 dogs (10%). Major complications were strongly associated with emergent presentation (OR, 7.45; 95% CI, 2.70 to 20.59), female sex (OR, 2.78; 95% CI, 1.11 to 6.67), high-grade laryngeal collapse (OR, 4.28; 95% CI, 1.56 to 11.79), and history of regurgitation/vomiting (OR, 2.16; 95% CI, 0.87 to 5.38). Risk factors for postoperative death and complications were identified. A predictive model was developed, allowing estimation of postoperative risk based on individual patient factors. A multivariable predictive model may be useful in clinical practice to obtain individualized postoperative risk predictions to contribute to prognostication, decision-making, and triage. However, as this model has not been externally validated, calculated risk should be utilized with caution and consideration for the clinical picture of each patient.

papers.title: Pretreatment with phenoxybenzamine improves short-term survival and hemodynamic stability in dogs undergoing adrenalectomy for pheochromocytoma.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
papers.authors: Wund Z, Monnet E
papers.abstract: To evaluate indices of hemodynamic instability (HDI) in dogs and evaluate the effects of phenoxybenzamine (PBZ) on HDI and short-term survival in dogs undergoing adrenalectomy for pheochromocytoma. A retrospective medical record review of all dogs that underwent adrenalectomy at a single institution between 1996 and 2024. Dogs were included if the mass was confirmed to be a pheochromocytoma on histopathology and excluded if they received α antagonists other than PBZ, had incomplete medical or anesthetic records, or were treated with laparoscopy. 52 dogs met the inclusion criteria. Thirty-five dogs that did not receive PBZ were entered in the NPBZ group, and 17 that received PBZ were entered in the PBZ group. The mean dosage of PBZ was 1.1 mg/kg/d (0.4 to 1.7 mg/kg/d) administered for a mean length of time of 13.4 days (9.3 to 17.4 days) before surgery. Indices of HDI including systolic blood pressure > 200 mm Hg seemed to be more appropriate for dogs with pheochromocytoma. Six of the 22 dogs in the NPBZ group that required cavotomy experienced HDI compared to 0 of 17 in the PBZ group. The 14-day survival rate was 94.1% in the PBZ group and 62.9% in the NPBZ group. Pharmacologic α-adrenergic blockade with PBZ prior to adrenalectomy improved short-term patient survival. Indices of HDI that include systolic arterial pressure above 200 mm Hg seem to be more appropriate for dogs. PBZ should be considered as an effective pretreatment strategy to reduce the effects of HDI during adrenalectomy in dogs undergoing adrenalectomy for pheochromocytoma.

papers.title: Serological response to extralabel use of parenteral rabies vaccines in 28 mammalian species.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
papers.authors: Wallace RM, Müller T, Freuling C, Seetahal JFR, Slavinski S, Brown C
papers.abstract: To evaluate immunogenicity, persistence of antibodies, survival after challenge, and anamnestic response following extralabel parenteral rabies vaccination across mammalian species compared with benchmarks from on-label canine vaccination. Mammals described in published studies of extralabel parenteral rabies vaccination. A structured literature review (1980 to 2025) identified studies reporting serologic or challenge outcomes after extralabel parenteral rabies vaccination. Extracted data included taxonomic family; vaccine type and schedule, timing of serum collection, antibody titers, survival after experimental challenge, and response to booster vaccination. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted by family and overall. Pooled proportions were compared with the World Organisation for Animal Health benchmark of 88% survival and with canine benchmarks for primary seroconversion (88.1%), antibody levels 6 to 12 months after primary vaccination (72.9%), and booster response (96.8%). 32 articles describing 41 studies met inclusion criteria, representing 2,630 animals from 28 species in 17 families. After primary vaccination, 84.4 ± 4.1% achieved titers ≥ 0.5 IU/mL, with 14 of 16 families noninferior to the canine benchmark. At ≥ 6 months, 63.7 ± 10.6% maintained titers ≥ 0.5 IU/mL. Among 79 vaccinated animals challenged with rabies virus, 89.0 ± 9.8% survived. Booster vaccination produced adequate titers in 89.1 ± 8.0% of 275 animals, with reduced responses in the families Elephantidae and Ursidae. Modern-day rabies vaccines generate strong antibody responses across diverse mammalian families, with nondomestic canids responding similarly to domestic dogs. These findings support recognizing extralabel vaccination as biologically protective and can inform public health and animal management policies.

papers.title: Ethanol ablation guided by sonographic appearance of the nodule is effective for treatment of primary hyperparathyroidism in dogs.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
papers.authors: Schindler S, Lane M, Woodard M, Baron-Chapman M
papers.abstract: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of a modified percutaneous ultrasound-guided ethanol ablation technique for the treatment of primary hyperparathyroidism in dogs. This prospective observational study was conducted at a single veterinary referral center. Dogs with persistent ionized hypercalcemia, normal/increased parathyroid hormone concentrations, normal/undetectable parathyroid hormone-related protein concentrations, and ultrasonographic identification of ≥ 1 presumed hyperfunctioning parathyroid nodule (≥ 2.5 mm) underwent percutaneous ultrasonographically guided ethanol ablation, in which ethanol was administered until real-time diffuse intralesional hyperechogenicity was achieved. Dogs with alternative causes of hypercalcemia were excluded. Data collected from October 2018 through April 2023 included signalment, lesion characteristics, ethanol volume administered, complications, and biochemical outcomes. Resolution of hypercalcemia following ablation was the primary outcome measure. 49 dogs were enrolled, and follow-up data were available for 47. Hypercalcemia resolved in 42 of 47 dogs (89.4%). Complications occurred in 12 of 47 dogs (25.5%) and were classified as minor in 10 and major in 2. Dogs with resolution of hypercalcemia received a greater median volume of ethanol than dogs without resolution (0.60 mL [IQR, 0.30 to 1.00 mL] vs 0.15 mL [IQR, 0.09 to 0.37 mL]; P = .012). Ethanol volume was not associated with ethanol leakage severity or complication rates. Sonographically guided ethanol ablation was an effective treatment for primary hyperparathyroidism in dogs, achieving resolution of hypercalcemia in nearly 90% of cases with a low rate of major complications. Ultrasound-guided ethanol ablation based on real-time nodule hyperechogenicity may be a practical alternative to volume-based protocols while maintaining efficacy and safety.

papers.title: Cardiac etiology is the leading cause of feline chylothorax: 35 cases (2006-2022).
papers.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
papers.authors: Severac L, Juette T, Conversy B
papers.abstract: To identify the most frequent underlying causes of chylothorax in cats and to assess whether clinical and laboratory findings at presentation could predict etiology and outcome. Cats diagnosed with chylothorax were retrospectively enrolled in 2 veterinary centers between 2006 and 2022. Data collected for each case included signalment, history, physical examination findings, pleural effusion analysis, hematologic and imaging results, etiology, treatment (medical and/or surgical), and survival time. Descriptive statistics and multinomial logistic regression were used to identify markers of etiology. Associations with survival were assessed with the Cox proportional hazards models. 35 cats met the inclusion criteria. Cardiac disease was the most common etiology (57%), followed by idiopathic (31%), neoplasia (9%), and peritoneopericardial diaphragmatic hernia (3%). Cats with neoplastic chylothorax were significantly older than those in other etiologic groups. Cats with cardiac chylothorax had a higher left atrial-to-aortic ratio (median, 2.4) than cats in other etiologic groups (< 1.4). Median survival times for cardiac, idiopathic, neoplastic, and peritoneopericardial diaphragmatic hernia etiology were 172, 416, 38, and 27 days, respectively. Regardless of the chylothorax etiology, survival was negatively correlated to older cats and low rectal temperature on initial arrival to the hospital. Cardiac disease was the predominant cause of chylothorax. All cats with a left atrial-to-aortic ratio > 1.4 had a cardiac etiology. All cats aged over 14 years had a neoplastic etiology. Felines with a cardiac etiology had a poorer prognosis than idiopathic cases. Neoplastic cats had the shortest survival time. An echocardiogram should be considered for all cats diagnosed with chylothorax.

papers.title: Measurement of abdominal fluid bilirubin concentration frequently fails to detect biliary tract rupture in dogs with gallbladder mucocele.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
papers.authors: Aicher KM, Gookin JL, Mathews KG, Stowe DM
papers.abstract: To evaluate the diagnostic utility of abdominal fluid bilirubin concentration-to-serum bilirubin concentration ratio (AFB:SB) measurement in detecting biliary tract rupture or leakage in dogs with gallbladder mucocele (GBM; GBM group) versus no GBM (non-GBM group). For this retrospective cross-sectional study, a search of medical records identified dogs with concurrent measurements of abdominal fluid bilirubin and serum bilirubin concentrations prior to surgery or postmortem examination for biliary tract rupture or leakage between July 1, 2007, and January 31, 2022. Results for AFB:SB and other variables of interest were compared between the GBM versus non-GBM group and those with versus without biliary tract rupture or leakage. 29 dogs were included (GBM group, n = 12; non-GBM, n = 17). Eleven GBM dogs and 7 non-GBM dogs had biliary tract rupture or leakage. The AFB:SB was > 2 for 2 of 11 (18%) GBM dogs with rupture, 6 of 7 (86%) non-GBM dogs with biliary tract rupture or leakage, and 2 non-GBM dogs without identified rupture/leakage. Abdominal fluid cytology confirmed the presence of bile in all dogs with a ruptured GBM. The use of AFB:SB alone frequently fails to detect biliary tract rupture or leakage in dogs with GBM; however, cytological analysis of abdominal fluid is valuable in helping to detect potential GBM rupture. It is essential that primary care and emergency veterinarians be aware that an AFB:SB > 2 can be indicative of biliary tract rupture or leakage in dogs; however, the ratio may not be > 2 in dogs with ruptured GBM.

papers.title: Respiratory distress in a newly diagnosed diabetic cat.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
papers.authors: Biedak N, Mahony O, Rozanski E, Remolina P R, McCobb E

papers.title: Biological response stability of refrigerated cosacthen after opening and non-hormonal effects of ACTH stimulation testing in healthy dogs.
papers.authors: de Oliveira MC, Nogueira TB, Gouvêa FL, Oliveira JM, Trevizan L, Pöppl ÁG
papers.abstract: The adrenocorticotropic hormone stimulation test (ACTHST) is widely used to evaluate adrenal reserve in dogs. This study assessed the effects of refrigerated storage of tetracosactide (Cosacthen) after opening for up to three weeks and investigated hematological, biochemical, and electrolyte changes following ACTH stimulation. Ten healthy beagle dogs (five males and five females) were enrolled. Each dog received tetracosactide (5 μg/kg, IV) at vial opening (T0) and at 7-day intervals over 3 weeks (T1 to T3), using aliquots from the same vial stored at 2-8°C. Blood samples were collected before and 1 hour after ACTH administration to measure cortisol, hematology, biochemistry, and electrolytes. Clinical monitoring was performed after each test. Cortisol concentrations increased significantly after ACTH administration at all time points (T0-T3). Delta-cortisol was higher at T1 than at T0 (P = 0.0104) and lower at T2 than at T1 (P = 0.0059), with no differences among T0, T2, and T3. After ACTH administration, red blood cell count, hematocrit, hemoglobin, albumin, alkaline phosphatase, triglycerides, cholesterol, potassium, and total calcium decreased significantly, whereas glucose increased. All values remained within reference intervals, and no adverse effects were observed. Refrigerated storage of Cosacthen after opening did not alter cortisol responses. Post-ACTH changes in laboratory variables should be considered when interpreting results.

papers.title: Polarization Sensitive Optical Coherence Tomography for Surgical Margin Assessment for Canine Soft Tissue Sarcoma.
papers.authors: Patel N, Fontes G, Dornbusch J, Biggo M, Erickson A, Jurcak N, Mignucci JS, Shen YF, Weaver H, Jennings R, Selmic LE
papers.abstract: Soft tissue sarcomas (STSs) and skeletal muscle both appear high scattering on spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) imaging, which resulted in instances of misclassification by observers in prior soft tissue sarcoma margin assessment studies. Polarization-sensitive optical coherence tomography (PS-OCT) is an extension of OCT that provides additional information about tissue polarization contrast. In this prospective study we wanted to evaluate whether PS-OCT improves tissue differentiation and diagnostic accuracy compared to spectral-domain OCT (SD-OCT) alone. PS-OCT images from surgical margins of 10 resected STS were compared with histopathology to identify characteristic features of normal and neoplastic tissues. Then, six observers of varying OCT image interpretation experience assessed surgical margins from 30 resected STS using SD-OCT alone and SD-OCT combined with PS-OCT. PS-OCT images demonstrated distinct birefringence (optical patterns), corresponding to tissue organization: skeletal muscle exhibited alternating high and low birefringence bands, fascia showed variable birefringence and STS had uniformly low birefringence. Overall diagnostic accuracy was high for both modalities [correct classification rate: SD-OCT alone 93.7% (95% confidence interval (CI): 90.1, 96.0) vs. SD-OCT combined with PS-OCT 92.6% (95% = CI: 89.3, 95.4)]; adding PS-OCT did not significantly improve accuracy across all observers (p = 0.82), though expert observers benefited significantly (p = 0.0018). Interobserver and intraobserver agreement ranged from substantial to near perfect. These findings suggest PS-OCT can be interpreted reliably after brief training and may enhance accuracy for experienced users. Further research should explore structured training and real-time applications for comprehensive surgical margin evaluation.

papers.title: Clinical Characteristics of Hair Cycle Arrest in Toy Poodles: A Retrospective Comparison With Pomeranians.
papers.authors: Ueyama A, Amatuji H, Iyori K, Hsiao YH
papers.abstract: Hair cycle arrest (HCA), known as alopecia X, is an alopecia disorder most commonly reported in Nordic breeds-particularly Pomeranians. Toy poodles (TPs) also are frequently affected, yet their clinical characteristics have not been reviewed systematically. The aim of this retrospective case series was to compare the clinical characteristics of HCA in TPs and Pomeranians. Medical records of client-owned dogs diagnosed with HCA between 2018 and 2024 were reviewed. Signalment, including age of onset and age at diagnosis, clinical features, skin barrier function (transepidermal water loss [TEWL], stratum corneum hydration [SCH]) and treatment outcomes were analysed. Fifty dogs (19 TPs, 31 Pomeranians) met the inclusion criteria. TPs were significantly older than Pomeranians both at disease onset and at the first presentation (p = 0.003 and p = 0.001, respectively). Both breeds exhibited similar bilateral symmetrical alopecia presentations; however, Pomeranians mainly presented with a single alopecic site, while nearly half of the TPs had multiple affected sites (p = 0.032). Pruritus and superficial pyoderma were common in both breeds. TEWL and SCH values frequently deviated from reference ranges (increased TEWL and decreased SCH), indicating impaired skin barrier function. TEWL was significantly higher in TPs with pyoderma than in those without (p = 0.025). Regarding outcomes, > 70% of patients showed partial or complete regrowth, despite various treatment regimens. HCA in TPs closely resembles that in Pomeranians, despite genetic divergence, suggesting a conserved pathogenesis across their breeds. Frequent pruritus and pyoderma, together with abnormal TEWL and SCH, indicate secondary skin barrier dysfunction. Clinical management should address both hair regrowth and restoration of skin barrier function.

papers.title: Letter regarding "ACVIM-endorsed statement: consensus statement and systematic review on guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of chronic inflammatory enteropathy in dogs".
papers.authors: Jablonski SA, Tolbert MK

papers.title: Case Report: Ventriculoperitoneal shunt for management of syringomyelia and Chiari-like malformation in a Cavalier King Charles Spaniel.
papers.authors: Fernandez Cid A, Tabanez J, Black C, Rusbridge C
papers.abstract: A 1-year-old male Cavalier King Charles Spaniel (CKCS) was presented with spinal hyperesthesia, reluctance to exercise, and phantom scratching. MRI revealed a Chiari-like malformation (CM) with brachycephaly, cerebellar herniation, ventriculomegaly, and syringomyelia extending from the odontoid peg to L5, with a maximum transverse syrinx width of 7.0 mm at C2-C3. Medical management (meloxicam and gabapentin) failed to resolve clinical signs. Due to significantly increased lateral ventricles and concern for syrinx progression, a ventriculoperitoneal shunt was placed. Aside from transient post-operative pneumocephalus, the procedure was successful. The dog showed significant clinical improvement, and follow-up MRI demonstrated syrinx reduction and resolution of lateral ventricles. At 6 months post-op, the syrinx measured 2.3 mm. Eight months after the surgery, the dog experienced a brief episode of a suspected movement disorder like but recovered fully. The patient remains pain-free and neurologically normal. This case describes the clinical and imaging outcomes of ventriculoperitoneal shunting (VPS) in a dog with Chiari-like malformation, syringomyelia, and ventriculomegaly.

papers.title: Effects of pregabalin added to a multimodal anesthetic protocol in cats undergoing ovariohysterectomy.
papers.authors: Romano M, Hernández-Avalos I, Nanci C, Costa S, Lombardo A, Di Pietro S, Spadola F, Interlandi C
papers.abstract: Advancement in anesthetic protocols is necessary to address the evolving challenges of perioperative cats' management in veterinary practice. In this study, 54 cats were enrolled and were randomly assigned to either Group P (Pregabalin, PGB) or Group C (Control). Group P received 5 mg/kg of PGB orally 90 min before hospital admission, while Group C received identical empty capsules. Sedation was assessed using a Feline Multiparametric Sedation Scale and a Simple Qualitative Scale. All cats were premedicated with methadone (0.2 mg/kg IM) and alfaxalone (1 mg/kg IM). Anesthesia was induced with propofol at 2 mg/kg and maintained with isoflurane. Physiological parameters (HR, RR, SpO2, EtCO2, Blood Pressure, and Temperature) were monitored throughout surgery. In the immediate postoperative period, the Glasgow Feline Composite Measure Pain Scale short-form and the Feline Grimace Scale were used, measured at 0, 15, 30, and 60 min after extubation. Statistical analysis included Two-way ANOVA for physiological data and Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney tests for pain and sedation scores. Sedation scores increased in Group P by 2.46 (95% CI: 1.69 to 3.23; p  < 0.001). Conversely, the scores of the scales used in the immediate postoperative period were significantly lower in the Group P at all evaluation times -2.15 (95% CI: -2.92 to -1.39; p  < 0.001). No significant differences were observed in physiological parameters. In conclusion, prehospital administration of PGB provides effective sedation and improves postoperative comfort, making it a valuable adjunct to feline anesthesia protocols.

papers.title: Assessment of the hepatoprotective effect of a multi-component preparation containing phospholipids, selected amino acids, betaine, and milk thistle extract in dogs with asymptomatic elevation of liver parameters: a pilot study.
papers.authors: Nieradka R, Jank M, Otto S, Kurosad A
papers.abstract: Liver diseases in dogs are often diagnosed at advanced stages due to the organ's high functional reserve. Early supportive therapy with hepatoprotective nutraceuticals may help slow disease progression in dogs with asymptomatic elevation of liver parameters. The aim of this pilot study was to evaluate the hepatoprotective effect of a multi-component preparation containing phospholipids, selected amino acids, betaine, and milk thistle extract in client-owned dogs with asymptomatic elevation of liver parameters. Seventeen dogs were included in the open-label study. The animals received Hepatiale Forte Advanced (Vet Expert) for 8 weeks at the manufacturer's recommended dose. Liver enzyme activities (ALT, AST, ALP, GGT), total bilirubin, serum bile acids, hematological parameters, and abdominal ultrasonography were assessed at baseline and after 8 weeks. Supplementation resulted in statistically significant reductions in ALT ( p  = 0.004), AST ( p  = 0.004), ALP ( p  = 0.001), total bilirubin ( p  = 0.001) and serum bile acids ( p  = 0.007). A trend toward a decrease was observed for GGT ( p  = 0.052). Hematological parameters remained stable, and the preparation was well tolerated with no adverse effects reported. Ultrasonographic findings were mostly stable or improved (resolution of biliary sludge in some cases). Eight-week supplementation with the multi-component hepatoprotective preparation was associated with significant improvement in liver biochemical parameters in dogs with asymptomatic elevation of liver parameters. The results support further research in a randomized, placebo-controlled trial.

papers.title: Case Report: Epitheliotropic cutaneous presentation of multicentric diffuse large B-cell lymphoma in a dog.
papers.authors: Kim GH, Ko BG, Kim SH, Seo KW, Youn HY, Ryu MO
papers.abstract: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is the most common histological subtype of canine multicentric lymphoma, whereas epitheliotropism is classically associated with cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. A 9-year-old neutered male Chihuahua was diagnosed with stage IVb multicentric lymphoma and achieved complete remission with a UW-25 L-CHOP protocol. However, an upper lip mass, cytologically consistent with lymphoma, developed during remission. Electrochemotherapy was performed for local control and resulted in marked reduction of the lesion. The dog later developed recurrent peripheral lymphadenopathy and multiple progressive cutaneous masses despite various chemotherapy protocols and was euthanized at week 59 because of progressive clinical deterioration. Histopathology confirmed diffuse large cell lymphoma in the submandibular lymph node, whereas the cutaneous lesions showed neoplastic lymphoid infiltration with multifocal epidermal invasion, mimicking epitheliotropic T-cell lymphoma. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) confirmed diffuse CD20 expression in both sites, with CD3 labeling limited to scattered background lymphocytes. These findings supported the interpretation of secondary cutaneous involvement of DLBCL with a highly unusual epitheliotropic pattern and emphasize the importance of IHC for accurate immunophenotypic classification of cutaneous lymphoma lesions.

papers.title: A New Application of 64 CuCl 2 PET/CT: Imaging of Cats With Mammary Carcinoma.
papers.authors: Yang VA, Lunceford JM, Garrett C, Lattimer JC, Papageorgiou C, Smith CJ, Maitz CA, Bryan JN, Talbott JL, Lewis MR
papers.abstract: Feline mammary carcinoma (FMC) is an aggressive and highly metastatic cancer that shares molecular and clinical characteristics with human triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), making it a relevant comparative model for a disease lacking targeted therapies. This study investigated the feasibility and clinical utility of 64 CuCl 2 PET/CT imaging in cats with naturally occurring mammary carcinoma. Eight cats (seven tumour-bearing, one healthy control) were administered an intravenous dose of 64 CuCl 2 and underwent whole-body PET/CT imaging. Semi-quantitative analysis was performed using standardized uptake values (SUVs), and tumour-to-muscle ratios were calculated to assess lesion conspicuity. Serum ceruloplasmin concentrations were measured as a marker of systemic copper metabolism. All primary masses were 64 Cu-avid and conspicuous, with consistently elevated tumour-to-muscle ratios across tumour-bearing cats, allowing clear differentiation between neoplastic and normal tissue. Imaging provided additional staging information by identifying locally invasive and metastatic disease that was not fully evident on physical examination. Physiologic tracer distribution was characterized by high uptake in the liver and gallbladder and low uptake in skeletal muscle, which served as a reliable reference tissue. Serum ceruloplasmin concentrations varied widely and did not correlate with tumour uptake. These findings suggest that 64 CuCl 2 PET/CT is a feasible functional imaging modality for FMC, potentially aiding in tumour detection. This was an exploratory study, and not all imaging results could be confirmed by cytology or histopathology. Nonetheless, our findings suggest that 64 CuCl 2 PET/CT should be investigated further as a method for probing copper utilization in FMC.

papers.title: Prevalence of antibiotic use in dogs and cats in US and Canadian veterinary teaching hospitals, 2022.
papers.authors: Clark H, Bollig ER, Beaudoin AL, Fellman CL, Allano M, Atiee GF, Blois SL, Blong AE, Brookshire WC, Burgess BA, Cohen AJ, Cohn LA, Cole SD, Collier AJ, Curran KM, DeMars P, Droog M, Forbes JM, Fox D, Frey E, Gochenauer A, Guptill L, Hartley AN, Johnston AN, King CA, KuKanich K, LeCuyer TE, Letendre JA, Menard J, Meyers K, Paul L, Perkins AV, Redding L, Santoro D, Stein MR, Sykes JE, Carr SV, Viviano K, Daniels JB, Granick JL
papers.abstract: Evaluation of current antimicrobial prescribing practices can inform antimicrobial stewardship efforts. Our primary objective was to describe current antibiotic prescribing practice in veterinary schools. Medical records from 1800 animals (1403 dogs, 397 cats) at 31 US and Canadian veterinary schools were included. Hospitals collected data from medical records of animals evaluated on a single date in August 2022. Data included patient signalment, hospitalization status, clinical condition(s), diagnostic testing, antibiotics prescribed, route of administration, evidence of infection, and intended use. Overall, 30.4% (95% CI, 28.3%-32.6%) of animals (32.0% of dogs, 24.9% of cats) were prescribed an antibiotic. The most common conditions for which antibiotics were prescribed were surgical (27.3%, 191/699), urinary (11.9%, 83/699), and respiratory (11.6%, 81/699). The most prescribed classes of antibiotics included aminopenicillins with beta-lactamase inhibitors, first-generation cephalosporins, and fluoroquinolones. First-line antibiotics were not prescribed for sporadic bacterial cystitis. For all prescriptions intended for the treatment of infection, the median duration was 10 days, whereas for those intended for prophylaxis, the median duration was 7 days. Opportunities for antimicrobial stewardship in veterinary schools include guidance for use of fluoroquinolones, decreased usage of antibiotics for surgical prophylaxis, and prioritization of first-line antibiotics for sporadic bacterial cystitis. Tracking of antibiotic use data is important to benchmark prescribing and track progress.

papers.title: Idiopathic facial neuropathy in cats: clinical presentation, magnetic resonance imaging findings, and outcome.
papers.authors: Stefaniuk M, Danciu CG, Muñiz Moris L, Ricco C, De Decker S, Brocal J, Alcoverro E, Marsh O, Taylor-Brown F, Mari L
papers.abstract: Idiopathic facial neuropathy (IFN) is commonly described in dogs, but information in cats is lacking. Describe clinical presentation, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings and outcome in cats diagnosed with IFN. Thirteen cats with presumptive diagnosis of IFN. Multicenter retrospective descriptive study with questionnaire-based follow-up. Magnetic resonance imaging was assessed by a single author blinded to clinical signs. Median age was 30 months (range, 6-142). Median time of onset to presentation was 6 days (range, 1-150). Facial paresis or paralysis was unilateral in 10 cases and bilateral in 3 (16 sides affected). Clinical signs included absent (11/16) or decreased (2/16) palpebral reflex; lip ptosis (5/16); absent or decreased ear movements (3/6 reported). Eight cats had vestibular signs, including head tilt (6/13), vestibular ataxia (6/13), head swaying (2/13), and horizontal nystagmus (3/13). Findings on MRI included thickened (4/16), or contrast-enhancing (7/16) facial nerve or both and smaller caudal belly of the digastricus muscle (9/16). Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) was normal in 10 of 11 cats. Treatments included eye lubrication (11/13) and anti-inflammatory doses of prednisolone (3/13). Follow-up was available for 9 of 13 cats (median, 13 months; range, 2-91). Median time to maximal recovery was 20 weeks (range, 2-24). Recovery of spontaneous blinking was complete in 7 out of 12 eyes, partial in 2 out of 12 and absent in 3 out of 12. Three cats had persistent abnormalities of the lips, face, ears or some combination of these. All vestibular signs resolved but one cat was euthanized because of relapse. Idiopathic facial neuropathy appears to affect mostly young cats, often unilaterally and frequently with vestibular signs. Spontaneous improvement is likely, but persistent neurologic deficits are possible.

papers.title: Point-of-care troponin I assay has acceptable performance detecting clinically important canine myocardial injury but reduced precision at low concentrations.
papers.authors: Ditzler B, Saunders AB, Wesselowski S, Guadiano P, Dunham JW, Lidbury JA
papers.abstract: To perform a partial validation of a point-of-care assay (Vcheck cardiac troponin I [VC-cTnI; cTnI]) for measurement of cTnI in canine serum and to perform a method comparison between the VC-cTnI and an established chemiluminescent assay (ADVIA Centaur XP High-Sensitivity Troponin I [AC-cTnI-HS]). From September 4, 2024, through August 21, 2025, surplus canine serum was collected from a diagnostic laboratory, and within-day variability, dilutional parallelism, spiking recovery, and the effect of common interferents (hemolysis, icterus, and lipemia) were analyzed for the VC-cTnI assay. A method comparison of the VC-cTnI and AC-cTnI-HS assays was performed with 121 canine serum samples. The within-day coefficient of variation ranged from 8.1% to 43.8%, decreasing as cTnI concentrations increased. Dilutional parallelism and spiking recovery assessments had mean ± SD observed-to-expected ratios of 80.5 ± 33.2% (range, 21.1% to 122.2%) and 112.8 ± 35.6% (range, 46.0% to 173.9%), respectively. There was no interference from icterus, hemolysis, or lipemia. There was a positive correlation between the VC-cTnI and AC-cTnI-HS assays (Spearman ρ, 0.742), though 16 of 121 samples (13.2%) were below the VC-cTnI detectable limit. The VC-cTnI assay lacked precision for measurement of concentrations below 0.2 ng/mL, but within-day variability was acceptable for higher concentrations. The VC-cTnI assay is more precise when measuring higher cTnI concentrations and can detect myocardial injury in dogs. Results in the normal and equivocal range of the manufacturer's reference interval may be more challenging to interpret because of suboptimal precision in this range.

papers.title: Case Report: Therapeutic plasma exchange for systemic centipede envenomation in a 2-kg Chihuahua dog.
papers.authors: Tang W, Li Y, Sun G, Zheng C, Gao Z, Li S
papers.abstract: A 2-kg, 8-year-old neutered male Chihuahua was presented after a centipede sting to the interdigital region of the right forepaw, followed by lameness and red urine. Wound care and intravenous fluid therapy were provided at the referring clinic; however, pigmenturia persisted and systemic manifestations developed, prompting referral. On admission, the dog had icteric mucous membranes, mild dehydration, and clinicopathologic evidence of systemic inflammation, tissue injury, hepatocellular damage, and suspected hemolysis. Because of the acute systemic manifestations following envenomation and persistence of clinical abnormalities despite initial medical management, membrane-based therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) was performed. Estimated plasma volume was 96 mL, and the prescribed exchange volume was 134 mL (1.4 plasma volumes). Approximately 1,080 mL of whole blood was processed over 3 h. The 68-mL extracorporeal circuit was primed with whole blood, anticoagulation was achieved with heparin, and fresh frozen canine plasma was used as the replacement fluid. TPE was completed over 3 h at a whole blood flow rate of 6 mL/min; transient asymptomatic ionized hypocalcemia was detected and treated with calcium gluconate. After treatment, C-reactive protein decreased from 8.9 to 1.5 mg/dL and appetite returned, although depression initially persisted. The dog subsequently improved during hospitalization and was discharged after 7 days. In this dog, membrane-based TPE was well tolerated despite the small body size and was temporally associated with improvement in clinical signs.

papers.title: Animal welfare assessment at four dog shelters in Central Uganda: a cross-sectional study using the shelter quality ® protocol.
papers.authors: Ashabahebwa L, Hoareau Z, Ssuna P, Tayebwa DS
papers.abstract: In Central Uganda, animal welfare advocates are increasingly promoting the establishment of animal shelters as a humane alternative to poisoning for controlling free-roaming dog (FRD) populations. However, dogs at these facilities face a number of welfare challenges arising from insufficient resources and substandard management practices. We aimed to assess the welfare of sheltered dogs in Central Uganda by identifying the animal-based welfare issues faced by the dogs, evaluating the housing and management infrastructure, and determining risk factors of animal welfare compromise. We conducted a cross-sectional study in four animal shelters, between July and August 2024. We used structured checklists from the Shelter Quality ® protocol (SQP) to collect data on animal-based measures (ABMs), resource-based measures (RBMs) and management-based measures (MBMs). Overall, the shelters housed 141 dogs (average 35.3, range 4-84) across 40 pens (average 10, range 2-17). A total sample of 32 pens were selected from which 81 dogs were assessed. Fifty-seven of the dogs were housed in groups, fourteen in pairs, and ten were housed individually. Thirty five dogs were females and 46 males. Thirty two dogs were juveniles, 41 were adults and 8 were geriatrics. The most prevalent ABMs were; 'too thin' body condition, skin lesions and fear/aggression, reported among 59.3%, 45.7% and 39.1% of the dogs respectively. At pen-level, signs of diarrhea, pain-associated behavior, and stereotypies were commonly seen in 46.9%, 56.3%, and 46.9% of the pens respectively. Multivariable firth's logistic regression revealed several risk factors of poor welfare outcomes; Skin conditions, especially wounds were significantly associated with the'other' bedding type (aOR = 5.27, p = 0.008). Panting was highly associated with poorly ventilated pens (aOR = 82.33, p = 0.010). Pain-related behaviors in dogs were significantly linked to group housing (aOR = 11.92, p = 0.006), while a lack of outdoor access was a risk factor for stereotypic behaviors (aOR = 20.71, p = < 0.001). Our findings indicate that the welfare of the majority of shelter dogs was suboptimal, largely due to inadequate resources, poor housing conditions, and questionable management practices. Improving dog welfare in Ugandan shelters requires regulating intakes and implementing evidence-based management interventions. Collaboration with veterinary providers and intervention from animal protection agencies or government bodies can ensure sustainable, high-welfare operations.

papers.title: Myoclonus as a neurologic manifestation of hypoglycemia in dogs.
papers.authors: Polidoro D, Liatis T, Álvarez P, Bhatti SFM
papers.abstract: Myoclonus consists of brief, shock-like jerks and is not reported in dogs as a neurological manifestation of hypoglycemia. To describe hypoglycemia-associated myoclonus in dogs and report diagnostic findings, treatment, and outcome. Ten dogs presenting myoclonus and concurrent hypoglycemia. Multicenter, retrospective study of dogs presenting hypoglycemia-related myoclonus. All dogs presented with myoclonus. Neurological examination was abnormal in 5/10 (50%). Myoclonus was generalized in 8/10 (80%) dogs and focal (head) in 2/10 (20%), with progression to generalized tonic-clonic epileptic seizures in 5/10 (50%). Hypoglycemia (<3.3 mmol/L) was observed in all dogs (median, 2.07 mmol/L) during the myoclonic episodes. Insulinoma was a suspected (n = 1), presumptive (n = 5), or definitive (n = 3) diagnosis in 9/10 (90%) dogs. One dog (10%) developed iatrogenic hypoglycemia after IV administration of fast-acting human insulin and myoclonic episodes resolved after dose reduction. Among dogs with suspected, presumptive or confirmed insulinoma, 5/9 (56%) received medical treatment alone, 3/9 (33%) combined medical and surgical treatment, and 1/9 (11%) was not treated. Medical treatment included, prednisolone (n = 6), diazoxide (n = 3) and therapeutic diet (n = 6). Surgical treatment consisted of pancreatic mass resection. Medical or surgical treatment resulted in short-term improvement in myoclonus frequency in all dogs, however, four were later euthanized due to recurrence of hypoglycemia and myoclonus. Myoclonus might represent an underrecognized neurological manifestation of hypoglycemia in dogs. Measurement of blood glucose concentrations is a fundamental diagnostic approach for identifying hypoglycemia-related myoclonus. Treatment can lead to clinical improvement, but prognosis is dependent on the underlying cause. The aim of this study was to describe muscle jerks in dogs with low blood sugar. Ten dogs were affected, and most had muscle jerks throughout the body, with some developing seizures during periods of low blood sugar. Most dogs were suspected of having a tumor of the pancreas, which might cause low blood sugar. Treatment with medication, surgery to remove the tumor, or both helped reduce the muscle jerks in all dogs at first, although some later had to be put to sleep because the low blood sugar and muscle jerks returned. Myoclonus wordt gekenmerkt door korte, schokachtige spiercontracties en werd bij honden niet eerder beschreven als neurologische manifestatie van hypoglycemie. Beschrijven van hypoglycemie-geassocieerde myoclonus bij honden en diagnostische bevindingen, behandeling en klinische uitkomst rapporteren. Tien honden met myoclonus en hypoglycemie. Multicentrisch retrospectief onderzoek bij honden met hypoglycemie-geassocieerde myoclonus. Alle honden presenteerden myoclonus. Bij 5/10 (50%) honden was het neurologisch onderzoek afwijkend. Myoclonus was gegeneraliseerd bij 8/10 (80%) honden en focaal (hoofd) bij 2/10 (20%). Bij 5/10 (50%) honden trad progressie op naar gegeneraliseerde epilepsieaanvallen. Bij alle honden werd tijdens de myoclonische episoden hypoglycemie (<3,3 mmol/L; mediane 2.07 mmol/L) vastgesteld. Insulinoma was de vermoedelijke ( n  = 1), waarschijnlijke ( n  = 5) of definitieve ( n  = 3) diagnose bij 9/10 (90%) honden. Een hond (10%) ontwikkelde iatrogene hypoglycemie na intraveneuze toediening van humane insuline. Van de 9 honden met vermoedelijke of bevestigde diagnose van insulinoma werden 5/9 (56%) medicamenteus behandeld, 3/9 (33%) kregen een combinatie van medicamenteuze en chirurgische behandeling en 1/9 (11%) werd niet behandeld. Medicamenteuze behandeling bestond uit prednisolone ( n  = 6), diazoxide ( n  = 3) en therapeutisch dieet ( n  = 6). Chirurgische behandeling bestond uit pancreasmassa resectie. Medicamenteuze en chirurgische behandeling resulteerde bij alle honden verbetering op korte termijn van de myoclonus frequentie. Vier honden werden later geëuthanaseerd wegens recidief van hypoglycemie en myoclonus. Myoclonus kan een onderkende neurologische uiting van hypoglycemie bij honden zijn. Het bepalen van de bloedglucoseconcentratie vormt een essentiële diagnostische stap. Behandeling van hypoglycemie kan leiden tot klinische verbetering, maar prognose is afhankelijk van de onderliggende oorzaak.

papers.title: Low complication rates are reported in cats presenting for neurological complaints and undergoing cerebrospinal fluid collection.
papers.authors: Spinoglio GJ, Korman R, Thompson AL
papers.abstract: To assess complications, outcomes, and associated risk factors of cats undergoing CSF collection. This was a single-center retrospective cohort study of client-owned cats presenting to 3 referral hospitals for CSF collection from January 2012 through December 2022. Cats were excluded for nonspecific and/or extraneural presenting complaints. If cats had multiple CSF collection presentations, only the first was included. Records were retrospectively assessed for signalment, physical examination findings, modified Glasgow coma scale, general anesthesia (GA) records, diagnostic imaging, clinical pathology results, and suspected or confirmed final diagnosis. Outcomes included complications and nonsurvival > 24 hours following CSF collection. Univariable logistic regression included breed, sex, body weight, age, modified Glasgow coma scale, evidence of herniation, evidence of intracranial hypertension (ICH) without herniation, GA protocol, GA duration, CSF analysis, collection site, inflammatory/infectious, and neoplasia diagnosis. P values were adjusted for multiple comparisons using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. 120 cats were identified, with 2 excluded for nonspecific and/or extraneural presenting complaint, leaving 118 cats. Seven (5.9%) did not survive > 24 hours following CSF procedure, and 9 (7.6%) reported complications, including apnea, suspected iatrogenic spinal cord trauma, and Cushing reflex. After multiple-comparison correction, no variable was significantly associated with outcome. Evidence of ICH without herniation and nonsurvival reported the largest effect estimate (OR, 36.99). Estimates are imprecise and reported as hypothesis generating. Feline CSF collection in this cohort reported low complication rates, and the majority survived > 24 hours after CSF collection. Imaging review for abnormalities associated with ICH is recommended prior to CSF collection.

papers.title: Two headless cannulated screws have a higher maximum failure load than screw-and-pin fixation at a 70° fracture angle in 3-dimensionally printed canine femoral neck models.
papers.authors: Song I, Kim S, Kim HY, Kim JM
papers.abstract: To compare maximum failure load among 3-D-printed canine femoral neck models differing in fracture angle and fixation configuration. This experimental biomechanical study was conducted in a university research laboratory from September 10, 2025, through March 10, 2026. Polycarbonate 3-D-printed models were created using left femoral CT data from a 2-year-old 11.9-kg Shiba Inu. The group configurations were a 50° femoral neck fracture stabilized with one 2.5-mm fully threaded headless cannulated screw (HCS) and an antirotation pin (1S1P50), a 70° fracture with the same fixation (1S1P70), and a 70° fracture stabilized with 2 parallel 2.5-mm HCSs (2S70). Initial construct stiffness was estimated from load-crosshead displacement curves. Maximum failure load, the primary outcome, was determined under single axial compression of the femoral head. 18 models were analyzed, with 6 in each group. There was no difference in initial construct stiffness among groups. Mean maximum failure loads were 511.5 N (SD, 81.9) in 1S1P50, 502.0 N (SD, 47.2) in 1S1P70, and 679.2 N (SD, 102.5) in 2S70. Maximum failure load was higher in 2S70 than in 1S1P70 (estimated difference, 176 N; Bonferroni-adjusted 98.3% CI, 31 to 301 N). Under static axial loading, 2S70 had a higher maximum failure load than 1S1P70, with no difference between 1S1P50 and either of the other 2 groups. Under static axial loading, 2 HCSs had a higher maximum failure load than did 1 HCS with an antirotation pin at a 70° fracture angle in 3-D-printed canine femoral neck models.

papers.title: Biomechanical evaluation of cerclage fixation constructs in a 3-dimensionally printed canine tibial long-oblique fracture model.
papers.authors: Park J, Kim JM, Kim HY
papers.abstract: To compare the biomechanical performance of cerclage fixation constructs in a standardized 3-D-printed canine tibial long-oblique fracture model. 3 fixation constructs-stainless steel wire cerclage (SSW), FiberWire cerclage (FW), and paraosseous clamp-cerclage stabilization (PCCS)-were compared in a standardized 3-D-printed canine tibial long-oblique fracture model. A standardized mid-diaphyseal long-oblique fracture was created in each specimen. Axial compression testing was performed until failure. Loads required to reach predefined displacement levels (1, 2, and 3 mm), maximum failure load, and failure mode were recorded. Data were analyzed using one-way ANOVA with the Tukey post hoc test. 21 tibial models (7/group) were evaluated. At all displacement levels, the FW group required significantly lower loads than both the SSW and PCCS groups, whereas no significant difference was observed between the SSW and PCCS groups. Mean loads at 1 mm displacement were 194.5 ± 32.2 N (SSW), 94.4 ± 21.0 N (FW), and 207.3 ± 64.0 N (PCCS). Maximum failure load was highest in the FW group (974.3 ± 77.0 N), followed by the PCCS group (879.0 ± 66.6 N) and SSW group (567.6 ± 63.2 N). PCCS demonstrated resistance to axial compression comparable to SSW fixation, whereas FW cerclage demonstrated the highest maximum failure load. These findings provide biomechanical information that may assist surgeons in selecting cerclage fixation methods for long-oblique tibial fractures in dogs.

papers.title: Effects of quercetin supplementation on the quality and metabolomic characteristics of sex-sorted frozen semen from Australian Wagyu bulls.
papers.authors: Yuan C, Yin Y, Wang X, Yu B, Wu J, Zhao Y, Liu J, Zhang K, Zhou W, Zhu Y, Xu L
papers.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the effects of different concentrations of quercetin on the post-thaw sperm quality of sex-sorted frozen semen from Australian Wagyu bulls and to investigate the underlying metabolic regulatory mechanisms using untargeted metabolomics. Sex-sorted frozen semen from Australian Wagyu bulls was treated with 0, 10, 50, 100, 150, and 200 μM quercetin. Sperm motility parameters, plasma membrane integrity, acrosome integrity, mitochondrial membrane potential, DNA integrity, reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, and antioxidant-related indices were assessed. Metabolomic profiling was further performed to compare the 50 μM quercetin-treated group with the control group. The results showed that the 50 μM quercetin group exhibited better sperm viability, motility, straight-line velocity (VSL), curvilinear velocity (VCL), and average path velocity (VAP), together with reduced ROS levels and increased activities of antioxidant enzymes, including SOD, CAT, and GSH-Px. High concentrations of quercetin (≥150 μM) adversely affected sperm motility and several functional parameters. Metabolomic analysis revealed clear metabolic differences between the 50 μM quercetin-treated group and the control group, with 131 upregulated and 395 downregulated differential metabolites identified. KEGG enrichment analysis indicated that these differential metabolites were mainly involved in lipid-related pathways, including glycerophospholipid metabolism and arachidonic acid metabolism. These results suggest that an appropriate concentration of quercetin may improve the post-thaw quality of sex-sorted frozen semen from Australian Wagyu bulls by alleviating oxidative stress and regulating lipid metabolism. This study provides experimental evidence and metabolomic insights for optimizing cryoprotectant formulations for bovine sex-sorted frozen semen.

papers.title: Long-term CT and US imaging of canine prostatic carcinoma after prostatic artery embolization: a 900-day follow-up case report.
papers.authors: Isshiki S, Tsuji-Kawahara S, Ogata M, Hisamoto S, Hashimoto M, Hasegawa T, Tsunoda I
papers.abstract: Canine prostatic carcinoma is a highly aggressive malignancy with a poor prognosis and limited long-term treatment options. Prostatic artery embolization (PAE) has emerged as a minimally invasive alternative, but long-term intraprostatic imaging changes after PAE in dogs remain poorly documented. We performed PAE on a 13-year-old neutered male Chihuahua with prostatic carcinoma. Designating PAE as Day 0, we monitored the prostate, bladder, and lungs with computed tomography (CT), ultrasonography (US), and thoracic radiography for approximately 900 days. Clinical signs remained well controlled; the dog survived until Day 918. CT showed intraprostatic hypoattenuating lesions (Day 33) that enlarged with gas accumulation (Day 173); US showed hypoechoic lesions (Day 271) that became scattered hyperechoic foci (Day 678). Following PAE, the prostatic parenchymal volume decreased by approximately 33% and remained stable until Day 481. No serious PAE-related complications were observed. These findings suggest that PAE induced sustained ischemic, cavitary, and chronic remodeling changes within the prostate, which may have contributed to the prolonged local disease control observed in this dog. To our knowledge, this represents the longest time-course imaging reported after PAE in a dog with prostatic carcinoma and illustrates the potential of PAE as a feasible, minimally invasive treatment option in general veterinary practice.

papers.title: Flow cytometry-based direct antiglobulin test for suspected feline immune-mediated thrombocytopenia: Assay development and demographic factors associated with direct antiglobulin test positivity.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Nedumpun T, Kamenkit O, Thongwandi S, Tripipat T, Wadeerat S, Boonyapisitsopa S, Bunpapong N
papers.abstract: This study aimed to develop and evaluate an in-house flow cytometry-based direct antiglobulin test (DAT) for detecting IgG-bound platelets in cats and to investigate the prevalence of DAT positivity and associated risk factors among thrombocytopenic cats. Platelets were identified by CD41/61 expression, and platelet-bound IgG was assessed using flow cytometry. A diagnostic cutoff for the percentage of IgG-positive platelets was established using 100 healthy cats and preliminarily evaluated in 50 cats with severe thrombocytopenia (platelet count <20,000/µl) before being applied to the remaining 411 thrombocytopenic cats (platelet count <200,000/µl) to determine the prevalence of DAT positivity and its associations with platelet count, breed, age, and sex. Healthy cats showed 0-10% IgG-positive platelets, and a cutoff of >10% was established. Using this cutoff, 105/461 (22.8%) thrombocytopenic cats were classified as DAT positive. DAT-positive cats had significantly lower platelet counts than DAT-negative cats (median 4000/µl; mean 12,562/µl vs 34,000/µl; mean 47,956/µl; P  <0.05), and the percentage of IgG-bound platelets was inversely correlated with platelet count ( r  = -0.38; P  = 0.048). No breed association was identified. Cats aged 5 years were more likely to be DAT positive, whereas castrated male cats were less likely to be DAT positive. Flow cytometry-based DAT is a useful adjunctive diagnostic tool for assessing suspected immune-mediated platelet destruction in thrombocytopenic cats. Younger cats may be at increased risk, whereas castrated male cats may be at lower risk. However, the interpretation of a DAT-positive test result should be made alongside assessment of clinical findings and investigations for underlying causes of thrombocytopenia.

papers.title: Prevalence and potential risk factors associated with idiopathic epilepsy in Golden Retrievers.
papers.authors: Winnerby M, Rohdin C, Strandberg E, Gredal H
papers.abstract: Idiopathic epilepsy (IE) in Golden Retrievers (GRs) has a suspected genetic basis with several endogenous risk factors potentially affecting the disease, including sex, breed subtypes, and chronic comorbidities. A subdivision into working (W-GRs) and show (S-GRs) Golden Retrievers presents a unique opportunity to investigate possible line-related risk factors. Define prevalence and investigate risk factors for IE in a population of Swedish GRs. We hypothesized a high prevalence of IE in GRs characterized by frequent cluster seizures, with the following representing potential risk factors for IE: subtype W-GR, male, and gastrointestinal or dermatologic signs or both. Twenty-nine client-owned GRs with IE and 714 controls. Prospective questionnaire-based study exploring the dog's health status, living conditions, and possible seizures, including questions regarding seizure characteristics, treatments, and clinical outcomes in affected dogs. Data was analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics and a logistic regression model was used to estimate the effect of potential risk factors on the probability of IE. The prevalence of IE in GRs was 3.9%, with 48.2% presenting with cluster seizures. A significant difference in prevalence of IE between W-GRs and S-GRs was not found. Being male, showing signs of gastrointestinal disease, and cereal-free diets were associated with increased risk of IE. Golden retrievers have an increased risk of IE, often presenting with cluster seizures. The association between IE and gastrointestinal disease might lead to new therapeutic strategies, but further investigations are needed.

papers.title: Global longitudinal strain assessment of systolic dysfunction in Doberman Pinschers with ventricular arrhythmias and normal echocardiographic measurements.
papers.authors: Hofmeister K, Friederich J, Schöbel J, Hertzsch S, Eberhard J, Schüttpelz R, Wess G
papers.abstract: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) in Doberman Pinschers (DPs) often initially manifests as ventricular arrhythmias (stage B1) without echocardiographic evidence of cardiac remodeling (stage B2). Global longitudinal strain (GLS) is a sensitive echocardiographic variable for detecting early systolic dysfunction. To assess whether GLS detects systolic dysfunction in DPs with arrhythmogenic stage B1 and to evaluate the association between arrhythmic burden and GLS. Sixty-three DPs with arrhythmogenic stage B1 DCM and 63 control DPs. Retrospective case-control study. Stage B1 was defined as ≥300 ventricular premature complexes (VPCs) within 24 h or >50 VPCs on two 24-h Holter recordings within 1 year, with otherwise normal echocardiographic measurements. Forty-three dogs had "last-normal" (LN) examinations 6-12 months before arrhythmia onset. GLS was measured using 2-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography (STE) from left apical 2-, 3-, and 4-chamber views. Stage B1 dogs were subclassified into low-grade (LGvpc) and high-grade (HGvpc) groups based on arrhythmic burden. GLS was lower in stage B1 dogs (mean ± SD, -16.80% ± 2.71%) compared to controls (-20.22% ± 1.90%; P = .044). Stage B1 dogs had lower GLS compared to their LN examinations (mean difference, -2.45%; 95% CI, -3.67% to -1.24%; P < .001). Dogs in the HGvpc group had lower GLS (-15.45% ± 2.79%) than LGvpc dogs (-18.39% ± 1.51%; mean difference, -2.94%; 95% CI, -4.28% to -1.60%; P < .001). GLS detects systolic dysfunction in DPs with arrhythmogenic stage B1 DCM despite normal conventional echocardiographic measurements. Higher arrhythmic burden is associated with more severe systolic dysfunction. Doberman Pinschers (DPs) are prone to dilated cardiomyopathy. This heart disease can cause abnormal heart rhythms, weakening and enlargement of the heart, heart failure, or sudden death. In some dogs, abnormal rhythms begin before a standard ultrasound scan shows changes in heart size or pumping ability. We studied whether an advanced echocardiographic method, named global longitudinal strain (GLS) could detect early weakening of the heart muscle. This measurement uses ultrasonographic images to assess how much the heart muscle shortens with each beat. The study included 63 DPs with abnormal rhythms arising from the lower chambers of the heart but normal standard ultrasonographic findings. We compared them with 63 healthy DPs. Earlier examinations before abnormal rhythms developed were available for 43 affected dogs. Dogs with abnormal rhythms had weaker heart muscle contraction than healthy dogs. Weakening was most pronounced in dogs with faster or more complex rhythms. These dogs were also more likely to later develop reduced pumping ability and heart enlargement. GLS might add useful information to screening, especially in dogs with more serious abnormal rhythms. It should be used alongside standard ultrasonographic scans and 24-h heart rhythm recordings, not as a replacement. Die dilatative Kardiomyopathie (DCM) beginnt bei Dobermännern häufig mit ventrikulären Arrhythmien (Stadium B1), bevor strukturelle Veränderungen echokardiographisch erkennbar sind (Stadium B2). Der globale longitudinale Strain (GLS) könnte eine frühe systolische Dysfunktion erfassen. Untersuchung, ob GLS bei Dobermännern im arrhythmogenen Stadium B1 eine systolische Dysfunktion erkennt und mit der Arrhythmielast zusammenhängt. Dreiundsechzig Dobermänner im arrhythmogenen Stadium B1 und 63 gesunde Kontrollhunde. Retrospektive Fall-Kontroll-Studie. Stadium B1 war definiert als ≥300 ventrikuläre Extrasystolen (VPCs)/24 Stunden oder > 50 VPCs in zwei 24-Stunden-Holter-Aufzeichnungen innerhalb eines Jahres bei normalen echokardiographischen Messwerten. Bei 43 Hunden lagen 6-12 Monate vor Arrhythmiebeginn „last-normal“-Untersuchungen (LN) vor. GLS wurde mittels zweidimensionaler Speckle-Tracking-Echokardiographie aus drei linksapikalen Ansichten bestimmt. Stadium-B1-Hunde wurden anhand der Arrhythmielast in LGvpc- und HGvpc-Gruppen eingeteilt. GLS war bei Stadium-B1-Hunden vermindert (Mittelwert ± Standardabweichung: −16,80 ± 2,71 % gegenüber −20,22 ± 1,90 % bei Kontrollhunden; P  = 0,044). Gegenüber den LN-Untersuchungen war GLS ebenfalls vermindert (mittlere Differenz: −2,45 %; 95%-Konfidenzintervall: −3,67 bis −1,24 %; P  < 0,001). Hunde der HGvpc-Gruppe hatten einen stärker verminderten GLS als Hunde der LGvpc-Gruppe (−15,45 ± 2,79 % gegenüber −18,39 ± 1,51 %; mittlere Differenz: −2,94 %; 95%-Konfidenzintervall: −4,28 bis −1,60 %; P  < 0,001). GLS erkennt bei Dobermännern im arrhythmogenen Stadium B1 trotz normaler konventioneller Echokardiographie eine systolische Dysfunktion. Eine höhere Arrhythmielast ist mit einer stärkeren Dysfunktion verbunden.

papers.title: Primary hyperparathyroidism in a 4-month-old German Shepherd mixed breed dog.
papers.authors: Aires-Serrano J, Shimali J, Renard J, Bird F, Hrovat A
papers.abstract: A 4-month-old female-intact German Shepherd mixed breed dog was evaluated for polyuria, polydipsia, oral discomfort, tachypnea, and pyrexia. Blood testing documented total and ionized hypercalcemia with an increased parathyroid hormone concentration. Computed tomography identified bone abnormalities of the mandibule and mild, diffuse pulmonary changes. Ultrasonography of the neck documented one mildly enlarged parathyroid gland that was surgically removed. Histopathology indicated diffuse chief cell hyperplasia. The ionized calcium concentration normalized within 7 days postoperatively.

papers.title: Morpho-molecular assessment of nanomaterials in teleost fish wound healing: a systematic review.
papers.authors: Rabea A, Ibrahim I, Mahgoub H, El-Shaieb A
papers.abstract: Teleost fish skin is a vital barrier for regulating osmoregulation, immune defense, and respiration. Cutaneous wounds in farmed fish cause significant economic loss and welfare concerns, as standard treatments, like antibiotics and chemical baths, are often ineffective, toxic, and fail to adhere to mucus-covered surfaces. While nanomaterials show great promise for wound healing, current data on how they work in fish remain incomplete. This systematic review evaluates the performance of these nanomaterials, explains their healing mechanisms, and highlights the key research gaps to guide future aquaculture treatments. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we included twelve in vivo studies (2017-2026). A clear shift was observed over time: research before 2020 focused only on metallic nanoparticles (silver and zinc oxide), whereas recent studies have mostly used biopolymeric nano-delivery systems. Nanoparticle treatments consistently led to faster wound closure, with several formulas healing over 90% of the wound within two weeks; however, these quantitative outcomes are strictly descriptive due to high methodological heterogeneity across studies. Under the microscope, nanomaterials accelerated re-epithelialization, improved collagen organization, and reduced inflammation. At the molecular level, they decreased pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL1β, TNFα) and matrix metalloproteinases (MMPS), while increasing anti-inflammatory markers (IL10, TGF-β) and antioxidant enzymes (SOD, CAT). Transcriptomics data also showed the activation of fibroblast growth factor 7 (FGF7) and the Jak-STAT pathways. Finally, zebrafish (Danio rerio) constituted 75% of the study models, showing a major gap in research on farmed fish like Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus). This systematic review shows that nanomaterials significantly accelerate teleost wound healing by promoting tissue regeneration and regulating the immune response. The shift toward biopolymeric systems, especially chitosan, indicates a clear trend toward safe and sustainable aquaculture medicine. Notably, testing hybrid nano-hyaluronic acid and nano-chitosan systems remains completely unexplored in farmed fish. This gap is important due to the complementary biological properties of these materials and the high global value of Nile tilapia. Testing this hybrid biomaterial under real farming conditions will help improve skin healing, support the immune system, and provide a safe wound treatment for global aquaculture.

papers.title: Survival patterns and prognostic factors associated with canine parvovirus infection in dogs presented at the KNUST Veterinary Teaching Hospital in Kumasi, Ghana.
papers.authors: Opoku ED, Folitse RD, Kodie DO, Agbota JD, Esther A, Tasiame W, Emikpe BO
papers.abstract: Canine parvovirus (CPV) remains one of the most severe and life-threatening infectious diseases affecting dogs globally, with disproportionately high mortality in puppies. Although CPV has been extensively studied in terms of prevalence and clinical presentation, evidence on survival patterns and prognostic factors in low-and middle-income country veterinary settings remains limited. This cohort study was undertaken at a Veterinary Teaching Hospital, Kumasi, Ghana. Diagnosis of CPV infection was based on clinical signs and confirmed by antigen detection using the CPV rapid immunoassay test kit. Only dogs that received treatment until recovery or death were included (n = 205). Data on factors influencing prognosis, including demographic, vaccination, clinical, and management variables, were collected. Time-to-recovery was analysed using cumulative incidence functions with Gray's test and Fine-Gray competing-risk regression. Mortality was evaluated using Cox proportional hazards regression. Hazard ratios (HRs) and subdistribution hazard ratios (SHRs) were reported with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. Mortality was highest in treated puppies aged 13-24 weeks and ≤ 12 weeks at 31.5% and 26.9% respectively, with dogs aged > 24 weeks recording the least with 5.9%. Mortality rate decreased progressively with an increasing vaccination frequency, being lowest in dogs vaccinated thrice. Among CPV-positive dogs, local breeds demonstrated a higher recovery rate than foreign breeds (SHR 1.64, 95% CI: 1.07-2.51; p = 0.022). Higher body weight was associated with a lower hazard of death (HR 0.86, 95% CI: 0.77-0.97; p = 0.012), while CPV-positive dogs showed a longer time to recovery, with a more gradual recovery trajectory observed beyond Day 5. This study highlights the significant impact of CPV on survival outcomes among dogs in Ghana, particularly among younger and incompletely vaccinated populations. The findings demonstrate that certain demographic and clinical factors play critical roles in recovery and mortality outcomes. Notably, local breeds exhibited a higher rate of recovery compared to foreign breeds diagnosed with CPV. These findings emphasise the need for strengthened vaccination coverage, early case detection, and context-appropriate clinical management strategies to improve recovery and reduce CPV-related mortality.

papers.title: Presumptive paroxysmal dyskinesia in 41 dogs: is the diet change enough?
papers.authors: Reyes HM, Galli G, Burbaitè E, Cocchetto A, Fiorentino E, Menchetti M
papers.abstract: Paroxysmal dyskinesia (PD) in dogs comprises episodic, involuntary, nonepileptic movement disorders. Recent evidence suggests that PD may be associated with gluten sensitivity, paralleling human gluten-related neurologic syndromes. Characterize clinical features, gastrointestinal comorbidities, gluten-related serology, and response to a gluten-free diet (GFD) in dogs with presumptive gluten-sensitive PD. We hypothesized that dietary modification would decrease episode frequency, particularly in dogs with gastrointestinal signs, seropositivity for anti-gliadin and anti-transglutaminase-2 immunoglobulin A antibodies or both. Forty-one client-owned dogs with presumptive PD. Retrospective review of dogs diagnosed with presumptive PD at a single institution between 2019 and 2023. Inclusion criteria included > 1 episode, video-documented episodes, normal interictal neurologic examination, serum gluten-related antibody titers, and ≥ 6 months of follow-up after transition to GFD. Gastrointestinal signs were reported in 33/41 (80.5%) dogs; 21/41 (51.2%) had at least 1 positive antibody titer. After dietary change, 24/41 (58.5%) dogs achieved complete resolution, 15/41 (36.6%) showed partial response, and 2/41 (4.9%) remained unchanged, regardless of antibody status. All owners reported gastrointestinal improvement. Nine dogs relapsed after initial response: 6 after gluten ingestion, 1 associated with stress, and 2 despite strict GFD. Response to GFD was not significantly associated with gastrointestinal signs or antibody status.
