Although dietary response was not significantly associated with antibody status or gastrointestinal signs, GFD led to substantial clinical improvement in most dogs with PD across multiple breeds, supporting a potential link between gluten sensitivity and PD, and a possible role of the gut-brain axis in disease pathogenesis.

papers.title: ClotPro viscoelastic testing in coagulation disorders in dogs: a retrospective analysis.
papers.authors: Doulidis PG, Frizzo-Ramos C, Prankch LJ, Rütgen B, Burgener IA, Luckschander-Zeller N
papers.abstract: Viscoelastic testing provides whole-blood assessment of coagulation, but clinical data on the performance of the ClotPro in dogs with naturally occurring diseases are limited. To evaluate pathway coherence of ClotPro variables with routine coagulation tests and to explore disease-associated viscoelastic phenotypes, fibrinolysis, and hypercoagulability. Eighty-four client-owned dogs admitted to a university hospital. Retrospective cohort study. ClotPro variables (clotting time, amplitude at 10 min, maximum clot firmness, maximum lysis across extrinsic pathway test [EX], intrinsic pathway test [IN], fibrinogen test channel, aprotinin test [AP] channels) were compared with prothrombin time (PT), activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT), platelet count (PLT), and D-dimer using Spearman correlation with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment. Group differences were assessed with Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn's post hoc. Hyperfibrinolysis (HF) was defined using paired EX-AP. A hypercoagulability index (HCI) and platelet/fibrin-adjusted residual firmness were derived. PT correlated with clotting time in EX channel (ρ = 0.48, q = 0.002) and aPTT with clotting time in IN channel (ρ = 0.42, q = 0.007). PLT correlated with maximum clot firmness in EX channel (EX_MCF) (ρ = 0.50, q = 0.001). maximum clot firmness in FIB channel correlated with EX_MCF (ρ = 0.58, q < 0.001) and maximum clot firmness in IN channel (ρ = 0.47, q = 0.003). maximum lysis in EX channel (EX_ML) correlated inversely with EX_MCF (ρ = -0.35, q = 0.028). D-dimer correlated with EX_ML (ρ = 0.30, q = 0.049). Group-level distributions overlapped substantially. HF was infrequent among cases (33% in dogs with hepatopathy and 21% in dogs with hemorrhagic diarrhea). The HCI differed across diseases (P = .0002), whereas platelet/fibrin-adjusted residual firmness did not. ClotPro variables demonstrated pathway-specific coherence with routine coagulation testing and consistent fibrinolysis patterns. Disease states did not define discrete viscoelastic phenotypes, supporting case-level interpretation.

papers.title: Prevalence of proprioception deficits in dogs visiting veterinary clinics for non-neurologic reasons: a cross-sectional study.
papers.authors: Tam A, Carney P, Merbl Y
papers.abstract: General proprioception deficits (GPD) detected during neurological exams aid in neurologic assessment and steer practitioners to consider neurological differential diagnoses. However, prevalence of GPD in without clinical signs of neurologic disease is limited. That elderly dogs have GPD that might be undetected in dogs not presenting for neurologic concerns and to determine GPD prevalence in dogs presented to a veterinary teaching hospital. The study included 277 client-owned dogs presenting to the Cornell University without neurologic complaints. Cross-sectional study with prospective data collection involved neurological assessment of dogs. Two hundred seventy-seven dogs met the inclusion criteria. For statistical analysis, ages were categorized into fractional lifespan (FL) groups: Group A (adult, ≤ 0.5), Group B (middle-aged, 0.5-0.75), and Group C (senior, >0.75). Dogs were scored based on hopping and paw replacement performance as normal, mildly, or severely affected. Seventy-two (26.0%; 95% CI, 20.9-31.7) exhibited GPD while 205 (74.0%) did not. Age distribution revealed 102 dogs (36.8%) in FL category 1 (≤0.5), 70 dogs (25.3%) in category 2 (>0.5 to ≤ 0.75), and 105 dogs (37.9%) in category 3 (>0.75). Both age (odds ratio [OR] 1.22, 95% CI, 1.13-1.33) and FL (OR 1.31, 95% CI, 1.18-1.46) were significantly positively associated with GPD (P < .0001). The prevalence of incidental GPD in dogs with no known neurological disease increases with age and is not influenced by sex or chondrodystrophic status. Awareness of this finding might aid general practitioners' decision-making, especially in aging dogs without overt acute neurologic disease. Proprioception is a dog’s built-in “sense” of where its legs and body are in space, without needing to look. It helps keep a dog’s gait steady and coordinated. Subtle problems with this sense (general proprioceptive deficits, or GPD) are usually looked for only when a dog shows signs of nervous system disease, so how common these deficits are in dogs and more interestingly is it more prevalent as dogs age, has not been well studied. This study examined 277 dogs visiting a veterinary teaching hospital for non-neurological reasons (such as eye, skin, or dental problems), with owners reporting no history of neurologic or gait problems. Trained examiners tested each dog’s paw-placement and hopping responses. About 1 in 4 dogs (26%) had a subtle proprioceptive deficit that owners had not noticed, and this became more common with age, affecting over 40% of senior dogs. The deficits were not linked to sex or to chondrodystrophic breeds (dogs with short, curved legs, such as Dachshunds or Corgis, who are prone to disc disease). These findings suggest that mild proprioceptive changes can be a normal part of aging in dogs, rather than always signaling active disease. For veterinarians, this offers a helpful reference point: an isolated, mild deficit in an older dog with no other concerning findings might not require immediate extensive workup, while awareness of this pattern can also help avoid dismissing early signs of a genuine, progressive neurologic problem.

papers.title: Clinical characteristics of pneumorrhachis in dogs and cats: a retrospective study of 125 cases.
papers.authors: Ooms S, Bossens K, Cornelis I, van Soens I, Kromhout K, Bhatti SFM
papers.abstract: Pneumorrhachis (PR), defined as gas within the vertebral canal, is an uncommon finding, and its clinical relevance and relationship to the vacuum phenomenon (VP) have not been systematically evaluated. To characterize the anatomical distribution of PR in dogs and cats undergoing computed tomography (CT) and to assess its relationship with signalment, VP, and concurrent neurological and non-neurological conditions. One hundred nineteen dogs and 6 cats with PR identified on CT between 2015 and 2023. Retrospective, descriptive study of medical records and CT reports. Cases were included when PR was documented in the radiology report, clinical and imaging information was available. Data included signalment, PR distribution, VP presence, final diagnosis categorized as neurological, non-neurological, postoperative, or no identified cause. Pneumorrhachis was identified with neurological conditions in 60/119 dogs (50%), including intervertebral disc disease (IVDD) in 50/60 (83%). Among IVDD-related PR, Hansen type I occurred in 32/50 (64%) cases. A VP was present in 23/50 dogs (46%), co-localized with the affected intervertebral disc in 78%. Non-neurological conditions accounted for 45/119 (38%) dogs, mainly neoplastic (44%) and respiratory (36%), with VP infrequently detected. Pneumorrhachis occurred postoperatively in 12/119 dogs. Two dogs (2%) had PR and epaxial muscle pain without an identifiable cause. In cats, PR was associated with neurological (2/6), non-neurological conditions (2/6), and postoperatively (2/6). No cases involved IVDD or VP. Pneumorrhachis in dogs and cats is considered an uncommon CT finding occurring with neurological and non-neurological conditions. Although often accompanying IVDD in dogs, PR was frequently incidental. Pneumorrhachis (PR) is the presence of air within the spinal canal. It is an uncommon finding in dogs and cats, and its clinical importance is not well understood. This study reviewed computed tomography (CT) examinations from 119 dogs and 6 cats in which PR was identified between 2015 and 2023. In dogs, PR was most commonly associated with neurological conditions, particularly intervertebral disc disease (IVDD). However, PR was also found in dogs with non-neurological diseases, including cancer and respiratory conditions, and after surgery. A vacuum phenomenon (VP), in which gas forms within a diseased intervertebral disc, was present in some dogs with IVDD and PR. In cats, PR was associated with neurological and non-neurological conditions and with previous surgery, but not with IVDD or the VP. These findings suggest that PR can occur in association with many different conditions and is not necessarily a sign of clinically important spinal disease. Although PR was frequently seen in dogs with IVDD, it was often an incidental finding. Recognizing these different associations may help veterinarians interpret PR when it is identified on CT.

papers.title: Management of volumetric muscle loss in a dog using bioactive glass-alginate-cellulose composite and a transpositional flap: a case report.
papers.authors: Zăvoi A, Ablassmaier T, Pop B, Mureșan Ș, Negoescu A, Lucaci F, Purdoiu R, Feraru A, Magyari K, Bel L, Dragomir M, Oana L, Taulescu M, Dreancă A
papers.abstract: This case report describes the management of a complex volumetric muscle loss (VML) injury in a 3-year-old mixed-breed dog following severe trauma to the right forelimb, which resulted in extensive multi-muscle defects that were unsuitable for primary closure. After initial stabilization and surgical debridement, reconstruction was achieved using a transpositional flap, while a gold nanoparticles-bioactive glass-alginate-cellulose (BGAuSP-Alg-MCC) composite was implanted to fill the dead space and support tissue regeneration. Postoperative healing was evaluated through clinical follow-up, computed tomography performed immediately and at 1 and 3 months postoperatively, as well as histological and immunohistochemical analyses. Imaging demonstrated progressive integration of the biomaterial, restoration of tissue density comparable to adjacent muscle, and absence of major complications. Histological evaluation demonstrated moderate inflammation and granulation tissue formation, containing numerous blood capillaries (neoangiogenesis), confirmed by CD31 and α-Smooth muscle actin (SMA) immunolabelling. Functional recovery was favorable, with preserved limb mobility and normal gait. These findings provide preliminary evidence of local biocompatibility and support the feasibility of incorporating the BGAuSP-Alg-MCC composite into a multimodal surgical management approach for extensive volumetric muscle loss in canine patients.

papers.title: Developmental lung disease with associated pulmonary hypertension in a Sphynx kitten.
papers.authors: Martin E, Wiggen KE, Williams K, Masseau I, Reinero CR
papers.abstract: This case report describes the clinical presentation, diagnostic findings and clinicopathologic features consistent with developmental lung disease (DLD) and pulmonary hypertension (PH) in a 3-month-old Sphynx Munchkin kitten. The kitten was originally referred for episodes of respiratory distress that was unresponsive to medical management, consisting of diuretics, antibiotics and corticosteroids. Echocardiography was consistent with a high probability of PH of a non-cardiac etiology. Baseline blood work, thoracic radiographs, thoracic CT with triphasic angiography and a bronchoalveolar lavage were performed. Thoracic CT revealed diffuse ground-glass opacity with bronchiolectasis and distention of the pulmonary artery and branches. The bronchoalveolar lavage identified an equal distribution of non-degenerative neutrophils and macrophages, with erythrophagocytosis and no overt neoplastic cells or infectious organisms identified. The kitten was humanely euthanized due to the lack of an identifiable treatable etiology and poor prognosis. Histopathological findings were most consistent with DLD with diffuse acinar underdevelopment and vascular changes including pulmonary capillary hemangiomatosis. These findings have not been previously reported in the feline DLD literature. There is a paucity of literature describing DLD and its potential to cause PH in cats. A comprehensive diagnostic evaluation, ultimately including histologic examination, is needed to reach a diagnosis of DLD. The presence of PH in a young kitten without any identifiable primary cardiac or respiratory cause, pulmonary thromboembolism or cardiac parasites should lead to a DLD being considered.

papers.title: Canine exposure to vector-borne pathogens in a rural Brazilian landscape.
papers.authors: Ubirajara Filho CRC, Mergulhão da Silva G, Lima MLO, Macedo LO, Alves LC, de Carvalho GA, Ramos RAN
papers.abstract: Vector-borne pathogens (VBPs) of medical and veterinary concern have mostly been studied in urban dog populations, while animals in rural settings, with limited access to ectoparasite prevention, have received less attention. In this study, we assessed canine exposure to VBPs in a rural Brazilian landscape. From August to October 2024, we collected 155 blood samples from dogs domiciled in a rural area of the municipality of Garanhuns, Pernambuco, Northeastern Brazil. Samples were assessed using an immunofluorescence antibody test (IFAT) to detect antibodies against Trypanosoma cruzi and using a rapid immunochromatographic test combined with an ELISA to detect Leishmania infantum antibodies. In addition, each sample was tested using a qualitative ELISA to detect D. immitis antigens and antibodies against Anaplasma phagocytophilum/Anaplasma platys, Ehrlichia canis/Ehrlichia ewingii, and Borrelia burgdorferi sensu lato. A total of 56.1% (87/155) of samples were reactive to at least one pathogen. Specifically, in 5.1% (8/155) were detected anti-T. cruzi antibodies, and in four of these samples (2.5%, 4/155) were co-detected antibodies anti-L. infantum. Antibodies against Ehrlichia spp. were observed in 50.9% (79/155), Anaplasma spp. in 8.3% (13/155), and B. burgdorferi in 0.6% (1/155). Antigens for D. immitis were detected in 1.2% (2/155). No statistical associations were observed on variables (sex, mobility, overnight stay and presence of ectoparasites) and pathogen seropositivity. In conclusion, dogs from rural areas are exposed to VBPs, which requires the use of ectoparasiticide preventive compounds to avoid ectoparasite infestation and reduce the risk of pathogen exposure.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Metagenomic Oxford Nanopore sequencing of feline aural inflammatory polyps for pathogen discovery.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Noland E, Conner K, Brame B, Petersen A, Thaiwong-Nebelung T
papers.abstract: ObjectivesFeline aural inflammatory polyps (FIAP) have been proposed to be induced by chronic viral or bacterial infections; however, the cause is still unknown. The aim of this study was to investigate potential etiologies of these polyps using metagenomic sequencing.MethodsPolyp tissue was collected from 13 cats following routine traction and avulsion procedures. Total nucleic acid was extracted and subjected to a host (feline) nucleic acid depletion protocol. Additionally, the Sequence-Independent Single-Primer Amplification (SISPA) method was used to enrich for low-abundance RNA viral genomes. Sequencing was conducted on the Oxford Nanopore MinION sequencing platform. Non-feline sequencing reads were taxonomically classified against custom bacterial/viral databases to calculate relative genus-level abundances.ResultsTaxonomic classification of sequencing reads identified various bacteria across samples and, in some samples, rare viruses. However, no common microbial sequences were associated with polyps to suggest a specific infectious etiology. Bacterial communities were dominated by Pseudomonadota, Actinomycetota, and Bacillota phyla, with Pseudomonadota and Actinomycetota being more frequently dominant. Lasallevirus was detected in few samples with unknown clinical relevance. Culture and sequencing showed partial concordance in identifying bacteria in some cases.Conclusions and relevanceNo common microbial-associated sequences found to be associated with polyp samples; therefore, no suspect causative agent was identified. 16S and ITS metagenomic sequencing on FIAP may help further elucidate if microbial population shifts have a role in polyp development and recurrence and/or persistence of inflammation leading to polyp development.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Assessment of caregiver burden in feline chronic kidney disease.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Lim L, Quimby JM, Caney S
papers.abstract: ObjectivesThe aim of this study was to investigate caregiver burden associated with management of cats with chronic kidney disease (CKD).MethodsCaregivers who had experience managing a cat with CKD were recruited through social media to anonymously participate in an online Qualtrics survey. The modified Zarit Burden Interview (mZBI) was incorporated into the survey to objectively assess caregiver burden. An mZBI score of ≥ 18 represents clinically significant burden.ResultsA total of 339 surveys were completed. 46% of caregivers reported an mZBI score of ≥ 18. Caregivers of cats with IRIS stages 3/4 had significantly higher mZBI scores (median 20.0, range 3 - 50) than caregivers of cats with IRIS stages 1/2 (median 14.5, range 0 - 58; P = 0.0007). Caregivers who reported never to rarely sharing care responsibilities had significantly higher mZBI scores (median 20.0; range 0 - 50) than those who reported sometimes to always sharing care responsibilities (median 15.0; range 2 - 58) (P = 0.0007). Caregivers who reported the need to coax their cat to eat on a daily basis had higher mZBI scores (median 22.8, range 2 - 50) than those who never coaxed their cat to eat (median 14.5, range 0-49) or coaxed their cat 1-2 days/week (median 19.2, range 3 - 42) (both P < 0.001). Caregivers who always felt supported by the veterinary care team had lower mZBI scores (median 13; range 0-58) than those that only felt supported sometimes to never (median 23; range 5-45) (P < 0.001).Conclusions and clinical importanceSignificant caregiver burden is present in feline CKD, emphasizing the need to for clinicians to provide empathetic advice and practical support.

papers.title: The hormonal effects of owner-cat interactions on pet cats of different potential attachment styles.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: He X, Huang H, Chang H, Xu W, Gui C, Pan J, Yan H, Guo Y, Avilas-Rosa E, Yang B, Deng B, Zhang L
papers.abstract: The aim of the present study was to investigate how different owner-cat interaction types influence stress and owner-bonding in pet cats with different potential attachment styles, using salivary cortisol and oxytocin as physiological indicators. Twenty pet cats were classified into potential secure, insecure-anxious or insecure-avoidant attachment styles using the Secure Base Test. Owners engaged in four types of interactions with their cats at home on separate days. Saliva samples were collected before and after each interaction and analysed for cortisol and oxytocin concentrations. The effects of attachment style, interaction type and time on hormonal changes were examined. Significant interactive effects of potential attachment style and time, as well as interaction type and time, were observed for both cortisol and oxytocin. Passive interactions were associated with increased oxytocin and decreased cortisol, whereas forced interactions showed an opposite pattern. Secure cats exhibited more positive hormonal responses to human interactions compared with insecure cats, who showed increased cortisol or limited hormonal changes. Insecure cats also showed higher basal oxytocin levels than secure cats. Human-cat interactions trigger changes in cortisol and oxytocin levels, depending on the interaction type and cat's attachment style. These findings highlight the importance of considering individual cat attachment differences when promoting appropriate interaction strategies to improve cat welfare and human-cat relationships.

papers.title: Effects of a Dietary Supplementation of Bovine Colostrum in Dogs With Atopic Dermatitis.
papers.authors: Schäfer L, Büttner K, Paßlack N
papers.abstract: Bovine colostrum (BC) shows immunomodulatory properties, which could be beneficial in the management of chronic immune-mediated diseases such as canine atopic dermatitis (cAD). To assess if a BC supplementation affects selected immune variables and clinical signs in cAD. Twenty client-owned dogs with non-seasonal, environmentally induced cAD were enrolled in this prospective, double-blinded, placebo-controlled study. After a 2-week adaptation to standardised feeding, the dogs were divided into two groups, receiving either a placebo or BC at 0.2% in dietary dry matter for 4 weeks. Afterwards, the dogs remained on their diets for another 4 weeks, without placebo and BC supplementation. Blood and faecal samples were collected on Day (D)14, D42 and D70 for immunological measurements (proliferative and phagocytic activity of blood leukocytes, faecal immunoglobulin [Ig]A, plasma concentrations of Igs, C-reactive protein [CRP] and serum amyloid A [SAA]). Additionally, the Canine Atopic Dermatitis Extent and Severity Index, 4th iteration (CADESI-04) was assessed. The owners evaluated pruritus (Visual Analog Scale) of their dogs retrospectively and daily (r-/d-pVAS), as well as quality-of-life (QoL), global assessment and quality-of-coat. No significant diet effects were detected for the clinical and immunological parameters evaluated. A slight improvement in QoL could be observed in both feeding groups over time. An oral administration of BC did not alter relevant clinical and immune parameters in patients with cAD.

papers.title: Palatability assessment of a commercial wet renal diet in healthy cats: an open-label in-home exploratory trial.
papers.authors: Magalhães TR, Corbee RJ, Queiroga FL, Lourenço AL
papers.abstract: Wet renal diets are considered the best option for managing cats with chronic kidney disease (CKD), but their palatability is a recurrent concern. Assess the palatability of a commercial wet diet formulated for early-stage CKD in cats. Forty-two healthy cats privately owned by 31 caregivers. An open-label in-home feeding trial was conducted over three 6-day phases, during which cats were offered the wet renal diet (Phase 1), their usual wet diet (Phase 2), and both diets simultaneously (Phase 3). Time from diet presentation to eating (latency time), food intake, and feeding-related behaviors were recorded by caregivers. Analyses included descriptive statistics and mixed-effects regression models. Caregivers classified renal diet acceptance as positive for 69.0% (n = 29) of cats, negative for 23.8% (n = 10), and neutral for 7.1% (n = 3). Overall, cats were significantly more likely (P < .001) to be recorded in a higher diet intake category in Phase 2 than in Phase 1, whereas latency time did not differ significantly (P = .07). Based on recorded intake during Phase 3, neither diet was significantly preferred (P = .34), although caregivers perceived a preference for the usual diet in 47.6% (n = 20) of cats and for the renal diet in 45.2% (n = 19). If prescribed, caregivers would offer this therapeutic diet to 78.6% (n = 33) of cats. In this short-term feeding trial, most healthy cats accepted the renal diet formulated for early-stage CKD with no apparent palatability concerns.

papers.title: Bacterial aortic endarteritis with sepsis as a rare complication of aortic dissection in a cat.
papers.authors: Lim S, Shekelle KL, Groch KR, Porter BF, Malcolm E, Gordon S
papers.abstract: A 14-year-old domestic shorthair cat was examined because of respiratory distress. Thoracic radiography showed a prominent aortic arch and no other abnormalities. Echocardiography documented a mobile flap within the ascending aorta creating 2 lumens, consistent with aortic dissection (AD), mild pericardial effusion with tamponade, left ventricular concentric hypertrophy, and normal left atrial size. Systemic hypertension (200 mmHg) was the presumed cause of AD, prompting administration of telmisartan, furosemide, and amlodipine. The cat clinically improved, became normotensive, and was discharged 2 days later. The cat remained well for 4 months, then became lethargic and died. Necropsy showed a 7.6 cm long aortic intimal flap, severe bacterial aortic endarteritis, and evidence of sepsis including multiple organ necrosis, thrombosis, and embolic glomerulonephritis. Bacterial culture of the kidneys yielded mixed bacterial growth including Pasteurella stomatis, presumably the same bacterium identified in the endarteritis lesion. Infective aortic endarteritis can be a fatal complication of AD.

papers.title: Low plasma butyrylcholinesterase activity in dogs: prevalence, association with underlying disorders, laboratory variables, and survival.
papers.authors: Tesseraux AM, Howard J, Peters LM
papers.abstract: Low blood butyrylcholinesterase (BChE) activity is associated with obesity, pancreatitis, inflammation, sepsis, and malignancy in people, often with negative prognostic value. The clinical relevance of BChE activity in dogs remains unclear. Describe the prevalence of low BChE activity in a large population of dogs and its association with selected underlying disorders, outcome, and clinicopathological variables. We hypothesized that low BChE activity would be associated with inflammatory disorders and a negative outcome. A total of 950 client-owned dogs presented to a university teaching hospital with BChE activity measured within 24 h of admission. Retrospective observational study of clinical records and laboratory data. Admission BChE activities ranged from 482 to 17 348 U/L (median, 4553 U/L; interquartile range [IQR], 3485-5926 U/L) and were below reference intervals (RI) in 83 of 950 dogs (8.7%) at admission and in 53 of 207 (25.6%) dogs with repeat in-hospital measurements. Low BChE activity was associated with systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS) and sepsis, but the predictive value was lower than that of C-reactive protein (CRP). Low admission BChE activity was associated with increased odds of non-survival, lower hematocrit and cholesterol concentrations and increased band neutrophil percentages, but no associations were found with obesity, acute pancreatitis, or malignancy. Activity of BChE behaves as a negative inflammatory marker in dogs, but its utility as a standalone clinical classifier for SIRS or sepsis is limited and inferior to CRP. Low BChE activity is associated with poor prognosis but is not an independent predictor of outcome. Butyrylcholinesterase (BChE), an enzyme related to acetylcholinesterase, contributes to neurotransmission, toxin metabolism and has anti-inflammatory properties. In humans, it is low in inflammatory conditions, high in obesity and associated with severity of disease and prognosis. We aimed to investigate the frequency of low BChE activity as well as its diagnostic and prognostic value in dogs with different disorders. Of 950 dogs presented to a small animal referral hospital over 12 months, 8.7% of all dogs had low BChE activity at admission and 25.6% of hospitalized dogs had low activity at some point during their stay. We found that BChE activity was often low in inflammatory conditions such as systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS) and sepsis, making it a negative inflammatory marker. However, its performance was inferior compared with the well-established inflammatory marker, C-reactive protein. Low BChE at admission and during hospitalization was associated with higher mortality. We could not confirm any association of BChE with obesity, acute pancreatitis, or cancer that were shown in previous studies of humans and dogs.

papers.title: Evaluation of serum pancreatic lipase activity in dogs with myxomatous mitral valve disease.
papers.authors: Kim C, Chae Y, Yun T, Kang BT, Kim H
papers.abstract: Previous studies have evaluated the association between myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD) and pancreatic lipase activity, but medications remain unconsidered. Elevated serum pancreatic lipase activity is related to cardiac medication in dogs with MMVD. Eighty-two client-owned dogs without clinical signs of pancreatitis (MMVD, n = 67 [stage B1 = 24; stage B2 = 22; non-medicated stage C = 9; medicated stage C = 12]; controls, n = 15). Retrospective cross-sectional study. Dogs were classified into MMVD stage and control groups. Serum pancreatic lipase activity was compared among groups, and correlation and multivariable linear regression analyses were performed. In non-medicated dogs, pancreatic lipase activity did not differ among groups. In contrast, medicated stage C dogs had higher pancreatic lipase activity than controls (median difference, 67.5 U/L; 95% CI, 19.0-184.0), stage B1 (57.0 U/L; 95% CI, 12.0-145.0), stage B2 (65.8 U/L; 95% CI, 18.0-156.0), and non-medicated stage C (58.0 U/L; 95% CI, 9.0-268.0). Moreover, 25% (3/12) of medicated stage C dogs had pancreatic lipase activity exceeding 400 U/L, whereas no non-medicated stage C dogs reached this threshold. Pancreatic lipase activity was positively correlated with furosemide (ρ = 0.67) and duration of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor (ρ = 0.62) administration. In multivariable analysis, medication was the independent predictor of pancreatic lipase activity in dogs with MMVD. Pancreatic lipase activity might be elevated in some dogs with MMVD receiving cardiac medications, highlighting the importance of considering medication history in clinical interpretation. 배경: 기존 연구에서 개의 점액종성 승모판막질병(myxomatous mitral valve disease, MMVD)과 혈청 췌장 라이페이스 활성도의 연관성이 평가되었으나, 심장약물이 혈청 라이페이스 활성도에 미치는 영향은 고려되지 않았다. 가설: MMVD에 이환된 개에서 혈청 췌장 라이페이스 활성도의 증가는 심장약물 투여와 관련이 있을 것이다. 연구대상: 췌장염의 임상증상이 없는 개 82마리를 대상으로 하였다(MMVD 67마리 [Stage B1 = 24마리, Stage B2 = 22마리, 심장약물을 투여 받지 않은 Stage C = 9마리, 심장약물을 투여 받은 Stage C = 12마리]와 대조군 15마리). 연구방법: 후향적 단면연구를 수행하였다. 연구대상 개를 MMVD 단계 및 대조군으로 분류하였다. 그룹 간 혈청 췌장 라이페이스 활성도를 비교하였으며, 상관분석과 다변량 선형회귀분석을 수행하였다. 결과: 심장약물을 투여 받지 않은 개에서는 그룹 간 췌장 라이페이스 활성도에 유의한 차이가 없었다. 반면, 심장약물을 투여 받은 Stage C 개에서는 대조군(중앙값 차이 67.5 U/L; 95% 신뢰구간 [CI], 19.0-184.0), Stage B1(57.0 U/L; 95% CI, 12.0-145.0), Stage B2(65.8 U/L; 95% CI, 18.0-156.0) 및 심장약물을 투여 받지 않은 Stage C(58.0 U/L; 95% CI, 9.0-268.0)에 비해 췌장 라이페이스 활성도가 높았다. 또한 심장약물을 투여 받은 Stage C 개의 25%(3/12)에서 췌장 라이페이스 활성도가 400 U/L를 초과한 반면, 심장약물을 투여 받지 않은 Stage C 개에서는 400 U/L를 초과한 개가 없었다. 췌장 라이페이스 활성도는 푸로세마이드 투여기간(ρ = 0.67) 및 안지오텐신-전환 효소 억제제 투여기간(ρ = 0.62)과 양의 상관관계를 보였다. 다변량 분석에서 심장약물 투여는 MMVD 개의 췌장 라이페이스 활성도와 독립적 연관 요인이었다. 결론 및 임상적 의의: 심장약물을 투여 받는 일부 MMVD 개에서 췌장 라이페이스 활성도가 증가할 수 있으 므로, MMVD 개에서 췌장 라이페이스 검사 결과 해석 시 심장약물 투여 이력을 함께 고려해야 한다. Dogs with myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD), particularly those with congestive heart failure, can have increased serum pancreatic lipase activity, which is commonly used as a marker of pancreatic injury. However, it remains unclear whether this increase is related to the severity of heart disease itself or to the medications used to treat congestive heart failure in dogs. The present study evaluated pancreatic lipase activity in 82 dogs, including 67 dogs with different stages of MMVD and 15 control dogs. Among dogs not receiving cardiac medications, serum pancreatic lipase activity did not differ according to MMVD stage. In contrast, dogs with Stage C MMVD receiving cardiac medications had higher serum pancreatic lipase activity than the other groups. Three of 12 (25%) medicated stage C dogs had pancreatic lipase activity above 400 U/L, a threshold considered suggestive of pancreatitis, whereas none of the non-medicated Stage C dogs exceeded this threshold. Longer durations of furosemide and angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor administration were also associated with higher serum pancreatic lipase activity in medicated stage C dogs. These findings suggest that cardiac medication use should be considered when interpreting increased serum pancreatic lipase activity in dogs with MMVD.

papers.title: Trichomonads in the oral cavity of dogs and cats: species composition and relationship with animal age and oral hygiene status.
papers.authors: Piekara-Stępińska A, Czerski A, Szczepankiewicz B, Lachowicz-Wolak A, Gorczykowski M, Piekarska J
papers.abstract: The oral cavity provides a suitable environment for various microorganisms, including protozoa such as trichomonads, which may be associated with periodontal disease development. Humans are considered the typical hosts of Trichomonas tenax but it has also been found in dogs, cats, and other animals, which makes it a factor with a significant zoonotic potential. Apart from T. tenax, domestic carnivores may be infected with such species as T. canistomae, T. felistomae and T. brixi. The aim of this study was to determine the prevalence, species composition, and risk factors of trichomonad colonization of the oral cavity in dogs and cats from Poland. Oral swabs from 238 household animals (151 dogs and 87 cats) were examined using cultivation methods. Amplification of ITS1- 5.8 S rRNA-ITS2 fragment was performed for microscopic-positive samples and PCR products were further sequenced. Trichomonads were identified in 26 out of 151 (17.22%) canine and 5 out of 87 (5.75%) feline samples. Higher frequency was observed in older dogs and dogs with intense dental calculus. T. brixi and T. tenax were the only species detected in both dogs and cats. The detection of zoonotic T. tenax in a substantial number of examined animals highlights the relevance of this finding also in the context of human health.

papers.title: The Role of Comorbidities in Pyoderma Among Canine and Feline Diabetic Patients.
papers.authors: Wixon V, Pieper JB, Bachtel J
papers.abstract: Pyoderma is considered a secondary complication of diabetes mellitus (DM), yet the relationship remains unclear. One study found 22% of diabetic dogs with dermatopathy had no other comorbidities while cats have not been evaluated. This study evaluated the association of DM and pyoderma in dogs and cats by identifying comorbidities. This retrospective study analysed canine and feline DM cases from August 2019 to November 2022 at Iowa State University and Colorado State University. We analysed cytologically confirmed pyoderma and assessed the prevalence of comorbidities, including allergies, thyroid and adrenal disease, neoplasia and other dermatological disorders. Pyoderma was prevalent in 7.6% (61 of 805) dogs and 4.0% (15 of 372) cats with concurrent DM. Of 61 dogs, two (3.3%) lacked comorbidities which was considered protective (odds ratio [OR] = 0.06; 95% CI 0.01-0.29; p < 0.001). Allergic dermatitis was the most common comorbidity (70.5%) in dogs with increased odds (OR = 9.15; 95% CI 4.25-19.72; p < 0.001). Among 15 cats, one (6.7%) lacked comorbidities (OR = 0.04; 95% CI 0.01-0.34; p = 0.003), while allergic dermatitis appeared most frequent and increased odds (73.3%; OR = 18.67; 95% CI 4.81-72.44; p < 0.001). West Highland white terriers (OR = 4.59; 95% CI 1.43-14.77; p = 0.011) and domestic medium hair cats (OR = 7.31; 95% Cl 1.05-50.68; p = 0.044) had increased odds of pyoderma. This study suggests that pyoderma in DM cats and dogs is uncommon as pyoderma owing to DM alone being seen in only 0.25% of dogs and 0.27% of cats.

papers.title: Mammary secretory carcinoma in a female domestic rabbit (Oryctolagus cuniculus): histopathological and immunohistochemical features.
papers.authors: Nunes MM, Oliveira ES, Wronski JG, de Souza Ruas Lopes R, da Rocha MLMS, Nakagaki KYR, Cassali GD
papers.abstract: Secretory carcinoma of the breast is a rare histological subtype in women and is uncommon in female dogs and cats, with only two cases described in female dogs and one case described in a cat. This report describes the histopathological and immunohistochemical features of secretory carcinoma of the mammary gland in a domestic rabbit (Oryctolagus cuniculus). Microscopic evaluation revealed a non-encapsulated, well-demarcated neoplastic proliferation composed of epithelial cells arranged in solid and tubular patterns, supported by a delicate fibrous connective tissue stroma. The neoplastic cells had slightly eosinophilic cytoplasm, frequently containing large, well-demarcated vacuoles that displaced the nucleus to the periphery, giving the cells a signet-ring-like appearance. Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) histochemical staining, performed with and without diastase digestion, showed positivity in the intracellular and extracellular secretory material in both approaches. Immunohistochemical evaluation was performed for the markers α-lactalbumin, Ki-67, estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and COX-2. Positive cytoplasmic immunolabeling for α-lactalbumin was observed in neoplastic cells and in intracellular and extracellular secretory material, confirming their secretory nature. The diagnosis of secretory carcinoma was established based on the association of histopathological, histochemical, and immunohistochemical features. Considering the secretory features of the mammary gland in rabbits, secretory carcinoma should be included in the differential diagnosis of mammary carcinomas with prominent secretory activity in this species.

papers.title: Reassessing neonatal hypoglycemia in kittens: Clinical relevance beyond the laboratory value.
papers.authors: de Oliveira NMS, Carneiro MD, Talieri IC, Milken VMF, Gouvêa FN, Borin-Crivellenti S, Crivellenti LZ
papers.abstract: The underdeveloped metabolism in newborn kittens, along with the quick use of liver sugar reserves and the limited ability to produce glucose, makes them prone to low blood sugar levels during this time. This condition may be potentially fatal, although reduced blood glucose values do not necessarily manifest with clinical signs. Fifteen neonatal kittens born to three clinically healthy pregnant queens were evaluated during the first three days of life. Apgar scoring was done daily, and blood glucose measurements began within the first hour after birth (T1), followed by evaluations every 2 hours, with a total of six measurements each day from T2 to T6. Samples were obtained via capillary puncture with alternating digital pads and analyzed using a glucometer validated for cats. A total of 270 glycemic measurements were performed, demonstrating instability during the first hours of life. On the first day, there was a mean glucose concentration of 61.7 ± 22.2 mg/dL. On the second day, it dropped to 53.9 ± 16.5 mg/dL. On the third day, metabolic recovery occurred (68.5 ± 14.7 mg/dL). All neonates maintained adequate Apgar scores and showed no clinical signs of hypoglycemia (< 50 mg/dL; weakness, apathy, or reduced suckling reflex). Marked fluctuations in blood glucose levels were observed during the first 48 hours, characterized by wide glycemic variability (22-165 mg/dL on day 1 and 21-86 mg/dL on day 2). A high frequency of hypoglycemic values was recorded, reaching 51.1% on the first day and 60% on the second, indicating initial metabolic instability despite intermediate mean glucose levels. Progressive stabilization was observed by the third day (range 26-95 mg/dL), with the rate of hypoglycemic events dropping to 22.2%, reflecting the maturation of neonatal metabolic homeostasis. Despite the laboratory diagnosis of hypoglycemia, none of the kittens exhibited clinical manifestations or required intervention.

papers.title: Comment on 'Fibroepithelial Polyps of the Ear Canal in Dogs: A Retrospective Analysis of 17 Cases'.
papers.authors: Lucas R, Tortoriello R

papers.title: Retrospective evaluation of lipiduria in urine from 140 dogs and 74 cats.
papers.authors: Cervone M, Legroux D, Barral G, Ramery E
papers.abstract: Lipiduria has recognized physiopathological and diagnostic relevance in human medicine, while data regarding its relevance in animals remain limited. To determine the frequency of lipiduria in dogs and cats and to assess whether lipiduria represents an epiphenomenon or is associated with animal-related factors. Urinalysis results from 140 dogs and 74 cats. Retrospective study. Cases were included if complete urinalysis data were available. Animals were classified as lipiduric or non-lipiduric. Animal characteristics, as well as selected hematologic and urinary abnormalities, were compared between groups. In dogs, factors potentially associated with the presence of lipiduria were further evaluated using multivariable logistic regression analysis. Overall, 58% (125/214) animals were lipiduric, including 46% (64/140) dogs and 82% (61/74) cats. Lipiduria was significantly more frequent in cats (82%) than in dogs (46%) (P < .00001). Among cats, lipiduric individuals were older (mean age 9.5 years; SD ± 4.5; P = .02). In dogs, females (63%; 40/64) were overrepresented in the lipiduric group (P = .0008). Lipiduric dogs had a higher mean urine pH (6.4; SD ± 1.2; P = .00054) and more frequently exhibited struvite crystalluria (17%; 11/64; P = .003). In multivariable analysis, female dogs had 3.5-fold higher odds of lipiduria (OR, 3.5; 95% CI, 1.7-7.3), and the odds of lipiduria increased by 5% for each 0.1-unit increase in urine pH. Lipiduria was a common finding in this study, particularly in cats. In dogs, our findings suggest a potential link between lipiduria, female status, and high urine pH. Lipid droplets can sometimes be detected in urine, a finding known as lipiduria. Although lipiduria is well described in human medicine, little is known about how common it is in dogs and cats or whether it is associated with animal-related factors. In this retrospective study, we reviewed complete urinalysis results from 140 dogs and 74 cats. Lipiduria was identified in 58% of all animals and was much more common in cats (82%) than in dogs (46%). Cats with lipiduria were, on average, older than cats without lipiduria. In dogs, after accounting for several factors, female dogs were more likely to have lipiduria, and the likelihood of lipiduria increased as urine pH increased. These findings suggest that lipiduria is common in dogs and cats, particularly in cats. In dogs, it might be associated with sex and urine pH.

papers.title: Assessment of bowel preparation quality in dogs undergoing colonoscopy using the Boston Bowel Preparation Scale.
papers.authors: Ruedi GL, Kook PH
papers.abstract: To evaluate the efficacy of a bowel preparation protocol consisting of at-home administration of clear broth and polyethylene glycol 3350 followed by colonic flushing immediately before colonoscopy in dogs. In this single-referral-center retrospective study, dogs with complete video documentation of the colon were included. Colonic cleanliness was assessed using the Boston Bowel Preparation Scale (BBPS), which scores the 3 colonic segments individually (total score range, 0 to 9 with higher scores indicating better preparation quality). Adequate preparation was defined as a total BBPS score ≥ 6 with no individual segment score < 2. Video footage from 49 colonoscopies performed in 47 dogs was assessed by a single examiner. Adequate colonic preparation was achieved in 41 of 49 (84%) colonoscopies. Median total BBPS score was 7 (range, 4 to 9), with median segment scores of 3, 2, and 2 for descending, transverse, and ascending colon, respectively. The ascending colon had significantly lower scores than the descending colon. In 57% of procedures, the indication for colonoscopy was evaluation of chronic enteropathy (combined upper and lower intestinal endoscopy) without specific suspicion of colonic disease. High-quality bowel preparation for colonoscopy can be achieved without complex or logistically demanding protocols. A straightforward, owner-friendly, at-home preparation regimen provided diagnostic-quality colonic visualization in dogs. These findings may facilitate broader clinical use of colonoscopy in dogs by supporting practical bowel preparation protocols that are feasible for owners and sufficient for diagnostic evaluation, particularly when complete colonic cleanliness is not essential for the intended diagnostic objective.

papers.title: Surgical management of cricopharyngeal achalasia in dogs results in low mortality but moderate incidence of recurrence or persistent clinical signs.
papers.authors: Zhang RM, Brisson BA, Holt DE, Park B, Ham KM, Hawker W
papers.abstract: To describe diagnostic and surgical management of cricopharyngeal achalasia (CA) in dogs and to identify patient or management factors that may contribute to postoperative outcomes. Signalment, diagnostic imaging findings, surgical information, complications, and outcomes were retrospectively obtained. Fisher exact and Wilcoxon rank-sum tests were performed to identify predictors of unsatisfactory outcomes using sex, breed, age, videofluoroscopic swallow study findings, laterality of surgery, and muscles resected as variables. 26 dogs surgically managed for CA from 2009 through 2025 were included. The most common breeds were Poodle mixes (n = 12) and Golden Retrievers (8). Ventral bilateral surgery resulted in shorter operative times than through 2 lateral incisions. Postoperative complication and mortality rates were 23% and 11.5%, respectively. Aspiration pneumonia was the most common postoperative complication. Unsatisfactory outcomes were reported in 42.3%. Recurrence of clinical signs after initial resolution was noted in 34.6%, and revision surgery was performed in 26.9%. Median time to recurrence was 84 days (range, 7 to 1,320 days). No significant association was identified for age, sex, breed, laterality, videofluoroscopic swallow study findings, or muscles resected. Surgical management of CA resulted in low mortality, moderate incidence of recurrence and revision surgery, and residual symptoms requiring long-term conservative management. Surgery is a safe option for management of CA, but owners should be informed of the risks of recurrence and residual clinical signs that may require long-term dietary modifications. Animals with CA are at risk of aspiration pneumonia both pre- and postoperatively and should be monitored accordingly.

papers.title: Cytokine priming shifts mitochondrial architecture and extracellular vesicle cargo of feline placental mesenchymal stromal cells toward an immunosuppressive phenotype.
papers.authors: Soltero-Rivera M, Arzi B, Marycz K
papers.abstract: To characterize effects of inflammatory cytokine priming on viability, mitochondrial morphology, and extracellular vesicle (EV) cargo in feline placenta-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs). Feline placenta-derived MSCs from 7 healthy cats were cultured under control, serum-deprived, or cytokine-stimulated (tumor necrosis factor-α, interferon-γ, IL-1, IL-6) conditions in vitro. Viability/apoptosis were assessed by flow cytometry and mitochondrial morphology by confocal microscopy with MicroP/MATLAB; EVs were characterized by surface markers, RNA sequencing, and microRNA (miR) profiling. Viability exceeded 96% across all conditions, with no significant intergroup differences. Kiel 67 proliferation marker and metabolic activity were significantly reduced under serum-free and cytokine-stimulated conditions versus controls (both P < .001). Cytokine priming increased branching and simple tubular mitochondria, whereas serum deprivation increased fragmented forms. Extracellular vesicle transcriptomics identified 329 differentially expressed genes, including upregulated immunosuppressive receptors C-C motif chemokine receptor 8 and poliovirus receptor-related immunoglobulin domain-containing protein and downregulated proinflammatory histone transcripts. microRNA (miR) profiling revealed 23 differentially expressed miRs, with enrichment of anti-inflammatory miR-204, let-7g, and miR-181b-2 and depletion of proinflammatory miR-34a and miR-320a. Cytokine priming induces mitochondrial elongation and shifts EV cargo toward an immunosuppressive phenotype without compromising viability, supporting inflammatory priming as a strategy to optimize MSC-based therapies for T-cell-mediated inflammatory diseases. Inflammatory priming prior to MSC administration may enhance therapeutic efficacy in cats, supporting investigation of cytokine licensing as a translatable approach to improving MSC therapy outcomes in veterinary medicine.

papers.title: Clotting and Coagulation Disorders in Cats: A clinical review of causes, diagnosis and management.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Evans J, Li RHL
papers.abstract: Hemostatic disorders in cats, while uncommon, can be life-threatening. In general, they can be diagnosed by utilizing a combination of history, physical examination findings, point-of-care assays and a basic understanding of hemostasis. This review aims to provide a general overview of hemostasis physiology, discuss common hemostatic disorders, diagnosis and interpretation of hemostatic testing, and summarize treatments of hemostatic disorders. The underlying cause of hemostatic disorders can often be diagnosed by a combination of history, physical examination and directed testing. Based on the information obtained during the work-up, a management plan can be constructed tailored to the individual patient. This article aims to review the literature surrounding the pathophysiology, diagnosis and management of hemostatic disorders in cats. By the end of this article, readers should be able to: understand the basic physiology of hemostasis; understand common primary and secondary hemostatic disorders in cats and their pathophysiologies in relation to clinical signs and diagnostic findings; compare and contrast common diagnostic tests to assess hemostasis and apply those that are appropriate; and list the appropriate therapeutic and management strategies for common primary and secondary hemostatic disorders in cats.

papers.title: Nasal phaeohyphomycosis in a cat caused by Cladophialophora boppii.
papers.authors: McCarthy J, Augusto M, O'Neill E, Otero Balda I, Wyatt E
papers.abstract: Phaeohyphomycosis is an opportunistic mycosis caused by dematiaceous fungi, typically affecting the cutaneous or subcutaneous tissues of the facial region and distal extremities in cats. This report documents a case of Cladophialophora boppii infection in a cat. A 7-year-old neutered male domestic shorthair cat was presented with a chronic, pigmented nasal lesion, non-productive sneezing, and stertor. Computed tomography, rhinoscopy, and tissue sampling were performed. Fungal culture and molecular sequencing confirmed the diagnosis. Oral itraconazole treatment failed to arrest progression, necessitating delayed nasal planectomy. Despite transient remission, disease recurred, requiring repeat surgical debridement, and prolonged antifungal treatment. Clinical resolution was ultimately achieved, with marked improvement in the cat's quality of life. Identification of a novel species of phaeohyphomycosis in a cat emphasizes the need for increased awareness of emerging fungal pathogens that can precipitate considerable morbidity, particularly in the absence of prompt aggressive intervention.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Evaluation of Left Atrial Reservoir Strain by Two-Dimensional Speckle-Tracking Echocardiography in Cats with Stage B1 Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Algan D, Varlik T, Bach MBT, Gleerup CH, Yilmaz Z, Koch J
papers.abstract: Left atrial reservoir strain (LA S_R), assessed by two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography (2D-STE), reflects left atrial (LA) function and may reveal subtle alterations in LA mechanics in cats with American College of Veterinary Internal Medicine (ACVIM) stage B1 hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) compared with healthy cats. This study aimed to determine whether LA S_R differs between cats with HCM (stage B1) and healthy cats using 2D-STE. Sixty-one client-owned cats were retrospectively identified and included from medical databases. These cats were classified as healthy controls (Stage A; n=30) or preclinical HCM (Stage B1; n=31) according to ACVIM consensus guidelines. All cats underwent a comprehensive conventional echocardiographic examination, including two-dimensional, M-mode, color Doppler, pulsed-wave Doppler, and tissue Doppler imaging, as part of clinical care or screening protocols. Conventional two-dimensional assessment of LA size and function included the LA/Ao ratio, LA diameter, LA area, LA fractional shortening (LA FS), and LA ejection fraction (LA EF). LA S_R was subsequently measured offline using automated function imaging software. Reproducibility was assessed via intra- and inter-observer intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to compare the discriminatory performance of LA S_R and the evaluated LA variables between the predefined study groups. Cats with ACVIM stage B1 HCM had significantly lower LA S_R than healthy controls (19.0% [IQR, 14.5-22.0%] vs 38.0% [IQR, 30.25-42.50%], respectively; P < 0.001). LA S_R reproducibility was high with an intra-observer ICC of 0.974 and an inter-observer ICC of 0.894. Assessment of LA S_R was feasible in cats with stage B1 HCM. LA S_R values differed between affected cats and healthy controls, with lower values observed in the affected group and good reproducibility. These findings suggest that LA S_R may provide complementary information on LA function in cats with this stage of disease.

papers.title: Multifaceted effects of Salvia hispanica oil and Lactobacillus farciminis on quail physiology.
papers.authors: Durna Ö, Önk K, Yildiz G, Merhan O, Erbay Elibol FK, Cengiz MM, Kocamaz D
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the effects of Lactobacillus farciminis and Salvia hispanica oil, alone or in combination, on growth performance, antioxidant status, cecal short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) profiles, and bone biomechanical properties in Japanese quails. These natural antibiotic alternatives were selected because L. farciminis supports the intestinal barrier, while chia oil-rich in omega-3s and phenolic compounds-modulates antioxidant defense and mineral bioavailability. A total of 216 one-day-old Coturnix coturnix japonica chicks were randomly assigned to four groups: control, probiotic (Lactobacillus farciminis, 1 × 10⁹ CFU/kg), chia oil (Salvia hispanica oil, 0.2 g/kg), and combined treatment Birds were maintained under identical rearing conditions and fed a maize- and soybean-based basal diet with or without supplementation. The trial lasted 35 days; at the end of this period, blood samples were collected from the wing vein, and following slaughter, the hind leg bones (femur and tibia) were collected along with the carcass contents for laboratory analysis. No significant effects were observed on growth performance parameters (BW, BWG, FI, FCR) or bone biomechanical properties of femur and tibia (length, width, UL, YL, DUL, DYL, stiffness) (p > 0.05). Similarly, MDA, total SCFAs, major SCFA fractions (acetate, propionate, valerate, isovalerate), and serum biochemical parameters (ceruloplasmin, albumin, total protein, globulin) were not significantly affected (p > 0.05). Antioxidant status showed selective modulation, with Lactobacillus farciminis increasing GSH levels (p < 0.001), while superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase (CAT), and glutathione peroxidase (GPx) activities were influenced by chia oil and interaction effects. In SCFA profiles, specific fractions were differentially affected. Notably, a significant probiotic × chia oil interaction was observed for SOD activity and butyrate levels. The combined supplementation of Lactobacillus farciminis and Salvia hispanica oil influenced certain antioxidant and fermentation-related parameters, particularly SOD activity and butyrate concentration, although no corresponding improvements were observed in growth performance or bone characteristics.

papers.title: Comparison of an Anti-α v β 3 Integrin NIR Fluorescent Probe and Indocyanin Green for Precision Resection of Naturally Occurring Sarcomas in Dogs-A Randomized Blinded Case-Controlled Pilot Study.
papers.authors: Nolff MC, Grest P, Seehusen F, Beer P
papers.abstract: The infiltrative growth of sarcomas represents a challenge for complete resection, as tumour borders are not easily detectable. Fluorescence guided surgery (FGS) allows improved visualization of tumour margins and could improve resection accuracy. Unfortunately, studies validating the impact of FGS are rare, and direct comparisons of different dyes are not available. Dogs (n = 20) that were presented for sarcoma resection were prospectively enrolled and randomized to either receive indocyanine green (ICG, Group 1) or a targeted anti-α v β 3 integrin probe (Group 2) prior to surgery. FGS was performed in both groups with the surgeon blinded to treatment. The false positive and false negative rates as well as tumour-to-background ratio (TBR) were calculated for each dye. Correlation of fluorescent area and histologically confirmed tumour extension was determined using the Dice Coefficient (DC). The clinical impact of FGS was determined by assessing the rate of rightfully adapted resections. False positive signal was detected in 9/10 dogs in group 1 and 3/10 dogs in group 2. Mean TBR at skin level was higher in group 2 (4.5 and 5.3) compared to group 1, and this difference reached significance in formalin-fixed tissue (5.3 vs. 2.6, p = 0.016). Correlation of fluorescent signal and histologic tumour extent was strong for both dyes (DC group 1 = 0.64; group 2 = 0.78). Resection of additional neoplastic tissue based on FGS was more frequent in group 2 (3/10 dogs) compared to group 1 (1/10 dogs). The initial results of this study indicate that the targeted anti-α v β 3 integrin probe is more tumour selective than ICG in dogs. This pilot as well as the subsequent follow up study are registered at animalstudyregistry.org https://doi.org/10.17590/asr.0000321.

papers.title: Phenotypic characterization of presumptive propriospinal myoclonus in young dogs (2013-2025).
papers.authors: Polidoro D, Bhatti SFM, Santens P, Mandigers P, Santifort KM, Kanazono S, Lu D, Sánchez-Masián D, de Stefani A, Shafie INF, Álvarez P, Meyerhoff N, Jeroncic T, Lai SR, Dutil GF, Rohdin C, Marchand A, Thomovsky S, Liatis T
papers.abstract: Propriospinal myoclonus (PSM) is characterized by repetitive, brief jerks of the trunk, hips, and knees in humans and has not been reported in dogs. To describe phenotype, diagnostic findings, treatment, and outcomes in presumptive PSM in dogs. Twenty-seven dogs with presumptive PSM. Multicenter, retrospective study of dogs with myoclonus affecting the limbs and trunk without head involvement, identified through online calls for suspected cases. Median age at onset was 9 months (range, 2-44 months). Propriospinal myoclonus involved pelvic limbs in all dogs, thoracic limbs in 14/27 (52%), and trunk in 9/27 (33%). Pelvic limb myoclonus was extensor in all dogs, whereas thoracic limb involvement was extensor in 12/27 (44%) and flexor in 3/27 (11%) dogs. Episodes were observed in a non-weight-bearing posture in all dogs, mainly lateral (25/27; 93%) and sternal (12/27; 44%) recumbency. Neurological examination was normal in all dogs. Abnormalities were not detected on magnetic resonance imaging of the spinal cord (4/6) or brain (6/6) in 5/6 dogs; in the remaining dog, findings were unrelated to the presumptive PSM. Follow-up information was available for 26/27 (96%) dogs. Sixteen dogs (59%) received no treatment, of which 9/16 (56%) showed spontaneous reduction in PSM frequency. Treatment with various antiseizure medications was started in 11/27 (41%) dogs, of which 5/11 (45%) improved. Presumptive PSM affected young dogs and is likely idiopathic. The condition is characterized by extensor myoclonus predominantly affecting pelvic limbs during recumbency, with preserved mentation. Spontaneous improvement seems common. Achtergrond: Propriospinale myoclonus (PSM) wordt bij mens gekenmerkt door repetitieve, schokbewegingen van de romp, heupen en knieën. Tot op heden is deze aandoening niet beschreven bij honden.Doelstelling; Het beschrijven van het fenotype, diagnostische bevindingen, behandeling en klinische uitkomst.Dieren: Zevenentwintig honden met vermoedelijke PSM. Methoden-Multicentrische retrospectieve studie bij honden met myoclonus waarbij de ledematen waren betrokken, geïdentificeerd via online meldingen van vermoedelijke gevallen.Resultaten: De mediane leeftijd bij aanvang van de symptomen bedroeg 9 maanden (spreiding: 2-44 maanden). Bij alle honden was PSM aanwezig in de achterpoten, bij 14/27 (52%) in de voorpoten en bij 9/27 (33%) in de romp. De myoclonus van de achterpoten was bij alle honden in extensie. Ter hoogte van de voorpoten was de myoclonus in extensie (12/27 (44%) en in flexie (3/27 (11%). De episoden traden voornamelijk op in zijligging (25/27; 93%) en sternale (12/27; 44%). Neurologisch onderzoek was bij alle honden normaal. Magnetische resonantiebeeldvorming van ruggenmerg (4/6) en hersenen (6/6) was bij 5/6 honden normaal. Follow-upinformatie was beschikbaar voor 26/27 (96%) honden. Zestien honden (59%) kregen geen behandeling, waarvan 9/16 (56%) een spontane afname van de frequentie van de PSM vertoonden. Bij 11/27 (41%) honden werd een behandeling met aanvalswerende medicijnen gestart, waarbij 5/11 (45%) een verbetering vertoonden.Conclusies en klinische relevantie: Vermoedelijke PSM lijkt voornamelijk voor te komen bij jonge honden en is waarschijnlijk idiopathisch. Het klinisch beeld wordt gekenmerkt door een myoclonus in extensie van voornamelijk de achterpoten tijdens het liggen. Een spontane verbetering lijkt vaak voor te komen. The aim of this study was to investigate a pattern of repeated muscle jerks in dogs similar to propriospinal myoclonus seen in humans. The condition mainly affected young dogs, involved the hind limbs in all cases and the front limbs in some, and was most often seen when they were lying down. No underlying cause was identified. Although several medications were used, some dogs improved without treatment.

papers.title: Systemic oxidative stress, selected nonenzymatic exogenous and endogenous antioxidants, and hematologic and biochemical alterations in bitches with pyometra.
papers.authors: Peker C, Uçar EH, Ekren Aşıcı GS, Musal B
papers.abstract: To evaluate oxidative stress biomarkers (malondialdehyde [MDA] and total oxidant status [TOS]), selected nonenzymatic endogenous (glutathione [GSH], albumin, and bilirubin), and, for the first time, exogenous (ascorbic acid, α-tocopherol, β-carotene, and retinol) antioxidants together with hematobiochemical alterations in canine pyometra. 33 bitches were classified into pyometra (n = 17) or control (16) groups based on clinical and hematological evaluations. Ascorbic acid was measured by the phosphotungstate method; GSH, MDA, β-carotene, and retinol spectrophotometrically; α-tocopherol by ELISA; and TOS by a colorimetric assay. Hematobiochemical variables were analyzed using automated analyzers. Bitches with pyometra had higher MDA and TOS than controls (36.30 ± 13.95 µmol/L vs 24.61 ± 4.80 µmol/L and 27.78 ± 15.51 µmol H2O2 Eq/L vs 13.13 ± 1.84 µmol H2O2 Eq/L; Hedges' g = 1.08 and 1.27, respectively). Glutathione tended to increase in pyometra (12.04 ± 10.80 nmol/g Hb vs 6.40 ± 2.97 nmol/g Hb; Hedges' g = 0.68), whereas the other antioxidants were similar between groups. Pyometra was also associated with leukocytosis, neutrophilia, monocytosis, decreased erythrocyte counts and Hct, and increased ALP, ALT, and cholesterol. Canine pyometra is accompanied by systemic oxidative stress and hematobiochemical alterations. However, circulating nonenzymatic antioxidants remained largely unchanged, suggesting complex antioxidant regulation rather than simple depletion. Increased GSH may reflect a thiol-based compensatory response to increased oxidative burden. Nonenzymatic antioxidant regulation in canine pyometra may be more complex than simple depletion. Further studies incorporating disease-severity stratification and tissue-level assessments of both enzymatic and nonenzymatic antioxidants are warranted.

papers.title: Subcutaneous medetomidine at the governing vessel 20 acupuncture point provides faster early sedation than intramuscular administration without altering intraocular pressure in cats.
papers.authors: Gölgeli Bedir A, Yanmaz LE, Akçora Y, Özkalipçi Ç, Kartal T, Okur S
papers.abstract: To compare sedation, intraocular pressure (IOP), mean pupil diameter, and recovery profiles after IM or SC administration at the governing vessel 20 (GV20) acupuncture point of medetomidine in cats. This prospective, randomized, controlled clinical study was conducted at the Animal Hospital of Ataturk University in April and May of 2026. Cats undergoing elective castration received medetomidine (70 µg/kg) either IM or SC at GV20. Sedation score, IOP, and mean pupil diameter were recorded before and 5, 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes after injection. 16 cats completed the study, with 8 cats in each group. Governing vessel 20 produced higher sedation scores at 5 minutes (GV20, 10 [range, 8 to 11]; IM, 5 [range, 4 to 8]; r = 0.69; 95% CI, 0.23 to 0.97) and 10 minutes (GV20, 11 [range, 11 to 12]; IM, 8 [range, 8 to 11]; r = 0.66; 95% CI, 0.20 to 0.98), with comparable scores thereafter. Intraocular pressure did not differ significantly between groups or over time. The mean pupil diameter was larger in the GV20 group than in the IM group from 10 to 30 minutes, with the greatest difference 30 minutes after medetomidine administration (GV20, 9.35 ± 0.98 mm; IM, 6.94 ± 1.78 mm; mean difference, 2.41 mm). GV20 administration produced faster early sedation than IM medetomidine without clinically detectable IOP alteration or clinically relevant changes in mean pupil diameter, although early recovery should be monitored. GV20 administration may be useful when rapid early sedation is desired in healthy cats, but early recovery should be monitored.

papers.title: Service dogs in a matched survey were more physically active and had higher odds of being fed grain-free diets than companion dogs.
papers.authors: Otero DK, Wilson K, James TG
papers.abstract: There is a strong, bidirectional relation between the health outcomes of service dogs and their human handlers. Despite this relation, limited information is available on service dog health. This study assesses differences in health status, diet, and physical activity among service dogs and companion dogs. We conducted a cross-sectional study of the Dog Aging Project's Health and Life Experiences Survey, using data collected on or before December 31, 2021. Service dogs and companion dogs were matched on signalment. Descriptive statistics, conditional logistic regression, and Poisson regression were estimated to assess health differences. 240 canines were in each group. A higher prevalence of service dog owners reported annual household income of less than $39,999. Owners in both groups reported their dogs' health to be very good to excellent, and almost 50% of each group used daily joint supplements. Service dogs had a higher adjusted OR of ever being on a grain-free diet (1.98; 95% CI, 1.18 to 3.33), 15% more total minutes of daily physical activity, and longer leashed physical activity compared to companion dogs. Service dogs in this matched cohort had higher activity levels, greater odds of grain-free diet exposure, yet similar prevalence of joint supplementation to companion dogs. Further studies are needed to elucidate functional impacts on both handlers and service dogs and to limit inherent selection bias. This study adds to the relatively limited evidence base regarding service dog health outcomes. The distinct lifestyle patterns of service dogs may warrant tailored veterinary monitoring and client communication, particularly for nutritional and musculoskeletal health.

papers.title: Epidural analgesia reduces or eliminates neuropathic pain refractory to oral medications in dogs and cats for weeks to months.
papers.authors: Bergstein O, Boesch JM, Thomson ACS, Todd-Donato A
papers.abstract: To describe epidural injection for neuropathic pain in dogs and cats and report outcome. Medical records of patients presented to an academic pain medicine service from 2015 through 2026 with clinical signs of neuropathic pain and a somatosensory nervous system lesion or disease that underwent epidural injection after failing treatment with at least 2 oral analgesics were reviewed; incomplete records were excluded. Six animals met these criteria. 4 domestic shorthair cats and 2 dogs (Dalmatian and mixed-breed) presented with neuropathic pain beginning after amputation (2 cats), blunt force trauma (1 cat, 1 dog), hemilaminectomy (1 dog), or parturition (1 cat). Abnormalities included paroxysmal, spontaneous self-mutilation, body-focused repetitive behavior, panic, and/or vocalization; signs of allodynia; teeth chattering; tail and skin twitching; abnormal posture or gait; and/or inability to perform normal activities. MRI was not performed in feline amputees but showed intervertebral disk disease in 2 cats and the Dalmatian and sciatic nerve neoplasia in the mixed breed. At least 1 epidural injection containing triamcinolone (0.1 to 0.5 mg/kg) and 0.125% to 0.250% bupivacaine or ropivacaine (with or without other analgesics) was performed. In 1 feline amputee, 1 injection was curative. In the other cats, injection mitigated or eliminated pain for a median of 6 months (range, 0.25 to 8); in 2 cats, repeat injections lasted 5 and 2.5 months. In the Dalmatian and mixed breed, initial and repeat injections lasted 6 and 3 weeks and 4 and 2 weeks, respectively. Epidural analgesia may relieve neuropathic pain when oral analgesics fail.

papers.title: Canine gastric polyps are predominantly hyperplastic, and endoscopic polypectomy is a safe and effective treatment associated with no recurrence during follow-up.
papers.authors: Zanardi S, Cola V, Del Magno S, Sabattini S, Dondi G, Romagnoli N, Foglia A, Pisoni L, Pietra M
papers.abstract: To characterize the clinical presentation, endoscopic features, and histopathological findings of gastric polyps in dogs and to evaluate the safety and outcomes of endoscopic polypectomy. Dogs diagnosed with gastric polypoid lesions during upper gastrointestinal endoscopy from January 2020 through December 2024 at the University Veterinary Hospital, University of Bologna (Italy), were retrospectively evaluated. Inclusion criteria were endoscopic identification of gastric polyps; dogs with primary gastric neoplasia were excluded. Signalment, clinical signs, history of proton pump inhibitor administration, endoscopic findings, histopathology, treatment, complications, and follow-up data were collected. Endoscopic polypectomy was performed using cold biopsy forceps or electrosurgical snare. Over a 5-year period, 57 dogs were included from 574 canine gastroscopies performed, yielding a detection rate of 9.9% (57 of 574). Polyps were solitary in 54.4% and multiple in 45.6% of cases, mainly located in the gastric antrum (77.2%). All polyps were hyperplastic on histopathology. Endoscopic polypectomy was performed in 17 of 57 dogs, with no intraoperative complications. Mild postoperative complications occurred in 5 of 17 dogs. Clinical signs resolved in all but 1 case and remained absent during follow-up (median, 16 months). Polyps removed with electrosurgical snare were significantly larger than those removed with cold biopsy forceps, with an exploratory cutoff of 10 mm distinguishing between the 2 techniques. No recurrences were documented based on clinical follow-up. Gastric polyps in dogs are uncommon lesions, typically hyperplastic and associated with chronic inflammation. Endoscopic polypectomy appears to be a safe and effective treatment and recurrence-free at follow-up. Endoscopic polypectomy represents a minimally invasive option for the management of gastric polyps in dogs, allowing clinical resolution with low morbidity in selected cases.

papers.title: The fibula contributes minimally to torsional stiffness and strength of the canine crus in an ex vivo study in Beagles.
papers.authors: Picavet PP, Balligand M
papers.abstract: To characterize the torsional mechanical properties of the canine crus, determine the contribution of the fibula to crus stiffness and strength under torsional loading, and describe the associated failure pattern. This ex vivo study was conducted from December 2021 through June 2022 and included 13 pelvic limbs from skeletally mature Beagles. Specimens were assigned to 2 groups: intact tibia and fibula (n = 7) and tibia with proximal fibular ostectomy (6). Crura were potted proximally and distally. Torsional loading was applied under quasi-static conditions until failure. Torque and twist angle at failure, torsional stiffness, and rotation relative to working length were recorded. All specimens sustained mid-diaphyseal oblique/spiral tibial fractures. Mean torque to failure was 17.33 ± 2.95 Nm in intact crura, 18.45 ± 3.36 Nm following fibular ostectomy, and 1.13 ± 0.6 Nm for isolated fibula. No significant differences were detected between groups for any measured variable. Following tibial fracture, the isolated fibula exhibited minimal torsional stiffness and sustained 6.5% of the torque at failure of the intact crus. The fibula contributes minimally to the torsional stiffness and strength of the canine crus under torsional loading. The torsional mechanical properties of the canine crus were primarily determined by the tibia, and failure was consistently characterized by tibial fracture preceding fibular failure. Fibular integrity appears to have limited influence on torsional stability in canine tibial fractures, although it may remain important for maintaining limb alignment and fracture management.

papers.title: Clinical findings and outcomes in canine ischemic neuromyopathy: neurologic status is associated with survival, and recovery is possible.
papers.authors: Atkins C, Maeso Ordás C, Phillips K, Krekis A, Freeman P, Gonçalves R, Faller K
papers.abstract: To describe the clinical findings and outcomes in dogs diagnosed with thoracic or pelvic limb ischemic neuromyopathy (INM) in a referral practice. This was a retrospective, multicenter study of client-owned dogs diagnosed with thoracic or pelvic limb INM at 5 referral hospitals (July 2013 to June 2023). Medical records were reviewed for clinical findings, comorbidities, treatments, and outcomes. The primary outcome was survival to discharge. Long-term outcomes were summarized when follow-up was available. 42 dogs met the inclusion criteria: 4 of 42 (9.5%) had thoracic limb INM, and 38 of 42 (90.5%) had pelvic limb INM. Comorbidities were documented in 35 of 42 (83.3%), most commonly protein-losing nephropathy (21 of 42 [50.0%]). All thoracic limb cases were ambulatory at presentation but were euthanized shortly after diagnosis at the owner's discretion. Among pelvic limb cases, 22 of 38 (57.9%) were ambulatory at presentation, 27 of 38 (71.1%) retained nociception, and 15 of 38 (39.5%) had onset of clinical signs > 24 hours. Nineteen of 38 (50.0%) survived to discharge. Among dogs with long-term outcome available, 7 of 28 (25.0%) fully recovered, including 2 of 16 (12.5%) initially nonambulatory dogs. In dogs with pelvic limb INM, ambulatory status, presence of nociception, and more gradual progression to maximal clinical severity were associated with survival to discharge. Complete recovery occurred in a subset of initially nonambulatory dogs, indicating that recovery is possible despite more severe neurologic deficits at presentation. Prognostic indicators such as ambulatory status and nociception should be used to inform clinical decision-making but should not be used in isolation when considering prognosis, as recovery may occur even in more severely affected dogs.

papers.title: Brachyspira hyodysenteriae detected in a dog with acute haemorrhagic diarrhoea: a case report.
papers.authors: Jeong H, Ahn H, Cheon DS, Oh Y, Yoon WK
papers.abstract: Brachyspira hyodysenteriae is a well-known pathogen of swine dysentery, a severe mucohaemorrhagic colitis in pigs. While several Brachyspira species are reported in dogs, natural Brachyspira hyodysenteriae detection in dogs is extremely rare. This case report aims to provide insight into the pathogenic potential and clinical significance of Brachyspira hyodysenteriae in dogs. A 5-year-old male mongrel dog was presented with acute haemorrhagic diarrhoea shortly after being adopted from a shelter, where he had a history of soft stools. The faeces were watery, containing fresh blood and fibrinous mucus. Initial wet mount and faecal flotation tests were negative for parasites or ova, but faecal smear cytology revealed diverse bacterial morphologies, including chevron- and spiral-shaped forms. Real-time PCR identified Brachyspira hyodysenteriae with a low Ct value (27.19), alongside Campylobacter coli, Campylobacter jejuni, canine astrovirus and Cystoisospora. The dog was treated with enrofloxacin, metronidazole, and fenbendazole, leading to complete resolution of haematochezia and gradual normalization of stool consistency. Follow-up real-time PCR confirmed the absence of all previously detected pathogens, and the patient remained asymptomatic. This case suggests that Brachyspira hyodysenteriae, traditionally regarded as a swine-specific pathogen, may contribute to gastrointestinal disease in dogs. However, because confirmatory bacterial culture was not performed and multiple enteropathogens were detected concurrently, a definitive association between Brachyspira hyodysenteriae and the observed haemorrhagic diarrhoea cannot be established. Nevertheless, it highlights the importance of considering Brachyspira hyodysenteriae in unexplained cases of infectious diarrhoea in dogs, particularly regarding mixed infections. These findings also raise concerns regarding potential interspecies transmission and associated biosecurity risks. Further research is warranted to enhance understanding of diagnostic strategies, treatment approaches and antibiotic resistance patterns.

papers.title: Comparative Phenotypic and Molecular Characterisation of Feline Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma Cell Lines Reveals Marked Biological Heterogeneity.
papers.authors: Tanveer Q, Pang LY, Farquharson C, Bergkvist GT
papers.abstract: Feline oral squamous cell carcinoma (FOSCC) is the most common oral malignancy, characterised by aggressive local invasion, frequent bone involvement, and poor prognosis. The limited availability of well-characterised in vitro models has hindered the understanding of tumour heterogeneity and invasive behaviour. This study aimed to establish and comparatively characterise a panel of FOSCC cell lines derived from tumours with and without documented bone invasion to identify intrinsic biological differences. Four FOSCC cell lines were evaluated for epithelial identity, growth kinetics, clonogenicity, migratory capacity and chemosensitivity.
